body.title: Physical punishment is not the only way to discipline a child.
body.body:
It’s is no longer a news that majority of the parents don’t punish there kids when the do anything wrong come time last week i was having a discussion with my mom about the way kids of this days are behavior of the are better back in the days where parents punish there kids according to my mom that kids back then are more disciplined and more respectful because the are always of receiving treatment from parents if the misbehave i was telling my mom that parents of this think that when you punish this kids you are scaring them away now here comes the big problem is the society weaker without corporal punishment, or are we simply trying to raise children in healthier ways?







We are in a generation that has changed parenting decades ago; in many homes, disciplining kids and spanking are seen as the normal ways of correction. I remember back then, my mom would always discipline me. When I did anything wrong, she would punish me. She so much believed in 'spare the rod and spoil the child'. If I must be sincere, this experience didn’t destroy me; rather, it built me to the woman I am today. One thing about parenting is that you don’t need to be too soft. When I see kids that are disrespectful, lack accountability and have poor behaviour, I always tell myself that the parent is too soft with the kids.



![IMG_1050.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cindynancy/241tjjcJo8rCpGGBKrUgmyevVuV1unJBPPAZ9639ExrRbvb61tr6hDUtEZUj3g1kzbtbK.png)


[source](https://pixabay.com/vectors/parenting-discipline-silhouette-9528352/)

In the modern day, most parents look so frustrated because they fail to train their kids. That is why many kids appear difficult to be corrected. It is so painful that parents don’t set boundaries because they don’t want to be tagged as toxic parents or harsh parents. Most parents have replaced discipline with excuses and negotiation. That is why most kids today fail to understand why it is important for them to take responsibility for their actions; instead, they push blame to people.





Physical punishment is not the only way to discipline a child. I can remember back then when I was still a child; it was not all the time my mom flogged me. Sometimes I would be the one to do all the house chores in the house while my siblings relaxed without doing anything. After the punishment, she would sit me down and give me advice; with that, I would correct myself. I always tell parents that fear will only bring a temporary obedient child; a child can stop a behaviour because he doesn't want to be punished, not that the understand but he is doing that. Thathe understands, is why it is important to correct these kids with love and care.




![IMG_1051.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cindynancy/23vhq34LQumhs6bSceFnhkgNRUhuPnPehTjg6LCdE1JUX98QGoF1YfP3eakwapa28Tro2.png)




[source](https://pixabay.com/illustrations/ai-generated-mom-daughter-fun-8951031/)



It is not as if the parents are not trying. The fact is that these kids are in a generation that can easily be influenced by what they see on social media or influenced by peer pressure, which is changing family patterns. The way parenting worked years ago is not the same. Correctly, some parents are trying to break protocol just to get it right because kids of these days are to be followed with love and care if you want to get it. In as much as you are correcting these kids, it is important we create boundaries; we should not avoid any form of discipline, or it can be dangerous.








A child should learn why there are consequences for every action, either physical punishment or corporal punishment; what matters is correcting the kids with love.



Thank you for stopping by on my blog. I appreciate your comments, support and upvotes. Do have a lovely day.

Posted Using [INLEO](https://inleo.io/@cindynancy/physical-punishment-is-not-the-only-way-to-discipline-a-child--8g7)

Yes, I know that summer hasn't started yet, neither the astronomical nor the meteorological summer, but the beautiful weather we have had these days with pleasantly warm temperatures was enough for me to open our *beach and swimming season* today. 🌊

<center>![1000076334.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mipiano/Ep3fpJT9tMbJotAVnoA24FcxRddqGW3SELAKtJ45xv7CiSMSt6gjt5x4zTNMzShA1GA.jpg)</center>


As you can see, my beach shoes are still serving my feet well. I searched for them this morning when we decided to kill two birds with one stone today, that is, to use our travel and go to the beach before a meeting with a manager and my private afternoon classes. In a backpack that had been sleeping through the winter on a high shelf in the pantry, these beach shoes were waiting for me, and as a surprise, I found an entire bottle of sunscreen in the same backpack. 



<center>![1000076335.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mipiano/EpVBAzRJPMUX15VqEqwUw2LgvXWVCMcLeW7GkV3kH7cQKpP99xj86PfEVCFuYm8VK3k.jpg)</center>


Another reason I could allow myself this pleasure of spending a few hours at the beach is that I will have some more free time in the next three days. It already feels relaxing; the idea itself made me take things easy, instead of sticking to strict schedules. 




<center>![1000076337.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mipiano/23zbMpHcdirvr9zZb5n1gigyWgvqVA8DHyJPkNBG6WnGsgmtf71sAP528UHce9sMCagqq.jpg)</center>

I am even thinking of going to the seashore tomorrow as well. Even though I don't have to go to my regular work tomorrow and on Friday, I do have things to sort out (both as household chores and around the musical project I am working on intensely), but now I feel I can give myself that little break. 

<center>![1000076344.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mipiano/EpnDM27s8tH8zZSwAT9kugLtpkUwrgHWTp2iZN9GAkwGVsF3UXjrpPm2eA7PeuzXbwq.jpg)</center>




During the Hive meetup we had about a month ago in the city of Alicante, I was already quite busy, and later, things intensified even more. The interesting thing is that once you get used to the crazy schedules and events, you also get ~~a bit~~ addicted to that pace, so at one point I asked myself what I would do during the summer when I have my summer break? Will I be bored? Lost?




<center>![1000076339.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mipiano/23tHE6f3SNLzWx6G4NAib2UiF8FaLhnh9gZ4ERJvwh9VwBwToqN4HCRnSHGaCds3TQnyx.jpg)</center>


One of the fellow Hivers said that then (during summer), I will have time for kindness rocks and for Hive posts. 

👀


...someone mentioned [Kindness Rocks](https://peakd.com/c/hive-102177/created)?

<center>![1000076346.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mipiano/EpCAvvNsykJEBc7dt71d2msNNK9vEkcAi8rqsLt4wURbreuU9Y3XZV5wCA9nM4EY4TB.jpg)</center>

At first, I spotted just those two pebbles on one rock. But then - surprise!!! 😍 Many pebbles appeared in front of my eyes. It wasn't me who played this balance game with pebbles, but yeah, it could perfectly represent our days, our thoughts, or efforts. 

<center>![1000076347.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mipiano/EoK7fw56hDQPJmjpWb9SfeKMSaWnm8NZUvzufeA7ctKNjJYcvuWwL9scBp5ZfULRbcj.jpg)</center>



<center>![1000076348.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mipiano/23vsV3hmPWrpkTP5LvbuSUcfiUxEsu5zGFAvPpXmpwV1Bf3DKtg9jSaZdNtZdpGo2iUzu.jpg)</center>

Stacking rocks and finding that balancing point where they would hold each other is kind of an art. Or just a matter of patience. Experience, maybe. Or luck? Whatever. Find what works for you and even if sometimes heavy storms open the covered and well-padded wounds and ruin the stack, just start again building a tower with your own balance points when you feel your hand is steady and calm again.

<center>![1000076361.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mipiano/EpNmtJT1yPMagncmV8CNYMwVcCh8udRj1XrYGbs75y76uByysn5kqPif6fpzBtLd9BZ.jpg)</center>




After adding my contribution with a few new pebble towers, I went to swim. The water was so clean and pleasant, and not cold (for my taste) at all. 


<center>![1000076363.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mipiano/23xyTCcoPRDH6EJ3TcYwLiRd4uoKieuUMcgdE96YrSQPyqJ6tEiLcHQ3WxqcxTpsPxTCM.jpg)</center>


Here we were leaving already as the afternoon had to continue with the useful stuff (<sub>oh, but who says spending some hours at a beach is not useful as well? 😂</sub>). And also... now that the summer vibes season is open at my side, I am looking forward to having more of these little breaks by the sea. 🌊

body.title: Tie Box: Creating a template in CANVA [ESP/ENG]
body.body:
> Crear algo desde nunca será fácil, requiere tiempo, practica y dedicación, así lo veas fácil, cuando te pones hacerlo tu mismo, te das cuenta, que no esta sencillo como lo muestran, sin embargo, cuando logras hacerlo, la satisfacción es grande. Desde hace unos días tenia esta idea en la cabeza, recuerdo haber hecho esta caja de forma manual, con cartulina, también fue un proceso, pero por supuesto, me quedo muy bien, ahora quise crear la plantilla en CANVA, como bien sabemos esto esta de moda, muchos usan este programa para crear los moldes de sus cajas, hacer el diseño e imprimir.
![post hive (84).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/23xf1AYnSNNAoDjYDrazj2QckPwkFPEHrB9pjQ9Vp2XpQrjsEmMt8T4365Zp1NnMc1wPs.png)
Y como ya se acerca el día de los padres, esta es la mejor ocasión, para aprender hacer estas Cajas Corbata, y promocionar dichas plantillas. Me tomo algo tiempo, por supuesto, dar con un molde fácil de armar y que no requiera de tantas hojas al momento de imprimir, aun así, esto dependerá del tamaño de la caja, esa es la ventaja de diseñar estas plantillas editables en canva.
![post hive (86).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/23w3CeANHasUStdqBcZhUvj5FEp9keVXB4Y6rvWCu8Ef24q3Uc5G6nL3YPJfBF4zyFw4F.png)
Al tener mi molde listo, tenia que por supuesto armarlo, y probar como quedo, como bien saben no tengo impresora, así que me toco realizarlo de forma manual, con papel en mano y tijeras, vamos a cortar y armar. **Materiales usado:** - Papel hoja grande - Tijera - Regla - Lápiz grafito - Pega barra **Como lo hacemos:** Bueno lo primero que hice fue dibujar o calcar mi molde, tal cual como diseñe en CANVA, una vez hecho procedo a cortar, por los lados. Como ven, hay unas partes que no recorto del todo, estas serán las pestañas para pegarla con los laterales.
![post hive (82).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/23uQxp3abnumwZn9uue2Urp1UufBM4oWn8Yc91mYyJntirq6941iqCZL72jhUmx8ynv2D.png)
Cabe señalar que dicho molde, lo armaremos dos veces, para así poder armar nuestra caja.
![post hive (83).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/23t7mRTYGMkUg6V9oL1G8Q9Zwk7vke4Lk49WgjzxaLEJECmjrbpH9f74MaS5wEtzNe3vb.png)
Como ven aquí abajo, fue lo que hice, en mi caso, la altura de mi caja, fue de 1cm, por lo tanto quedo delgada, esto ya se podría ajustar mejor, al momento de imprimirla.
![post hive (85).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/23t7hNgKtLrpn4WKyumdv4yFgYDvuBdoBYdFsrj1ZnXbyeaqsvTD2YX4BEpSoPiANSUnW.png)
Espero poder crear por completo el diseño, para así luego imprimirlo, y mostrar de mejor manera, como quedaría esta cajita, pero creo que ya di el primer paso, tan perdida no estoy jeje. Que les pareció, se atreven a crear su propia plantilla, es cuestión de ensayo y error, sin duda, vale la pena intentarlo. ---
ENGLISH VERSION

Creating something from scratch is never easy; it takes time, practice, and dedication. No matter how simple it may seem, when you try to do it yourself, you realize it’s not as easy as it looks. However, when you finally succeed, the sense of accomplishment is immense. I’ve had this idea in my head for a few days now. I remember making this box by hand out of cardstock—it was a process, but of course, it turned out great. Now I wanted to create the template in CANVA. As we all know, this is all the rage; many people use this program to create their box templates, design them, and print them. And since Father’s Day is just around the corner, this is the perfect time to learn how to make these tie boxes and promote these templates. It took me some time, of course, to find a template that’s easy to assemble and doesn’t require so many sheets when printing, though this will depend on the size of the box—that’s the advantage of designing these editable templates in Canva.

![post hive (86).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/23w3CeANHasUStdqBcZhUvj5FEp9keVXB4Y6rvWCu8Ef24q3Uc5G6nL3YPJfBF4zyFw4F.png)
Once my template was ready, I had to put it together, of course, and see how it turned out. As you know, I don’t have a printer, so I had to do it by hand, with paper and scissors—let’s cut and assemble. **Materials used:** - Large sheet of paper - Scissors - Ruler - Graphite pencil - Glue stick **How to do it:** Well, the first thing I did was draw or trace my template, exactly as I designed it in CANVA. Once that was done, I proceeded to cut along the sides. As you can see, there are some parts I don’t cut all the way through; these will be the tabs to attach to the sides.
![post hive (82).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/23uQxp3abnumwZn9uue2Urp1UufBM4oWn8Yc91mYyJntirq6941iqCZL72jhUmx8ynv2D.png)
Note that we will assemble this template twice in order to build our box.
![post hive (83).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/23t7mRTYGMkUg6V9oL1G8Q9Zwk7vke4Lk49WgjzxaLEJECmjrbpH9f74MaS5wEtzNe3vb.png)
As you can see below, this is what I did. In my case, the height of my box was 1 cm, so it turned out thin; this could be adjusted better when printing it.
![post hive (85).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/23t7hNgKtLrpn4WKyumdv4yFgYDvuBdoBYdFsrj1ZnXbyeaqsvTD2YX4BEpSoPiANSUnW.png)
I hope to be able to fully create the design so I can print it out and better show what this little box would look like, but I think I’ve already taken the first step—I’m not that lost, haha. What do you think? Do you dare to create your own template? It’s a matter of trial and error, but it’s definitely worth a try.

body.title: School life
body.body:
- 
![72246274-0C4E-464D-ACA8-CED249E9B166.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dwayne16/23wMckno7uKjnAfk38LHvRiJd9hbKFx3MgVGatQ5zjuMfrNAt4Fe71n6ZN4WRf93GhrmT.jpeg)

***
This morning I got a text from one of my course mates that we have a five o’clock class. On a normal day, I would complain and start saying things aren’t easy for students, but this time around I just said okay, I would be there thirty minutes after the class starts.

There’s a certain level of frustration that leaves you speechless cuz yesterday I slept late and I got home drenched and now I had to prepare for class again and I already had plans to go grocery shopping and do laundry cuz who on earth declares impromptu class. “ahhhhh o ti su mi” I am tired but sacrifices must be made in order to achieve goals cuz you can’t get anything if you don’t work for it and in order to be successful you have to study cuz even the rich who is not properly educated will end up poor.

My father says knowledge is power not because he’s wiser than I am but because the weight of knowledge beats the futile things we think matters most, sometimes I feel a strong sense of diversion in my work but diversion drives us to the main point.

succuss derives from a thought, to a choice and most importantly, an initiative paired with discipline and ambition. hard work surely beats talent. And as generic at this cliche gets, its what reveals either a well-deserved breakthrough or an unfortunate shortcoming.

Our growing generation has found so much comfort in degeneration and forever residing in their comfort sphere. Opportunities aren't lucky handouts that appear at the right time and place, there laid out by the divine once God sees you deserve it. Having a mindset of optimism and ambition that leads into action instead of contentment brings more wonders then being in a constant state of quick dopamine rushes and short-term satisfaction.

Having such a uniquely purpose-driven state of mind is spiritual ammunition that fights against pessimism and negative energy. Greatness isn't given, its deserved.

We are humans we walk, we talk, we rest and everything has its time and must be done accordingly.

body.title: Mi pequeña colección de abrebotellas/My Small Collection of Bottle Openers (Esp-Eng)
body.body:
> Hola, mis amigos. Que placer saludarlos. Coleccionar abrebotellas es un hobby que, para mí, transforma lo sencillo en extraordinario. Cada pieza cuenta una historia, ya sea antiguo o modermo. La emoción está en la caza, buscando en mercados, viajes o regalos de amigos. Un abrebotellas no solo abre cervezas, abre recuerdos, conversaciones y sonrisas. Tener cientos de ellos sería maravilloso, además, es poseer un arsenal de experiencias compartidas. Para el coleccionista, no es un simple útil, sino un tesoro que celebra la amistad, los viajes y esos pequeños placeres que merecen ser brindados con paciencia y alegría. >Hello, my friends. What a pleasure to greet you. > >Collecting bottle openers is a hobby that, for me, turns the ordinary into something extraordinary. Each piece tells a story, whether it’s old or modern. The thrill is in the hunt—searching through markets, during travels, or through gifts from friends. A bottle opener doesn’t just open beers; it opens memories, conversations, and smiles. Having hundreds of them would be wonderful—more than that, it would be owning an arsenal of shared experiences. For the collector, it’s not just a simple tool, but a treasure that celebrates friendship, travel, and those small pleasures that deserve to be toasted to with patience and joy.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmfY3zfz2Z261LmzDHxbhPB3NbFZtZgq81j26UBvvJqh5C/1779917940248.jpg)

> La gente se queda mirando para mi pequeña colección y no lo entienden. “¿Para qué quieres tú tantos abrebotellas si con uno basta?”, me sueltan. Y yo, les respondo con una sonrisa: Eso es como decir que con un solo zapato tienes suficiente para caminar”. Para mí, esto es cosa seria, tiene un valor aunque para ellos sea solo un pedazo de metal. Todo empezó por casualidad. Un día, hace como cinco años, estaba yo en casa de una amiga, celebrando un cumpleaños. La madre, que es más despistada que gallina en vitrina, no encontraba el abridor. Y el que tenía parecía una pinza vieja, todo oxidado. Me dio tanta lata que al otro día fui a la ferretería y me compré uno nuevecito, de esos con el plástico de colores. >People stare at my small collection and don’t understand. “Why do you need so many bottle openers when one is enough?” they blurt out. And I, smiling, reply: “That’s like saying one shoe is enough to walk in.” For me, this is serious business—it has value, even if to them it’s just a piece of metal. It all started by chance. One day, about five years ago, I was at a friend’s house celebrating a birthday. Her mother, who is more scatterbrained than a chicken in a shop window, couldn’t find the opener. And the one she had looked like an old pair of pliers, all rusty. It annoyed me so much that the next day I went to the hardware store and bought myself a brand-new one, one of those with colorful plastic handles.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcK4GDs6uB2kYPsnV1CfPwAXHsxg4SCXu6JsUBqnKpGYB/1779918108448.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmeiKiBapLC6W5e5wSgtzCUwRLeHuic2NUC12LxV2ydpbe/1779918108636.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRzXhFqrSwsJ2YNtGhw6ZXMWXcpbhhx1Y2uPiQb8KXqY9/1779918108796.jpg)

> A los meses, mi tio vino de Miami y me trajo dos de recuerdo con un color dorado precioso. Ahí fue que me picó el bichito. Empecé a pedirle a todo el mundo que si viajaban, que me trajeran uno. No importa de dónde: de Varadero, de la playa, de una discoteca… El más raro que tengo es uno que parece un sacacorchos de la era mesosóica. Ese me lo regaló un pintor loco que vivía en el Vedado. >A few months later, my uncle came from Miami and brought me two souvenir openers with a beautiful golden color. That’s when the bug bit me. I started asking everyone—if they traveled, bring me one. It didn’t matter where from: Varadero, the beach, a nightclub… The strangest one I have looks like a corkscrew from the Mesozoic era. That one was given to me by a crazy painter who lived in Vedado.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmaWRZJ5fVYSTXm2ddnxW95PGR3NJLLhgM2m47QKRGrqae/1779918108985.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmV3LCSN1AP9fF6TLsivQjFQvyGRF3cWoJW9howH1XwQUU/1779918109203.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmU2tML7NFAm7Xj6poKibVrvZ7R2pr8sqggpuSruwKhAaX/1779918190379.jpg)

> Lo mío no es una colección grande sino más bien modesta pero aspiro a que siga creciendo. Tengo apenas ocho, pero cada uno tiene su historia. Está el rojo y negro, que me lo gané en una rifa del colmado. Está el que tiene un cabo rosado, que era de mi abuelo, que en paz descanse. Ese no se lo presto ni al más pintado. Luego estan los más sencillos en forma de llavero que me los gané como parte de regalilllos en concursos literarios. Todos son útiles y prácticos. Cuelgan teanwuilos y felices en la pared de mi cocina, esperando su momento para abrir una Cristal o una Bucanero bien fría. >My collection isn’t big—rather modest—but I hope it keeps growing. I only have eight, but each has its own story. There’s the red-and-black one I won in a raffle at the corner store. There’s the one with the pink handle that belonged to my late grandfather. That one I wouldn’t lend to anyone, no matter who. Then there are the simpler keychain ones I got as little prizes in literary contests. They’re all useful and practical. They hang calmly and happily on my kitchen wall, waiting for their moment to open a nice cold Cristal or Bucanero.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPNFmH1hTBd59oTkHDHAkBi7PptEdrfvwxrnX4yuzgFhf/1779918216216.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmb3npBjE1RLJy7DJ9mkxZWvTCDtJJp4v2mDfgSK5EMX41/1779918255127.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdtqyu4sU1gWp8DVDiEx8uUZBZXDBWcecDtWXKamZLGtB/1779918255284.jpg)

> Mis amigas se ríen de mí. Dicen que parezco una ferretera. Pero a ellas les encanta venir a casa, porque saben que aquí nunca vas a pasar trabajo para destapar una Malta o una lata de refresco. Para mí, cada abrebotellas es un recuerdo en la mano. Es la gente que quiero, los viajes que no he podido hacer, los momentos de fiesta y celebración. Cuando abro una botella con los que me regaló mi tío, siento que él está aquí sentado conmigo. Así que sí vienes a mi casa, trae cerveza y si traes un abridor nuevo, mejor. Que este vicio, como el café, no se quita con nada. >My friends laugh at me. They say I look like a hardware store. But they love coming over to my house, because they know you’ll never struggle to open a Malta or a soda can here. For me, each bottle opener is a memory I can hold. It’s the people I love, the trips I haven’t been able to take, the moments of partying and celebration. When I open a bottle with the ones my uncle gave me, I feel like he’s sitting right here with me. So if you come to my house, bring beer—and if you bring a new opener, even better. Because this habit, like coffee, is here to stay.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRkXQFcZ2sZ1LqazpUFCYZPgDNHzmk1Jyq5ZtPSboThYQ/1779918354536.jpg) https://images.ecency.com/DQmUJDibgVv7QpnG7cFRyL8RrNKwrY4Tkx4636U9mec4jSH/img_8206.gif Gracias por visitar mi blog Texto e imágenes de mi propiedad Thanks to visite my blog Text and imagen are my own https://images.ecency.com/DQmdmftReAUFLd1o6yeBP8wg9ths82CW6Fpu7doGEYgCEWV/img_7269.jpg

body.title: Staying Smart, Being Aware And Limiting Important Information
body.body: /> [source](https://pixabay.com/vectors/phishing-fraud-hacking-online-fraud-6926470/) We are in the era of the 21st century where many things has changed and lifestyle has become so fast paced. And the internet which is created to make life easier for the world 🌍, has become a source for all kinds of frauds. The internet has helped the world 🌎, making online payment so easy, communication with family swiftly, connecting with the world one of the most valuable thing as we can reach out to friends any where around the world, and other advantages we are enjoying. But the internet has also created avenues for fraudsters who has continued to scant for peoples information for the purpose of thefts of all kinds. Self Aware: =========== To protect myself from scammers, I have made sure to know the system this fraudulent people use. Being self aware should be the first thing to protect ourselves. Scammers and fraudsters are two online alert 🚨 we should at this stage of our lives be aware of without anyone telling us about them. I mean, with the awareness we have gathered and stories we have heard from other people, we should be at alert at all times, looking out for those signs that we already know. Because the internet is a place where we interact with people, either on social media or through websites for businesses or course studies. So, practically, we can not avoid the internet because of scammers, but we need to be self aware that they are out their preying on people they will scam. Watch Out For Unknown Links: ============================ This is another major way to properly protect myself from scammers. Many times I have received some unknowns links in my WhatsApp asking me to click here for this or that. First thing I do when I see messages like this is to check out the sender. And once is someone I don’t know, I will ignore it and delete it after sometime. Some few months ago I received a message from one of my WhatsApp contacts and this profile is someone close to me. The message was asking me to send some money 💰 to him because he was under emergency. But the tone of the message is not of the person I know who is a cousin of mine. I immediately knew something was up. I decided to ignore the message to see if my cousin will call me. But he never did. After two days I decided to call him on his mobile number and not WhatsApp. He immediately told me they hacked his WhatsApp. This is very important, that we look out for signs that we use in knowing people. What they can do, the way they relate with you and tone of the messages. Limit Personal Information Online: ================================== Yes! This is another way I can use in limiting scammers. Too much of our information online can create openings for scammers. Here, we should know what to post and what not to post. There some vital information we are not supposed to post online. Although, this might be difficult for a lot of us since many of us work and earn online. And many do big businesses online, so we are all having this as a problem. But still, we need to limit some information, especially those that are more important and private. This is my entry into the #indiaunited weekly contest. Join #here. Thanks for visiting friends 😍💕. ================================= Best Regards @sunshine29 🧡 ===========================

body.title: [Esp-Eng]
body.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWXmFXoTa1nCvw35V4dNH1nuNFHhCUVppCiitc6DBbb9o/1779915615728.png)

[Fuente](https://pixabay.com/es/vectors/amamantamiento-maternidad-madre-1582978/)

La maternidad es un viaje intenso, lleno de momentos hermosos, pero también de desafíos emocionales que a veces parecen insuperables. Validar lo que sen siente, buscar apoyo y conectar con su “niña interior” puede convertirse en una terapia sencilla.  

Hace poco, una paciente me compartía su preocupación. Desde que tiene un implante anticonceptivo subdérmico con progesterona, siente que su carácter cambió. Irritabilidad, agresividad, cambios de humor… todo esto en medio de la exigente tarea de ser madre primeriza de una niña de dos años. Me contaba que cualquier detalle la desbordaba: si la niña no quería comer, se molestaba; si hacía una pataleta, perdía la paciencia. Incluso notaba que su hija imitaba sus reacciones, golpeando a los abuelos o diciéndoles que se fueran.  

Su angustia era genuina: “Yo no era así”, me repetía. “Me preocupa que un día esté peor y no logre controlarme.”  

Este relato es más común de lo que pensamos. Muchas madres atraviesan un torbellino de emociones en los primeros años de crianza. Los anticonceptivos hormonales pueden influir en el estado de ánimo, sí, pero también pesan el cansancio, la falta de sueño, el estrés social y la propia etapa de oposición de los niños pequeños. Todo se mezcla y se convierte en un círculo vicioso: no dormir bien aumenta la irritabilidad, la irritabilidad dificulta el descanso… y así sucesivamente.  

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXwsk8ERbHvq13ZTwkYa6ghYVUYi5UqNEKQkbNBiqSRus/1779915894108.jpg)

[Fuente](https://pixabay.com/es/illustrations/mujer-leyendo-sala-de-estar-leer-6284845/)

Validar lo que se siente:
Sentirse desbordada en estas circunstancias es completamente normal. Validar las emociones significa reconocer que lo que sienten tiene sentido en el contexto que viven. No se trata de juzgarse ni de ponerse etiquetas, sino de aceptar que la situación es difícil y que necesitan herramientas para afrontarla. Reconocer que estan cansadas, que cuesta mantener la calma o que necesitan ayuda es un acto de honestidad y de autocuidado.  

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcMjWUz5CRGoNh7A8w1jgqFxGkmDoj5D3uNf2g6vH7yq7/1779916147474.jpg)

[Fuente](https://pixabay.com/es/illustrations/d%C3%ADa-festivo-mujer-amor-antecedentes-7441664/)

Pequeñas herramientas de regulación:
Una de las más sencillas es la respiración consciente. En el momento en que la paciencia parece agotarse, detenerse unos segundos y repetir internamente: “Ahora estoy calmada, ahora puedo actuar con paciencia”. Ese gesto puede marcar la diferencia entre reaccionar con enojo o responder con serenidad.  

Otra estrategia es buscar micro-espacios de autocuidado. No hablamos de largas horas de descanso —que muchas veces no son posibles—, sino de cinco minutos para tomar aire, escuchar música o simplemente cerrar los ojos y respirar. Esos instantes ayudan a romper el círculo del estrés y a recordarnos que también merecemos un respiro.  

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTqidzS45jzoTUiLyc2Ei5Thnxh1vjv5p6Z3ZZnHkcWDK/1779916293019.jpg)

[Fuente](https://pixabay.com/es/illustrations/campo-ni%C3%B1a-ni%C3%B1o-p%C3%A1jaro-serenidad-9322539/)

El poder del juego simbólico:
En la conversación con mi paciente surgió una idea hermosa: jugar con su hija y las muñecas, montar un pequeño “microteatro”. Representar escenas donde la muñeca está molesta, no quiere comer o pega a otra, y mostrar cómo se resuelve con abrazos, besos o respirando profundo.  

Este tipo de juego no solo divierte a madre e hija, sino que despierta la “niña interior” de la madre, recordándole que también puede disfrutar y aprender a través del juego. Además, la niña ensaya conductas positivas y aprende que sus emociones son válidas, pero que existen formas sanas de expresarlas. El juego se convierte en un puente entre la crianza y el autocuidado.  

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVscMBXcvFF6LGmtFiaG1VBHxE1HQkJ2SUC7Ssy9UqVdA/1779916362995.jpg)

[Fuente](https://pixabay.com/es/illustrations/madre-ni%C3%B1o-granja-dibujos-animados-9088547/)

Generalizando la experiencia:
La historia de esta paciente refleja una realidad más amplia: la maternidad es un desafío emocional, físico y social. No existe un manual perfecto, pero sí podemos construir recursos prácticos que nos permitan transitarla con más calma. Validar lo que sentimos, buscar apoyo, cuidar pequeños espacios de descanso y usar el juego como recurso terapéutico son pasos que cualquiera puede dar en su vida cotidiana.  

La clave está en aceptar que no somos máquinas, que el cansancio pesa y que pedir ayuda no nos hace menos capaces. Al contrario, nos recuerda que somos humanas y que la crianza es un trabajo compartido.  

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRcnrmFtazwGPUMvJPGpkSPvEjwJ7oMukfgBsStJQU3C3/1779916501252.png)

[Fuente(https://pixabay.com/es/vectors/beb%C3%A9-los-beb%C3%A9s-ni%C3%B1o-ni%C3%B1os-6908460/)

Un mensaje final:
Y si quien me lee es una madre que se siente irritable, cansada o desbordada, recuerda: no estás sola, y tus emociones son comprensibles. Reconocerlas es el primer paso para transformarlas. A veces, la mejor terapia puede ser tan simple como un abrazo, una respiración profunda o un microteatro improvisado que nos recuerde que la calma también se aprende.

***

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmS8NxVgy4gwzyp6DQhH5bFiDnCC7e3UoZD2sHdkm8NfM4/1779916590106.jpg)

***

English Version 

\

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWXmFXoTa1nCvw35V4dNH1nuNFHhCUVppCiitc6DBbb9o/1779915615728.png)

[Source](https://pixabay.com/es/vectors/amamantamiento-maternidad-madre-1582978/)

Motherhood is an intense journey, full of beautiful moments but also emotional challenges that sometimes feel insurmountable. Validating what one feels, seeking support, and connecting with the “inner child” can become a simple form of therapy.  

Recently, a patient shared her concern with me. Since getting a subdermal contraceptive implant with progesterone, she feels her temperament has changed. Irritability, aggressiveness, mood swings… all of this in the midst of the demanding task of being a first-time mother to a two-year-old girl. She told me that any small detail overwhelmed her: if the child didn’t want to eat, she got upset; if she threw a tantrum, she lost her patience. She even noticed her daughter imitating her reactions, hitting the grandparents or telling them to leave.  

Her anguish was genuine: “I wasn’t like this,” she repeated. “I worry that one day it will get worse and I won’t be able to control myself.”  

This story is more common than we think. Many mothers go through a whirlwind of emotions in the early years of parenting. Hormonal contraceptives can influence mood, yes, but fatigue, lack of sleep, social stress, and the natural opposition stage of toddlers also weigh heavily. Everything mixes together and becomes a vicious cycle: poor sleep increases irritability, irritability makes it harder to rest… and so on.  

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXwsk8ERbHvq13ZTwkYa6ghYVUYi5UqNEKQkbNBiqSRus/1779915894108.jpg)

[Source](https://pixabay.com/es/illustrations/mujer-leyendo-sala-de-estar-leer-6284845/)

Validating what you feel:  
Feeling overwhelmed in these circumstances is completely normal. Validating emotions means recognizing that what you feel makes sense in the context you’re living. It’s not about judging yourself or labeling yourself, but about accepting that the situation is difficult and that you need tools to face it. Acknowledging that you’re tired, that it’s hard to stay calm, or that you need help is an act of honesty and self-care.  

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcMjWUz5CRGoNh7A8w1jgqFxGkmDoj5D3uNf2g6vH7yq7/1779916147474.jpg)

[Source](https://pixabay.com/es/illustrations/d%C3%ADa-festivo-mujer-amor-antecedentes-7441664/)

Small regulation tools:  
One of the simplest is conscious breathing. In the moment when patience seems exhausted, pause for a few seconds and repeat internally: “Now I am calm, now I can act with patience.” That gesture can make the difference between reacting with anger or responding with serenity.  

Another strategy is to seek micro-spaces of self-care. We’re not talking about long hours of rest —which often aren’t possible— but about five minutes to get some air, listen to music, or simply close your eyes and breathe. Those moments help break the stress cycle and remind us that we also deserve a pause.  

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTqidzS45jzoTUiLyc2Ei5Thnxh1vjv5p6Z3ZZnHkcWDK/1779916293019.jpg)

[Source](https://pixabay.com/es/illustrations/campo-ni%C3%B1a-ni%C3%B1o-p%C3%A1jaro-serenidad-9322539/)

The power of symbolic play:  
In the conversation with my patient, a beautiful idea emerged: playing with her daughter and dolls, setting up a small “micro-theater.” Acting out scenes where the doll is upset, doesn’t want to eat, or hits another, and showing how it can be resolved with hugs, kisses, or deep breathing.  

This type of play not only entertains mother and daughter, but also awakens the mother’s “inner child,” reminding her that she too can enjoy and learn through play. Moreover, the child rehearses positive behaviors and learns that her emotions are valid, but that there are healthy ways to express them. Play becomes a bridge between parenting and self-care.  

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVscMBXcvFF6LGmtFiaG1VBHxE1HQkJ2SUC7Ssy9UqVdA/1779916362995.jpg)

[Source](https://pixabay.com/es/illustrations/madre-ni%C3%B1o-granja-dibujos-animados-9088547/)

Generalizing the experience:  
This patient’s story reflects a broader reality: motherhood is an emotional, physical, and social challenge. There is no perfect manual, but we can build practical resources that allow us to navigate it more calmly. Validating what we feel, seeking support, caring for small moments of rest, and using play as a therapeutic resource are steps anyone can take in daily life.  

The key is to accept that we are not machines, that fatigue is heavy, and that asking for help does not make us less capable. On the contrary, it reminds us that we are human and that parenting is shared work.  

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRcnrmFtazwGPUMvJPGpkSPvEjwJ7oMukfgBsStJQU3C3/1779916501252.png)

[Source](https://pixabay.com/es/vectors/beb%C3%A9-los-beb%C3%A9s-ni%C3%B1o-ni%C3%B1os-6908460/)

A final message:  
And if the reader is a mother who feels irritable, tired, or overwhelmed, remember: you are not alone, and your emotions are understandable. Recognizing them is the first step to transforming them. Sometimes, the best therapy can be as simple as a hug, a deep breath, or an improvised micro-theater that reminds us that calm can also be learned.  

***

body.title: Growing passion fruit plants
body.body:
![IMG_20260527_083022.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWCs1oNeYsC2jebJzJPSJe28STukEEFyRhwuLBged9Esn/IMG_20260527_083022.jpg)

Hello, friends at Gems! How are you? I’m so grateful to God for allowing me to share with you again. Today I’ll be talking about these growing passion fruit plants.


![IMG_20260527_173643.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSUqvaESXJUQfo9x5E8zDKY3N9zm3gqQMXPWckY9zFZJj/IMG_20260527_173643.jpg)
 

These passion fruit plants—or maracuja, as they’re known in other places—were a gift from an aunt of mine, and they were very small. So when I got home, I put them in a pot with soil and transplanted them. Since then, I’ve been taking care of them, watering them only twice a day—in the morning and at night. 


![IMG_20260527_173648.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPeHNzGAfcDMdHfev8wBGKq1qiDFxzZKtY2ZNzhPXUHKu/IMG_20260527_173648.jpg)


I haven’t added any fertilizer yet; I’m waiting for them to grow bigger so I can transplant them to a trellis. My aunt was amazed when she saw them, since she says mine have grown so much while hers are still stunted. 


![IMG_20260527_173654.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTAFA4sAu2fc3dAAsAmuHeV6E8bH6DwBS4bqLbhzrNgiy/IMG_20260527_173654.jpg)


My grandmother used to say that not everyone has a green thumb.

body.title: How my day went…🙁😕on a public holiday
body.body:
by isalifestyle on Girly Isabella 
View my bio on Blurt.media: https://blurt.media/c/girlyisabella [![How my day went…🙁😕on a public holiday](https://blurt.media/lazy-static/previews/cade2c29-2f6e-4287-b31e-7909d7ad0d50.jpg)](https://blurt.media/w/6kThiUdJNYkmqbiU8XXVEH) 
 
 Today was a public holiday for *Eid Malud*, so the whole day had a different pace from the usual routine.

The morning started around *9 AM*, but instead of stepping out early, the time went into an extended gaming session. Hours passed quickly, and before noticing, it was already *1 PM*. The focus was completely on the games, with little break in between.

Right after that, the plan shifted. There was a *political movement* scheduled, and it ended up lasting about *3 hours*. It wasn’t a local event either — the journey took them from *Imo State to Abia State*, so a good amount of time was spent traveling as well as participating.

By the time everything wrapped up, the day had been split into two distinct parts: a long, uninterrupted stretch of gaming in the morning, followed by hours of movement, travel, and activity in the afternoon. The holiday ended up being more active and eventful than expected.
Thanks for visiting  
 ***
[**Check out today's video..!**](https://blurt.media/w/6kThiUdJNYkmqbiU8XXVEH)

body.title: Field And Stillness; No Noise, No Rush Just Green Field
body.body: >\nIt was a quite and a peaceful day here at the Farm yesterday, no noise and only the sounds of wind breeze and splashing of water at the river. This month is the manggoe season and expected that most of the manggoe tress produced lots of manggo fruits. As for that, I checked most of the fruit trees we have here and I felt very happy that some of it are already have lots of manggoes. Most of the manggoes here are Russian Manggoe, it is a kind of big and tall fruits and highly demanded at the super market. Last week, we created smoke our of dry manggoe leaves here and now, hundreds of fruits can already be seen.\n</div class=\

>

![Messenger_creation_725BE3CE-BCED-4184-9F31-F5EADAC78349.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/daily.life/EogMNPf8iHY4KUkchgEgiS3p5pigdoU3Ff2i744j7zTissFtTyzFD3uzqPZGRW7fYYL.jpeg)
</center>
Most of the fruits are very easy to reach, but I felt very worried because it will might be gone when we are not here at the farm. Most of the people who pass by here are attracted and will get the fruits without asking any permission. But my Father told me that He will stay here for a few Months just to look out our fruit trees and young coconut plants. It can help our plants and fruits safe without getting gone.

![Messenger_creation_13C3122A-E613-487E-9644-98B20C7E386B.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/daily.life/Ep1XurL5CuuS4nJ6tqEyQb4gBtr4JSHMLJRoMAdQDcinLnAD2zsJCwTSAiEwED2C7qc.jpeg)
</center>

![Messenger_creation_1DDF7A96-2EA7-4CA3-A534-D375D1A2417F.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/daily.life/Eou9iHNJ2X6jnG8UkcyvP9ZL1PbLgsAapmsGfCnRxhgzJbTGMstcGx55gveCybyzLQi.jpeg)
</center>
Here at the farm, we also have this simple manual water pump. This was built many years ago and it produced lots of water even in a hot and intense heat situations we experienced here. The water comes out from this water pump is drinkable and it supports lots of houses on nearby Sitios and also us here at the farm. Everytime when we do gardening and giving water for the animals like cows, we will get more waters here instead at the river. This can make the animals safe and the water is surely very clean. 

![Messenger_creation_C0DA64BE-70D7-4800-9DF0-8DCE759E2D95.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/daily.life/Eos1KyGJUFtLJAbRAhJZJkHmiWfXE4vgqbDWtUqxSUmgC2bmhWcqBy2EfqqxbZmsTXr.jpeg)
</center>
Not only exploring the Green field farm but also checking our farm animals like our goat. Our place is full of wild grass grows and it is perfect place for farm animals. Oir goats and cows always fed here in this place everyday because of the grass they can eat. Since it was already 10 in the morning, and the heat from the sun becomes more intense that is why I decided to untied the rope of my goat and transferred to other place where the goats wont exposes to the sun. Just as what I did to our Cows here.

![Messenger_creation_48112B11-AC63-435B-95F2-21DC60EF4C4B.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/daily.life/EpvhV2XhJhmcXFDzywRJ76ev82RakT2emTzh8AvKqzFuFxnrCkyhmsjrYG4L4ra16eq.jpeg)
</center>

![Messenger_creation_287F8C0A-4A59-475D-8968-D00AE0714764.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/daily.life/EqDigaYFGqfMyhVQ1iNnP7jURM5vK6YQEt93tzQWsafTaQvJQp6gt7iVq61u7dFiF1d.jpeg)
</center>
This green fields we have here is very relaxing to eyes because of the green grasses. Those tall coconut trees are already produced lots of coconuts to be harvested this coming June 10. I felt very excited to went here again and helping to do harvesting. This place here was once cultivated by our Single tenant but as He died already, a thick bushes areas where lots of wild grass and small branches can be found but as the landowner hiers take actual possession by cleaning at harvesting the coconuts, the place is totally clean ready to plant any agricultural plants like Corns and vegetables. 

![Messenger_creation_6262BA8C-DBCD-42AB-A597-80860FB2154A.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/daily.life/Eoc82YL7KA5p3ZW565HJsPmjgJnzXHVGQjtZLQDQvmjcMUEZ1hNBtkVHB6kjzw9PfJM.jpeg)
</center>

![Messenger_creation_8CD9D428-E896-49F7-8EA7-426D06BF5D8A.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/daily.life/Eoc7ZFMBNuNCgyALFfFMs2TBUV2zRp1dXCqyEV2rVMf6RbXRPzXXoEqk29q9kkMWGXL.jpeg)
</center>
This is our Madre de Agua Plant, we brought those small branches for 1 USD that is 1 HBD already. After that, We hurriedly planted it here in this recycled empty sacks near at the water pump because this kind of plants is only grows near at the watery places. This kind of plants is perfect for farm animals like Goats and Cows, chickens also eat the leaves mixed in feeds. I am very happy to see that our planted branches of Madre de Agua plants are now producing lots of young leaves and a small branches. 

![Messenger_creation_7ADCA9F3-176B-477B-92D0-0A70B195ED38.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/daily.life/Eq5DbJku1qy5E1ckCJFJfPxqoMM1B8aaexjiiMyDrbxADYqEMYEVUdamgWG9QyFzNy7.jpeg)
</center>
As I finally went back home, I also picked this two fall coconuts and brought it at home also. This is also what I always do everytime when I explored our farm, to looked and gathered any fall coconuts here and put in one place so it will be easy to hauled and transported to other place.

![IMG20260527172017_00.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/daily.life/EoK6KqUyFoiY29odptDbMjrbYRCSwjQu1KDBmX5Q6cK2tdCdXdCj969vNrESfzcQeex.jpg)
</center>
After a few hours of exploring the farm, its time eat one of my favorite snacks, The Banana fritter. Our Generous and kind neighbor gave this to us and I noticed that the fritter was mixed with banana crumbs. It was very enjoyable day I had here at the farm and another exciting farm life experience wait for me tomorrow. 

Until next post, have a nice day to everyone.

body.body:
[![](https://hotipfs-3speak-1.b-cdn.net/ipfs/Qmc5QiLNWVenrQebsg5EPyd4t4g299NZL8n16A9Ect512w/)](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=davidnollearth/d36ee503)

▶️ [Watch on 3Speak](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=davidnollearth/d36ee503)


---

This is the video series for an oil painting 'Wisteria' I did from 2016-2020.  The painting was destroyed in 2021 due to a number of reasons, but mainly: the painting's faulty experimental linseed-epoxide substrait, Covid-19 crushing lockdowns, extreme poverty, family attacks and ongoing US government (Big Tech + Big Media) censorship of me and my 30 years of artwork.

Its not ideal to not be able to show this piece, but I still gained the knowledge of how to do it and invented several useful oil painting mediums & varnishes used in its creation which never yellowed and still cannot be bought anywhere.

I am posting these videos for posterity and for people that are interested in seeing an oil painting created from start to finish in the Baroque style evolved for the 21st century.  I also must have deleted some of the initial videos when I did the quick underpainting, but what still exists, I give to you.

I hope this can be an educational experience as no gallery will show any of my controversial art even today.

---

body.title: Malice keeping Break Marriage More Than Anything
body.body:
Marriage is supposed to be a place where two people find peace, support, and love in each other. But the truth is, not every marriage stays sweet all the time. There are moments of misunderstanding, anger, disappointment, and frustration. What really matters is how couples handle those moments. When malice begins to grow in a marriage, it slowly damages the relationship in ways many people do not notice at first.

https://img.leopedia.io/DQmPkuCZCwFLW6DX5rFPgWYXaB6ZgUnYor3cCoDgoCspmC1/1000220554.jpg 

[Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/wedding-beach-love-couple-1770860/)

Malice is more than just being angry. It is when someone keeps bitterness in their heart and intentionally acts in ways that hurt the other person. In marriage, this can show itself through harsh words, silent treatment, constant criticism, or even bringing up old mistakes during arguments. These things may seem small at the beginning, but with time they create distance between husband and wife.

I believe one of the biggest problems malice causes in marriage is the loss of healthy communication. Couples who once talked freely and laughed together may suddenly start avoiding each other. Instead of discussing issues calmly, every conversation turns into an argument. Pride takes over, and both partners begin to focus more on winning than understanding each other. When this happens often, love starts to fade little by little.

Trust is also affected when malice becomes part of a marriage. It is difficult to feel safe with someone who constantly speaks or acts out of bitterness. A husband or wife may begin to feel lonely even while living in the same house with their partner. That emotional separation can become very painful. Some couples stay together physically but are completely disconnected emotionally because unresolved anger has built a wall between them.

Another thing I have noticed is that malice makes forgiveness difficult. No marriage is perfect because nobody is perfect. Every couple will offend each other at some point. But strong marriages survive because both people are willing to forgive and move forward. When bitterness is allowed to stay for too long, couples keep records of past wrongs and use them against each other whenever there is a disagreement. That only keeps the wounds fresh.

Love cannot grow where malice is constantly present. Marriage needs patience, kindness, understanding, and effort from both sides. Couples need to learn how to speak to each other with respect even when they are upset. Sometimes a simple apology, honest conversation, or willingness to listen can save a relationship from unnecessary pain.

Malice does not keep good between husband and wife in marriage. It destroys peace, weakens trust, and creates emotional distance. A happy marriage is built on love, forgiveness, and mutual respect and understanding. When couples choose understanding instead of bitterness, their relationship becomes healthier and stronger over time.



**Thanks for checking on my blog and have a wonderful day** 


Posted Using [INLEO](https://inleo.io/@leemah1/malice-keeping-break-marriage-more-than-anything--84q)

body.title: Why Staking SPS Is One of the Smartest Moves in Splinterlands
body.body:
If you’ve been playing Splinterlands for a while, you’ve probably heard experienced players constantly talking about SPS staking. At first, it might seem like just another crypto feature inside the game… but the reality is very different.

Staking SPS is one of the most important long-term strategies for growing your account in Splinterlands. It’s not just about holding tokens — it’s about unlocking opportunities, increasing rewards, and becoming part of the ecosystem itself.

So why is SPS staking such a big deal?

Let’s break it down.  
  

<h1 style=\

>SPS Is More Than Just a Token SPS (Splintershards) is the governance token of Splinterlands. That means it powers a huge part of the game’s economy and future development. When you stake SPS, you’re not simply locking tokens away. You’re actively participating in the ecosystem while earning rewards at the same time. Think of it like planting seeds that slowly grow your account over time.

>Passive Rewards Every Day One of the biggest reasons players stake SPS is simple: passive income. By staking SPS, you earn additional SPS rewards daily. This creates a compounding effect where your account can continue growing even when you’re not actively grinding battles. For smaller players or free-to-play users, this is extremely valuable because it allows gradual progression without constantly investing more money. Over time, those daily rewards can become a serious advantage.

>
Better Long-Term Account Growth In modern Splinterlands, strong cards alone are no longer enough. The game has evolved into a full ecosystem where SPS plays a central role. Players with staked SPS are usually in a much stronger position for future updates, promotions, and reward systems. That’s why many veteran players consider SPS staking the financial foundation of a powerful account. A balanced account today usually includes: **_Competitive cards _** **_SPS staking _** **_DEC management _** **_Guild participation _** **_Brawl activity_** **_Governance: Your Voice Matters_** Another major benefit of staking SPS is governance power. Staked SPS allows players to vote on important decisions involving the future of the game, including: * Reward system changes * Card balancing * Economic updates * New gameplay features * Ecosystem improvements The more SPS you stake, the more influence you have. This transforms players from simple users into active participants helping shape the future of Splinterlands.

>Final Thoughts Splinterlands is no longer just a card game — it has evolved into a complete blockchain gaming ecosystem. And within that ecosystem, SPS staking has become one of the core pillars for long-term success. Whether you are a competitive player, an investor, or simply someone trying to grow steadily over time, staking SPS can provide: Passive rewards Governance power Future opportunities Stronger account progression Better ecosystem participation In many ways, SPS staking separates short-term players from long-term builders. And in blockchain gaming, long-term builders are usually the ones who win the most.

Although in the last year, I’ve seen more and more people giving up. There are many different reasons why those individuals left, but they did. While there are still a bunch of members active now, it’s great to continue adding members. We did so many things as a community. We did tons of raffles, group crypto buys, voice chats and more. During that time there was such an interest in making a silvergoldstackers silver round. This began in 2017. Members submitted designs and we voted on them to pick the winner. The first two years of the rounds sold out quickly. The final year of the round 2019 did not sell out. Ray Brockman worked out deal with the mint to produce the 1,500 rounds to be numbered. Whichever rounds didn’t sell got melted. I believe the final years total was somewhere in the mid seven hundreds. Making a silver round is a great undertaking and the cost now is not very appealing. My guess would be over $50 a round easily. So here is a set of identical numbered silvergoldstackers rounds.
/>\n\nMaybe someday we can get another round produced. But I highly doubt it at this point.

body.title: Heading to Wipeout
body.body:
>

> He smelled like herb.

It was the spring party evening at my daughter's school tonight, where the older kids put on a bit of a play of some kind, and there were a few songs and the like. However, as the parents were shuffling in, a father passed me and there was a very, very strong smell of herb. I would have been fine if it was weed, but it was *oregano!* It was like he had bathed in it and for the entire hour and a half, I could smell it, even though he was standing some five meters away from me. 


---


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tarazkp/243g1JVHX5pkeoLstDtFLADvJy9uU5csqJ8ovXm5ujcvhuoo49NYFch8D1B9iu3AE8Sap.png)


---

Since I was at the back and short, I didn't see much of the show on stage. Not that it mattered, because I didn't understand most of what they were saying anyway, as it was in Finnish. Still, it is always nice to see kids who like to perform, performing. Since the school has a lot of music nerd kids, there are also quite a few future theatre nerds. 

It is going to be interesting to see what happens in the future of performance art, because AI is already replacing actors and is getting hundreds of millions of streams on Spotify, because they don't have a filter to filter AI-generated music out - which is pathetic. But it is only going to become more mainstream and since some people are *already* falling in love with and committing suicide over their AI \

, it is going to get far worse.

I think that just like how people underestimated the impact of AI on creative pursuits like art and music, they are now underestimating how quickly it will go into the physical areas through robotics. Yes, it is going to take time to crawl under the sink and unclog a drain, but there are going to be *heaps* of other areas that are currently done by humans and a robot driven by AI with hundreds of sensors, will do it better. 

> It is going to get weird. 

But because of this inevitable continuous encroachment until we are obsolete, I constantly question what we are going to do with ourselves and if there will be anything to \
at all. I can't think of anything worse than sitting around for a lifetime with nothing to do. A lot of people I talk to think that it means we can do \

we want, but I suspect that a lot of the joy we get comes from doing something useful, and when there is no point to do it at all, the desire to continue disappears. Many behavioural studies back this view up also. And that is of course if we work out the economics of it. As currently, we need to earn in order to be able to consume, and the earning positions will dwindle, so consumers will dwindle. It doesn't matter how efficient a company can produce its product, if there are no consumers able to buy it. The economy is made to continually grow profits, but even now the only way to do that is to pump in inflation. When there aren't enough people earning to make businesses viable, they all collapse. As I was saying with a client yesterday, the vast majority of the supply chains are used on relatively useless consumer goods and services so we can be entertained. Crap is dug out of the ground, processed, machined, assembled and sold, so we can watch AI-generated TikTok videos. Cut out all of the entertainment related supply, and 80% of the economy disappears. So what happens when we can't even afford food? > The numbers don't add up. But hey, the laws of economics don't matter. And they don't really, *if we are able* to change the way we organise ourselves so that money is no longer the driving force required to be a consumer. I don't know what the trade will be, but there is always a cost involved. > Always a trade-off. We have been heading on this path for decades, but it is clear that the trade-off we are making for convenience, is our humanity. We are losing the ability to interact with each other, or even build our own skillset. Yet, time and again, I hear from people who are adamant that it will all work out for them, because they assume that their job is safe, or they have enough in the bank to ride it out, like an economic recession. But this isn't a wave that will pull back to sea, it isn't going anywhere except forward. > There is no riding it out. It is either learn to ride it as a species, or be wiped out as a species. body.title: A Random Memory
body.body:
You know how sometimes we randomly remember a moment in our past that makes us cringe? Well, I had one of those moments today, and it's something that happened years ago during my childhood that I didn't quite grasp the complete meaning of back then, but now that I do, I just can't help but cringe every time I think of it.

![1001117760.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/prayzz/242Y7md7aUoqaWEzmx5Pc2QBBVhu5yGX1rJnsNgrm97s5JZCtk1mEWC3YBDiXc4QcM7Bi.jpg)
<sub> [photo by Ewa Gillen](https://unsplash.com/photos/depth-of-field-photograph-of-kangaroo-HGPKUYFO-2k) </sub>

On this particular day, I had gone to my friend's house. The plan had been for me to eat with him at home, but after he brought out the pot containing the food from his kitchen, I changed my mind and told him that I no longer wanted to eat anymore. Meanwhile, by then he had already brought out two spoons, one for me and one for him.

This friend of mine lives in a public compound. This was back then when I and my family still lived in the ghetto, so almost every back door to a building led to another street, and everyone could walk in freely to access it.

Unfortunately for us back then, the public kitchen was right next to the back door at my friend's place, and I remember this lady had walked past and made a comment to my friend, one I never fully understood until years later.

She had made a funny remark on how my friend was enjoying himself to the extent where he now was eating with two spoons. She obviously was being sarcastic and was trying to tell us that she knew I was eating with him but had quickly given him my spoon when I heard her walking towards us.

That was obviously what she thought, even though that wasn't the case. And I know it's not a big deal, but every time I think about that situation, I wish I could go back in time and clarify to her that I really wasn't eating with my friend.

And it's not like doing that would change anything or do anything, but I just have to do it for my own sanity because, for some reason, it just doesn't sit right with me that she had gotten the situation entirely wrong.

It's weird, I know, but it has just refused to leave my mind, and I cringe every time I think of it.

body.title: The Hospital Deposit
body.body:
>



![1001599485.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/julie100/23z7DSczUapuWTMpSqnzdSRQHWjiP7U5y7vSeFEuUzd83hXfDJURQw9Cp8x5dcLMHyDhb.jpg)


It was the first time that Chika lied to her mother and the rain was gentle on the zinc roof above their Surulere shop.

This was Tuesday evening. The kind that perfumes Lagos with a scent of roasted corn and traffic fumes and wet sand.

“Have they given you your salary?” “Was it a boy in the womb or was it not?” Mama asked as she was placing Peak milk tins on the shelf.

Chika took her office shoes off, and tried to smile. “Not yet.”

The liar came in stealthily and sat down between them.

Her mother slowly nodded her head. “Hmm. This country.”

Chika looked away.

In reality, it was even worse.

Three weeks ago she had invested nearly all her savings in an online business her colleague promised would “change her life”  Femi. Crypto trading. Fast profits. Easy money. He had sent her screenshots of withdrawals, and smiling faces with dollar bills.

You are too careful, Chika!\

he said softly.

“I’m fine.”

“You’re not.”

Chika made some sort of effort to make a joke. “Small stress.”

Seyi rested his back against the wall next to hers. “Has someone stolen your heart?”

She almost smiled.

“Well, “I wish it was that easy.”

He waited and she wouldn't say a word.

She was able to sleep that night no more. She continued to look at the ceiling fan which was whirling slowly above her bed.

Lastly, approximately 2 a.m., she went to her banking application.

Balance: ₦11,420.

Her throat tightened.

She covered her face and started to cry silently.

Not small tears.

The deep one that affects the shoulders.

The next morning it was Sunday. Mama insisted that they go to church together.

Chika attended the worship service and heard nothing. People danced. The choir sang out loud. But her mind was still stuck in numbers and in regrets, and someone called out “Hallelujah.”

When people were coming out of the service, their pastor walked up to her and greeted her.

Pastor Daniel Okorie beamed with a friendly smile. “Chika, you're very tired, are you?”

“I’m okay, sir.”

“No, you, you're holding something.”

Those words did break her right off the bat.

However, she still managed to smile. “Just work stress.”

The pastor nodded. \

She wasn't intending to go.

But on Monday, after work, she was sitting in his little office behind the auditorium of the church. The room was rather musty, with a slight air freshener odor.

She didn't say anything for a few minutes.

All the other guys were waiting, but not Pastor Daniel.

Then at once the words flowed out.

Everything.

The investment. The lies. The fear. The shame.

“I destroyed our future,” she whispered at the end. “My mother trusted me.”

The room was in silence.

She expected disappointment.

But the pastor softly asked, “Have you told her?”

Quickly, Chika shook her head. “She’ll be hurt.”

“Yes.”

“She’ll cry.”

“Maybe.”

“She may not have faith in me again.”

Pastor Daniel folded his hands. “Is this something that you are carrying on your own that is helping?”

This question remained unanswered.

Chika noticed that her fingers were trembling.

She knew how exhausted she was for the first time in weeks.

The pastor sighed quietly. “Loss doesn't kill anyone, it's silence that kills.”

Her eyes were filled once more.

When she arrived home that night NEPA had taken light. Mama was sitting outside with neighbours, fanning herself.

“Chika, before it's too late, you need to eat the rice.”

But Chika did not move from where he was standing by the gate.

“Mama…”

The older woman looked up at once when she heard something about her voice.

After twenty minutes they were sitting by themselves in the dark sitting room, between them being lit only by the light of rechargeable lamps.

And Chika confessed.

Every single thing.

First, Mama remained silent.

There was a hush that was oppressive.

Gradually her mother leaned back and pressed her hands to her face.

“Aiih, Chika…”

Her voice was disheartened.

“Apologies,” Chika stuttered time and again. “Ohhhh, sorry, mama.”

Her mother gazed at her for a good long time.

“During my father's life when he was deceased, I lost money as well,” she said quietly, “I thought my life was finished then.”

Chika squinted her eyes, stunned.

“Well, it wasn't the money that killed me,” Mama continued, “it was the shamefulness.”

Chika cried again as the tears rolled down her face.

“Well, I was frightened,” she said.

“I know.”

Mama stretched out to her, and took her hand.

There was little else going on in the room, apart from the generators outside roaring in the street.

Finally her mother said, \

Not angrily. Not dramatically. Just simply. For some reason, those three words helped Chika to release something from his chest. For the first time in many weeks she took a full breath. Traffic went outside, yelling into the night at Lagos. The burden had finally begun to depart from the little room.

body.title: My Big Sister Wants to Talk Again
body.body:
My big sister wants to talk to me again. 
-------------------

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmesseYvEPAfpis1vKaxS3UGzkc8HQD3UkxK7BkC2fyDLW/1779916494448.jpg)

I first stopped talking to my sister over 2 years ago now. To be fair, the movement had originally started with her -- she suddenly and without warning went MIA. 

When I confronted her about her absence, I received back, \

Despite the fact I hardly ever smoked in front of her, and the last time I had was a year, if not YEARS ago. 

(And I'm not even going to begin to defend weed -- this God-given medicine has saved my life on 4 separate occasions while fighting a deliberating condition.)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdvPstNvxYmG16kxM5KwYUX5PKkGEaxT4igxL1sxoKieT/1779916529575.jpg)

This is the same sister who abandoned me, while I was 3,000km away from home and being physically ab🥴ed by my ex, because I \

leaving and driving home by myself. 

So, I thought, that's enough, and Blocked her on everything. She has since moved to the UK and is engaged to her fiance. 

That was 2 years ago. 
-----------------

Today, my dad messages me to let me know that my sister wants to talk to me again. 
-------------------

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWqLW5RcjAdGNXrS1kRsXwy53HBUpwEJyv1aRmoXJBLAp/1779916689520.jpg)

And, without hesitation, I told him no thank you. Here's why...
----------------------

God tells us NOT TO LOOK BACK. He made an example of Lot's wife when she looked back at Sodom by turning her to salt; salt symbolizes preservation, which is what she desired to do with her old life when she looked back. 
-----------------------

Jesus reiterates this lesson in the New Testament:

\

(Luke 9:62)
--------------------

God tells us not to look back because the past can tarnish the future. When we think of the past, we often do so negatively: with regret, shame, anger, unsatisfaction -- even the happy moments we recall sorrowfully, knowing we can never go back. We waste so much of our lives being stuck in a time that has long since passed, that already existed, over the future that calls us to actively focus upon it. 

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbhf8fXSCWsDvzjP2JmR3E5hiopGNeu5w4AAvAjLFH53F/1779916809173.jpg)

God tells us not to look back because He has SAVED us from those situations, from those people, for a reason -- and you can guarantee that reason is for YOUR BETTERMENT. We sacrifice the vices, habits, environments, and bad influences for the sake of a better us, a better tomorrow. 

I realize this -- I have ALREADY realized this awhile ago. I have already established contact with those who never repented for their prior sins against me first, and it simply does not work. 

I do not want it to. God has already removed several people/stumbling blocks from my life since I started walking on His path. No regrets. I pray that He continues to remove anyone else who is a hindrance to my progress. 

\

There are moments when I just need to get away from everything for a little while. No notifications, no sales, no stress, no endless scrolling… just silence, fresh air, and time to think 💭

Being young doesn’t mean life is easy. Sometimes people only see the pictures, the smile, or the cute outfits, but they don’t see the pressure behind everything. Trying to make money online, dealing with uncertainty, and still pretending everything is okay can be exhausting sometimes.

I still dream about the day I can live more freely, travel more, invest smarter, and stop worrying so much about surviving month by month. Until then, I’ll keep moving forward one step at a time 🤍

body.title: Shadow Hunters SMASh Contest - Round #427 A Redundant Shadow! [Eng/Esp]
body.body:
> Hello friends of [Shadow Hunters](https://ecency.com/created/hive-179017), happy hump day! I usually post my SMASH contest entry on Saturdays, but this week I've been swamped with teaching responsibilities at the university. I'm starting not only lab sessions but also theory classes! This has prevented me from sitting down to write in my favorite community, so I decided to gather the material to participate in this contest [round #427](https://ecency.com/@melinda010100/shadow-hunters-community-smash-contest-79e225099f08d) on the fly. Actually, this isn't my usual lab routine, but as a coordinator with several years of experience, I know I should always be present during the lab sessions of the professors in my teaching unit. Unexpected situations always arise that require solutions, sometimes unorthodox ones. And there I was, sitting in the equipment room, making sure the still and ice chest were working so the students would have distilled water and ice for their subcellular fractionation lab. While I was there, the afternoon sun was already beating down on the teaching buildings with all its fury, and of course, the heat was intense. I had to step out of the equipment room into the hallway for some fresh air, and there I noticed the shadows cast by the emergency stairwell. The angle at which the sun was hitting them created this peculiar shape that I wanted to share with you.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYabDT6vpjqBvJNz4AmNDWY8k6bv4Ke6C6WEnEC6N6Gah/photo_5_2026_05_27_13_02_10.jpg)|![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSoajR6cPgGC9huAPNAD54hBVWiBnuRgGzqciFGJkuM6z/photo_4_2026_05_27_13_02_10.jpg) --|--

> The shadows cast by these buildings are simply spectacular. What's most exciting is that, depending on the time of day, you can see one or several types of shadows. In this case, we're seeing the horizontal wall supporting the vertical concrete columns projected onto the stairs. From below, the effect isn't noticeable, but when viewed from above, you can see how that horizontal shadow distorts, creating a stepped shadow on the stairs—a redundant shadow intersected at a perpendicular angle by the thin shadows of the vertical walls.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYPrmpL6s5WE6Gx7tGFC3SvCGhJsZD7eLHgQmQC5PbYgW/photo_2_2026_05_27_13_02_10.jpg)
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bulkathos/23tRvWxqnFqswK34rLXwwDzLFHimD2xstYf7ZmmjmX39TA7DFGfV3AbTDuBxHmK6AMydA.png)

> Well, friends, I won't lie, I ended up leaving that lab session around 7 pm! I had started at 7 am and had only had breakfast, so after 12 intense hours of work, I was exhausted and starving. But at least the students' experiment turned out beautifully, and I left with the satisfaction of having captured an exceptional shadow, so I can't complain, friends. See you in the next SMASH contest where we'll continue hunting shadows to share with you. Best regards!
--- # Versión Español ---
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZobrfFDhtoRtPgWeThk9QwrsYtnd7Cq5PzPtZgi4mr5L/photo_3_2026_05_27_13_02_10.jpg)

> Hola amigos de [Shadow Hunters](https://ecency.com/created/hive-179017), feliz ombligo de semana! Normalmente dejo mi aporte al concurso SMASH para los sábados, pero esta semana se me han justado todas las responsabilidades en la docencia de la facultad, no solo comienzo prácticas de laboratorio, sino teoría también! Esto me ha impedido a sentarme con calma a escribir en mi comunidad favorita, así que decidí conseguir el material para participar en este concurso [round #427](https://ecency.com/@melinda010100/shadow-hunters-community-smash-contest-79e225099f08d) sobre la marcha. En realidad, esta no es mi práctica de laboratorio, pero como coordinador y ya con varios años de experiencia, se que siempre debo estar en las prácticas de los profesores de mi unidad docente ya que siempre surgen eventualidades que requieren formas de resolver que en algunos casos son poco ortodoxas y aquí estaba yo, sentado en el cuarto de equipos supervisando que el destilador y la hielera estuviera funcionando para que los estudiantes tuvieran agua destilada y hielo para su práctica de fraccionamiento subcelular. Mientras estaba allí, ya el sol de la tarde estaba incidiendo sobre los edificios docentes con toda su furia y por supuesto la sensación de calor no se hizo esperar, tuve que salir un momento del cuarto de equipos hacia el pasillo para tomar aire y alli me conseguí con las sombras de las escaleras de emergencia que con el ángulo en la que incidía el sol le dieron esta forma tan peculiar que quise compartirla con ustedes.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYabDT6vpjqBvJNz4AmNDWY8k6bv4Ke6C6WEnEC6N6Gah/photo_5_2026_05_27_13_02_10.jpg)|![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSoajR6cPgGC9huAPNAD54hBVWiBnuRgGzqciFGJkuM6z/photo_4_2026_05_27_13_02_10.jpg) --|--

> Las sombras que se forman en estos edificios son simplemente espectaculares, lo más emocionante es que dependiendo de la hora del día puedes conseguir una o varios tipos de sombra y en este caso lo que estamos viendo es el muro horizontal que da soporte a las columnas verticales de concreto proyectarse sobre las escaleras. De abajo hacia arriba no se nota el efecto, pero de cuando la perspectiva es de arriba hacia abajo se ve como esa sombra horizontal se deforma y es como ver entonces una sombra escalonada sobra las escaleras, es decir una sombra redundante que esta atravesada en ángulo perpendicular por las finas sombras de los muros verticales.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYPrmpL6s5WE6Gx7tGFC3SvCGhJsZD7eLHgQmQC5PbYgW/photo_2_2026_05_27_13_02_10.jpg)
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bulkathos/23tRvWxqnFqswK34rLXwwDzLFHimD2xstYf7ZmmjmX39TA7DFGfV3AbTDuBxHmK6AMydA.png)

> Y bien amigos, no les mentiré, terminé saliendo de esa práctica de laboratorio casi a la 7 pm! cuando había entrado a las 7 am, y solo había desayunado por lo que después de 12 horas intensas de trabajo terminé exhausto y con mucha hambre. Pero al menos a los estudiantes el experimento les salió hermoso y yo me fui con la satisfacción de haber conseguido una sombra excepcional, así que no me puedo quejar amigos. Nos vemos en un próximo concurso SMASH donde seguiremos cazando sombras que compartirles. Saludos!

body.title: Late nights carry a different kind of silence.
body.body:
Around 2 in the morning, everything slows down. Phones stop ringing, social media becomes quiet, and most people are peacefully asleep. But somehow, that is the exact moment when the mind becomes the loudest. During the day, life keeps us distracted enough to avoid certain emotions. Work, entertainment, conversations, responsibilities — they all keep the heart busy. But once the night becomes still, there is nothing left to escape your own thoughts.

And that is when hidden emotions begin to speak.

Old memories suddenly return without warning. Small disappointments feel bigger than they should. A person you tried to forget enters your thoughts again. Unanswered questions replay inside your head, and regrets begin visiting like unwanted guests. Sometimes the mind even creates imaginary conversations, hoping to finally receive the closure reality never gave.

The strange part is that you may not even know exactly what is hurting you.

You just feel mentally tired.

You lie awake staring into darkness, thinking about how quickly people change, how some friendships slowly disappear, how dreams take longer than expected, and how life looks so different from what you once imagined. These emotions are difficult to explain because not every pain comes with tears. Some pain simply sits quietly inside the chest.

The hardest thing about midnight thoughts is how real they sound.

At night, doubts become stronger:
“Am I falling behind in life?”
“Do people truly understand me?”
“Will things ever get better?”

Yet many of those thoughts lose their power once daylight arrives.

Darkness has a way of making loneliness feel heavier. The quieter the night becomes, the louder the overthinking grows. Memories become emotional, and the heart becomes more sensitive than usual.

But not every late-night thought is harmful.

Sometimes silence forces us to face truths we have been avoiding. It reveals emotional wounds we ignored while pretending to be okay. And sometimes it reminds us that even the strongest people need comfort, healing, and rest.

People often speak about success, discipline, and motivation, but very few speak about the private battles people fight inside their own minds after midnight.

Some people spend the whole day smiling around others, then quietly fall apart once they are alone.
Some people look completely fine outside while carrying emotional exhaustion nobody notices.

Maybe that is why kindness matters more than we think. We never truly know what someone is struggling with once the world goes silent.

So if you ever go through nights like these, remember this carefully: every thought that appears in darkness is not necessarily the truth.

Sometimes the mind is simply exhausted.
Sometimes the heart only needs peace.
And sometimes what feels unbearable at 2 AM becomes easier to carry after sunrise.
