body.title: Jatropha multifida [Spn/Eng]
body.body:
>Magica semana llena de salud, energía, ideas maravillosas, magia. Encuentros con tu propio ser y mucho entusiasmo en cada actividad que realicen.

\n\n

>Esta vez comparto esta especie que se encuentra en las caminatas matutinas que realizo cada día. Bien cuidadas o no, igual están presentes en las calles adornando con sus hermosas flores de colores y hojas verdes, a veces parece que las siembran allí luego las olvidan, sin podarlas, atenderlas, darles su amor que también se lo merecen por mostrar su belleza (así las veo, bellas) además de su función biológica para nosotros los humanos como es ayudar a mantener el aire limpio. Esto es de acuerdo a mi observación, aunque es una planta que presenta ciertas característica de tener cuidado al manipularlas, acerca de esto se desprende, lo que aquí se comparte.

https://www.glitter-graphics.com/images/t/b/480x60/2838/2838549ab0hu2ihc1.webp

>La jatropha es un arbusto o árbol pequeño de hoja perenne con flores espectaculares que atraerán mariposas y colibríes a tu jardín. Hay dos especies de jatropha que crecen muy bien en el sur y centro de Florida: Jatropha integerrima y Jatropha multifaria.

\n\n

>De acuerdo a la investigación realizada la planta que se comparte es la especie Jatropha multifida, conocida comúnmente como planta coral, es originaria de México. Esta especie presenta inflorescencias circulares de color rosa coral y un follaje de aspecto claramente tropical, profundamente dividido y en forma de abanico. La planta coral es un poco más sensible al frío que la Jatropha peregrina.

\n\n

>Su nombre científico es Jatropha multifida conocida en varias regiones como Planta de Coral, Tártago Emético, Chaya brava, o Ceiba de Jardín (este último nombre para mi es más fácil de recordar)

https://www.glitter-graphics.com/images/t/b/480x60/2838/2838549ab0hu2ihc1.webp

>Entre sus características se puede señalar que todas las partes de la jatropha son venenosas si se ingieren, así que se debe tener cuidado si tiene niños o mascotas que frecuentan su jardín. Es importante esta acotación acerca de esta planta, es una especie que la he visto en un solo espacio, así pequeña. Luego por otro espacio vi otra de más tamaño aunque casi sin vida. Comprendo que por ser una planta venenosa si se ingiere, evitan tenerlas en casa o espacios abiertos. (Igual es hermosa).

\n\n

>Es un árbol tropical de hoja perenne con tallos delgados y múltiples troncos. Estas plantas pueden alcanzar unos 4,5 metros de altura y tener una extensión similar si no se podan.

\n\n

>Por las características de esta planta y la Evaluación de Plantas No Nativas en Áreas Naturales de Florida, realizada por la UF/IFAS, ha catalogado a Jatropha gossypiifolia y Jatropha curcas como plantas invasoras que no deben plantarse. (Es decir hay que tener cuidados para tenerlas en jardines).

https://www.glitter-graphics.com/images/t/b/480x60/2838/2838549ab0hu2ihc1.webp

>Plantas con hojas profundamente lobuladas y una flor que se asemeja a un coral naranja con frutos verdes en forma de nuez. Se entiende por qué a Jatropha multifida se la suele llamar planta coral.

\n\n

>Una vez establecidas, Jatropha multifida requieren poco mantenimiento y toleran la sequía. Las plantas de jatropha necesitan un suelo bien drenado y, aunque toleran desde sombra parcial hasta pleno sol, florecen mejor en zonas soleadas. Esta planta no tolera la salinidad.

>La jatropha tolera bien la poda, lo que te ofrece varias opciones en cuanto a su forma. Puedes dejarla crecer de forma natural hasta convertirse en un interesante árbol de varios troncos, o, con un poco de poda, puedes darle forma de espaldera, arbusto o árbol de un solo tronco. A pesar que esta especie presenta la característica que puede dañar la salud de un humano se recomienda al tenerla cuidado al podar la jatropha, ya que su savia lechosa puede irritar la piel sensible.

\n\n
>La versatilidad de estas plantas no se limita a tus habilidades de poda: la jatropha también se adapta muy bien a macetas grandes en porches o patios.

>
https://www.glitter-graphics.com/images/t/b/480x60/2838/2838549ab0hu2ihc1.webp

>Have a wonderful week filled with health, energy, marvelous ideas, and magic. May it be a week of connection with your inner self and great enthusiasm in every activity you undertake.

\n\n

>This time, I'm sharing this species that I find on my daily morning walks. Whether well-cared for or not, they are always present along the streets, adorning them with their beautiful colorful flowers and green leaves. Sometimes it seems they are planted there and then forgotten, without pruning, tending, or giving them the love they deserve for their beauty (that's how I see them, beautiful), in addition to their biological function for us humans, such as helping to keep the air clean. This is based on my observation, although it is a plant that requires certain care when handling it, which is why I'm sharing this here.

\n\n

>Jatropha is an evergreen shrub or small tree with spectacular flowers that will attract butterflies and hummingbirds to your garden. There are two species of jatropha that grow very well in South and Central Florida: Jatropha integerrima and Jatropha multifida.

\n\n

>According to research, the plant being shared is Jatropha multifida, commonly known as the coral plant, which is native to Mexico. This species has circular, coral-pink inflorescences and distinctly tropical-looking foliage, deeply divided and fan-shaped. The coral plant is slightly more sensitive to cold than Jatropha peregrina.\n\n<div class=\

>Its scientific name is Jatropha multifida, and it is known in various regions as Coral Plant, Emetic Castor Bean, Chaya brava, or Garden Ceiba (this last name is easier for me to remember).

\n\n

>Among its characteristics, it should be noted that all parts of the jatropha are poisonous if ingested, so caution should be exercised if you have children or pets that frequent your garden. This is an important point to note about this plant, as I have only ever seen it growing in one small area. Then, in another area, I saw another, larger one, though almost lifeless. I understand that because it's a poisonous plant if ingested, people avoid having them at home or in outdoor spaces. (It's still beautiful, though.)

\n\n

>It's a tropical evergreen tree with slender stems and multiple trunks. These plants can reach about 4.5 meters in height and a similar spread if left unpruned.

\n\n

>Due to the characteristics of this plant and the Florida International Forestry Association's (UF/IFAS) assessment of non-native plants in natural areas, Jatropha gossypiifolia and Jatropha curcas have been classified as invasive plants that should not be planted. (In other words, care must be taken when planting them in gardens.)

Planting and Care

>Plants with deeply lobed leaves and a flower that resembles orange coral with green, nut-like fruits. It's easy to see why Jatropha multifida is often called the coral plant.

\n\n

>Once established, Jatropha multifida requires little maintenance and tolerates drought. Jatropha plants need well-drained soil and, while they tolerate everything from partial shade to full sun, they thrive in sunny locations. This plant does not tolerate salinity.

\n\n

>Jatropha tolerates pruning well, giving you several shaping options. You can let it grow naturally into an interesting multi-trunked tree, or, with a little pruning, you can train it into a trellis, shrub, or single-trunked tree. Although this species has the characteristic that its sap can be harmful to human health, it is recommended to be careful when pruning jatropha, as its milky sap can irritate sensitive skin. The versatility of these plants is not limited to your pruning skills: jatropha also adapts very well to large containers on porches or patios.

body.title: Applying For Jobs On The Indeed Platform: My Experience / Postulandome Para Empleos En La Plataforma Indeed Mi Experiencia  [ENG-ESP]
body.body:
>

Hello, everyone.

Hi everyone, I hope you're all doing great. We're still on the lookout for opportunities—stay tuned and I'll keep you posted. Well, folks, nobody here is giving up. I’m still on the hunt for a well-paying job, so I’ve applied through many platforms. As I’ve already mentioned, one of the most widely used is Computrabajo, and several people—myself included—have noted that sometimes recruiters never even look at the resumes. However, something curious has happened in my case: several companies have viewed my application, but we’re all still waiting for that call. You need to have a well-presented resume to catch the recruiter’s attention, and I have mine well-structured. I actually discovered Indeed among the many platforms I’ve explored, and I find it quite appealing. Here’s my experience: as you can see, they have openings for content editors, customer service representatives—or, as they’re more commonly known, call center agents. You really have to read carefully what they’re looking for, though I think the mistake they make is saying they need someone even if they don’t have the experience, and when you apply, it turns out that’s not what they’re looking for. Who can make sense of that? I’ve realized that having to learn English—or at least the basics—and trying to move up to those positions hasn’t been easy, believe me, and the few in-person jobs that exist pay just enough. Tell me if I’m the only one who thinks there aren’t many good job opportunities right now—you have to adapt to whatever you can get. The idea behind this blog is also to hear from anyone working from home: which platform has worked for you, or was it just a stroke of luck? I’d love to read your stories. I hope you enjoyed my post. Greetings, Hive Music Festival community. I hope you are all doing excellent. We continue moving forward with a new participation for the HMF; as always, I take the opportunity to share my experiences, which are things that undoubtedly affect my melodies throughout the improvisation.

The ups and downs in this life give a lot of context to everything I do. Since this week began, many things have happened: I feel that work has been slow and with less income compared to previous weeks. Somehow, I manage to stay calm, but what is it that I am keeping calm? Well, all those feelings of anxiety that manifest when seeing my plans frustrated in one way or another. Also, on the other hand, some of my family members have been sick due to the rainy weather, apart from the things we deal with day by day, such as the lack of water or electricity service; in fact, yesterday, just as I started recording for Hive, the power went out.

That doesn't bother me anymore; I am certainly indignant about the situation, however, for the moment, I just remain patient. On the other hand, I am also thinking about ways to have all those comforts; I will probably have to try new things to improve my quality of life and have my own water and electrical resources.

It is not an easy path; I have also had health issues, and sometimes there seems to be no chance to improve. But that is the mind telling you that \
when it should actually rise up saying, \

Progress comes when we stop calmly to think about how to approach the next situation with a plan that allows you to move ahead.

Los altibajos en esta vida le dan bastante contexto a cada cosa que hago, y bueno desde que empezo esta semana han pasado cosas, siento que ha sido lento el tema del trabajo, muy pocas ganancias a semanas anteriores, y de alguna manera logro mantener la calma, pero que es lo que mantengo en calma? pues, son todas aquellas emociones de ansiedad que se manifiestan al ver los planes en cierta manera frustrados, tambien por otra parte algunos en mi familia por los climas de lluvia han estado enfermos, a parte de las cosas con las cuales convivimos dia a dia, asi como que falta el servicio del agua o el de la electricidad, de hecho ayer justamente al empezar a grabar para hive, se fue la electricidad.

Ya eso no me molesta, ciertamente me indigna totalmente la situacion, sin embargo por los momentos solo permanezco paciente, por otro lado tambien pensando las formas para poder tener todas esas comodidades, problablemente otra vez tenga que intentar nuevas cosas para mejorar la calidad de vida y tener mis propias cargas tanto de agua como electricas.

No es un camino facil, tambien estuve con incomodidades de salud, a veces parece no haber oportunidad de mejorar, pero eso es la mente diciendote que \
cuando mas bien debe elevarse diciendo \

sigo avanzando, y el avance viene cuando nos detenemos en calma a pensar sobre como abordar la siguiente situacion con un plan que te permita avanzar.

Y todas estas cosas sin duda son las que queria compartir en mis notas interpretadas.

body.title: MCGI Topic Review | Christian life — a prayerful life
body.body: > https://youtu.be/DFhIujzvlvI?si=rJnkjHjmr4wFE6iP A Christian life is truly a prayerful life. As I look at my relationship with God I see that I need to pray on a daily basis and not just when I feel like it. Through prayer I communicate with God, confide my problems and thank God for all. In 1 Thessalonians 5:17, the Bible instructs us to pray constantly. A reminder to me that prayer is to be a life habit and not just when I have issues. In my personal life, there was a period when I was pretty bewildered and stressed out. I had lots of cares in my heart, but I was not praying much at all. I only quickly prayed and got on with my day. One night I was feeling very heavy inside and I set out to pray very slowly and honestly, telling God everything. Following that prayer, I was filled with a peacefulness that I did not know. It was as though God was saying don't be afraid. I realized during that time the true strength of prayer. Jesus also showed us the importance of prayer. The Bible tells us in Luke 5:16, “But Jesus often went aside to pray. Since Jesus took time to pray, I have to take time to pray in my own life. Prayer brings me strength, humility and closeness to God. I have also been taught that prayer is not just for requests, it is also for the purpose of relationship with God. I just pray at times to thank Him for his life, for his protection, for his mercy. In the book of Philippians I am told in verse 6 that I am not to be anxious but am to bring all things to God in prayer. To sum up, I think it is impossible to live a Christian life without prayer. Prayer helps me to keep my heart in God and helps, even during the hard times, with peace. I want to live a life of prayer daily, to trust God in all that I do.

body.title: Drifting with the atmosphere: an unusual Sunday
body.body: > Greetings, dear readers of Weekend Experiences. I’m a volunteer with the Spanish Red Cross, and last Sunday we were called upon to participate in an environmental activity to help protect the environment. In addition to assisting the injured and supporting immigrants, the Red Cross also carries out various environmental initiatives. That’s why a group of volunteers gathered in the town where I live, La Herradura, on the tropical coast of Andalusia. The event had two objectives: to collect polluting waste in an area of the beach at the end of the bay, and then to go on a kayaking excursion to collect water samples and analyze them for microplastics.

> When the day began, it wasn't cloudy, but there wasn't much sun. I felt excited because I had never gone kayaking before. New activities give you mixed feelings—they're a little scary, but they also get you excited. I put on my bikini, grabbed the shoes I wear to go into the water (the beach at La Herradura is full of rocks), grabbed a hat to protect myself from the sun, a long-sleeved shirt, a towel, dry clothes to change into when I got back from the water, and I put on some moisturizer. I didn’t bring my cell phone.

> When Daniel and I arrived at the meeting point, we saw some tourists who were about to head out to sea in kayaks, but we didn’t see anyone from the Red Cross. That’s when I realized I’d left my cell phone at home. We figured they’d arrive a little later, so I asked Daniel to take some photos of me. I walked over to the kiosk where the people renting out the kayaks were, and a man greeted me and said he was also a Red Cross volunteer, and that no one else had arrived yet. Pedro. We saw a Red Cross van drive by, but it kept going. Shortly after, three more volunteers arrived.
![IMG-20260525-WA0062.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/beaescribe/23y8z73cFvtDtzQixoiis6NDgu3UogcgXDt2t2EAwNsyiSkMbgf9w86SvrXm5jDmvVKx8.jpg) ![separador blancoynegro.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/beaescribe/23vsqueDeqMiXPMy19iWN6mH3SxmnfhavaLFeZiptP54FLq86pSU9amnAZoHRV7XFnXpn.png)

> Pedro decided to call the head of the environmental department; it turned out they had changed the meeting point, and they had been picking up trash on the beach for over an hour. That’s because there was nowhere to park where we were. They sent a message, but we hadn’t seen it. I explained the situation to Daniel, who had stayed behind for a while enjoying the beach; we said goodbye, and I went to where the Red Cross group was and started searching for and picking up polluting waste myself—plastics that people throw on the beach, cigarette butts, and I even found a piece of broken brick, construction debris. By then, at noon, the sun was much stronger.
![IMG-20260524-WA0042.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/beaescribe/EqUeuFofhbTVSwBwyxb8vdg2cYquHg9Ui1CMQW3sHR2iFh7WYRUk8GzSJMrLu9HbeYj.jpg) ![separador blancoynegro.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/beaescribe/23vsqueDeqMiXPMy19iWN6mH3SxmnfhavaLFeZiptP54FLq86pSU9amnAZoHRV7XFnXpn.png)
![IMG-20260524-WA0031.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/beaescribe/EptcMyKELUPiXSCa9xF1uUKFpofdV1Zqv82DPdiw5e8qpbd8r5z15AdMs96GDXS8p41.jpg) ![separador blancoynegro.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/beaescribe/23vsqueDeqMiXPMy19iWN6mH3SxmnfhavaLFeZiptP54FLq86pSU9amnAZoHRV7XFnXpn.png)
## *Adrift*

> Some say that common sense is the least common of the senses. That’s absolutely true. Daniel’s daughter (my current partner)—she runs a diving school—warned me that if I’d never kayaked before, I’d be better off going with someone who knew how to kayak. I didn’t listen to her. The logical thing would have been to listen to her, but I got into the kayak to head out to sea with two young women who didn’t know how to kayak either. Because they were the only people I knew in the group. It was a very foolish decision that had consequences.
![IMG-20260525-WA0063.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/beaescribe/243WMjm8dFVouqvjQuEvDoikuHkhdKySpcx6vhwZCqnQJrtC5FHE69yzRfWckTzSYJU61.jpg) ![separador blancoynegro.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/beaescribe/23vsqueDeqMiXPMy19iWN6mH3SxmnfhavaLFeZiptP54FLq86pSU9amnAZoHRV7XFnXpn.png)

> The three of us decided to use the restroom before heading out to sea, and we ended up running late. They had already given instructions on how to handle the kayak. A man came back to explain to us, very quickly, how it was done. It’s not easy, especially if you’re with another person. The instructor didn’t explain clearly to us that the person in front is the one who propels the kayak forward, and the person in the back is the one who steers if the kayak needs to change direction, but the person in the back must follow the pace set by the person in front. We did everything wrong; the person in the back was setting the pace and giving instructions, because some people just like to be in charge. I was in the middle and had neither paddles nor a say. And really, I had nothing to say.

> What happened? We weren’t making any progress—or were moving very slowly—and ended up all alone in the middle of the sea. We watched the rest of the group quickly swim away toward a cave that’s apparently very beautiful, but we couldn’t see it. We were out in the blazing sun, exhausted, and not getting very far, and when the group returned, a man came over to help us and started giving us directions, which is how we managed to get back to the beach. Very tired, sunburned, and in a bad mood. The moral of the story: we need to realize that we often make bad decisions that have negative consequences for ourselves. What was the right thing to do? Use common sense, of course—get in the kayak with someone who knew how to paddle. What could have been a pleasant activity because of the setting turned into something very unpleasant.
![separador blancoynegro.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/beaescribe/23vsqueDeqMiXPMy19iWN6mH3SxmnfhavaLFeZiptP54FLq86pSU9amnAZoHRV7XFnXpn.png)

> Since my native language is not English, I have had to rely on the Deepl.com platform to translate this article into English.
![separadores ondulante.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/beaescribe/23vsrS7E29oEF4iBqmwKikunxU2JASbabJMYECKTFXa4RTEjGAQmk1znVd5UBW73VunyG.png)
All photos belong to my personal photo album. The photos I didn't take with my camera aren't as sharp, but I wanted to share them to show what we did with the Red Cross group.
![Thanks for readind me.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/beaescribe/23viJrPqtctcizzoP6Y5mjkLQLF8W8cJ7uAxBYzz5JpM6iGkX47S7HknwpWjy5sCAm9sW.png)

body.title: Adiós a las manchas de mi baño / Goodbye to bathroom stains
body.body:
Hola amigos feliz tarde a todos espero que estén bien , les cuento que en la casa que vivo actualmente pasamos casi 4 meses sin agua fue una total pesadilla aunque compraba cisternas realmente no era lo mismo , eso hizo que la regadera del baño se manchar totalmente yo creo que fue por el uso constante de tobos en el baño aunque dos veces a la semana lavo la regadera con cloro estás manchas no se iban y ya me estaba generando una ansiedad terrible , en el supermercado encontré un limpiador para el baño y el inodoro de la marca alive y lo compre para probar.

>Hello friends, happy afternoon to all, I hope you are well. I wanted to tell you that in the house where I currently live, we went almost 4 months without water; it was a total nightmare. Even though I bought water from tankers, it really wasn't the same. This caused the shower to become completely stained. I think it was from the constant use of buckets in the bathroom, even though I wash the shower with bleach twice a week, these stains didn't come out and it was causing me terrible anxiety. At the supermarket, I found a bathroom and toilet cleaner from the brand Alive and bought it to try it out.

![Screenshot_2026-05-27-15-05-19-827_com.canva.editor.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmd3JTMLtGSvC89zynQ7MGjYXoTpyqVrU9WajqL5GJjhyz/Screenshot_2026-05-27-15-05-19-827_com.canva.editor.png)


![IMG_20260508_184500.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmZqWoPSTWxS51eKWyjzfFvkFA5UMfcFtKcyHPZbU9TNpb/IMG_20260508_184500.jpg)

Les puedo decir que tiene un olor bastante fuerte por lo tanto mantengan las puertas abiertas la otra es que por nada del mundo lo vayan a mezclar con Otro producto mucho menos cloro , en las instrucciones decía como usarlo y decía que si era para manchas muy fuertes aplicarlo directamente así que eso hice pues como les dije esas manchas ya yo le había talla con múltiples productos, después de aplicar deje actuar por 5 Min y talle con una escoba.

>I can tell you that it has a pretty strong smell, so keep the doors open. Also, under no circumstances should you mix it with any other product, much less chlorine. The instructions said how to use it and that if it was for very tough stains, apply it directly, so that's what I did. As I said, I had already scrubbed those stains with multiple products. After applying it, I let it sit for 5 minutes and scrubbed with a broom.

![IMG_20260508_184519.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmNsrKWvZBCSomARmATWJKCF9LiAJduYjF9LRuE8GKrTK4/IMG_20260508_184519.jpg)

![IMG_20260508_184616.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmNdri1qwbRCM3hKqspc81s7hEq5xjQuWMHPb7DfUkbHJw/IMG_20260508_184616.jpg)

![IMG_20260508_184621.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSkrWKdyvgYjMQdGqkeG4qMkYwJ8twbqto8cqCNF1yAuu/IMG_20260508_184621.jpg)

También aplique en el inodoro que este la verdad está bastante blanco Pero aproveche y aplique en el lavamanos que si tenía dos manchas pequeñas y quería ver si funcionaba , luego de dejar actuar y tallar muy bien saque el producto con abundante agua y por supuesto use guantes durante todo el proceso ya que como les dije olía bastante fuerte.

>I also applied it to the toilet, which is actually quite white. But I took the opportunity to apply it to the sink as well, since it had two small stains and I wanted to see if it would work. After letting it sit and scrubbing very well, I rinsed the product off with plenty of water, and of course I wore gloves throughout the process because, as I mentioned, it smelled quite strong.

![IMG_20260508_185310.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmVHxDJKq1b6fwuYQdTHFxTQ88H8NBQw51hGqcLM9BSNP3/IMG_20260508_185310.jpg)

El resultado fue espectacular el piso quedó como nuevo y todas esas manchas se fueron , y en lavamanos quedó sin una sola mancha de verdad recomiendo mucho el producto si tienen una mancha fuerte que no sale con nada , quedé muy satisfecha con el resultado.

>The result was spectacular; the floor looked brand new and all those stains disappeared. The sink was completely spotless. I highly recommend this product if you have a stubborn stain that nothing else seems to remove. I was very satisfied with the results.

![IMG_20260508_192634.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQiWbYQu1qgW1fCKWMk44ckPimMQ49AYRTqXuYvDr3tbK/IMG_20260508_192634.jpg)

body.title: When You Know Your Currency Is That Bad
body.body:
/></center>





My daughter asked me today how much the value of HIVE is and being on or about $0.06c it is roughly R1 with the exchange rate fluctuating between R16.3 and R16.5 to the US Dollar so give or take $0.061c. This is quite an eye opener knowing we all feel that HIVE is so low in value due to the markets and at least it has a chance of rising in value in the future.

The Rand with the US Dollar being fairly weak is still maintaining it's position for now and is expected to depreciate even more over the years to come. There is no silver lining with this one having returned to South Africa in 2004 and have slowly watched the Rand move from R5.61 to as low as R19.20 to the dollar since then. The crazy thing is HIVE will at some point have more value than the Rand and that is not a maybe, but guaranteed.

I have never looked at HIVE as being one on one with the South African Rand and even though this is quite shocking is also reassuring at the same time knowing HIVE is in USD and not in Rands. I have no positive things to say on the Rand as there is no long term future and why you have to keep all funds off shore in either USD, Euro or GBP.

Those that have wealth tied up in South Africa are here for the long term and they have no thought of leaving the country. What I have is two properties and a business, but the thoughts are not about staying and more about leaving. I see no point as I am not only thinking of myself, but my kids and grand kids and why I cannot tie finances up locally because at some point it will be impossible to move due to the weakness of the Rand.

I spoke to my son about this a while ago and his generation will at some point be stuck here if they have not moved already. Selling a property in South Africa for millions does not guarantee you a property overseas with the proceeds and a 4 bedroom house here will most likely only afford you a two bedroom semi detached house in the UK or Europe. This is the reality and why keeping funds off shore is the only sane way to think.

Having a crypto portfolio including crypto like HIVE does give me some peace of mind knowing that there is external investments if the need arises which I am sure it will at some point. the crypto in my mind earning rewards daily via staking is more of a plan B and is more a pension type fund for later in life. I can only imagine what it must be like having a pension fund in South Africa because it will never be enough no matter how much financial planning you have done. When the Rand hits R20-R25 to the USD even those well off would have lost 30% of their true wealth.

Posted Using [INLEO](https://inleo.io/@cryptoandcoffee/when-you-know-your-currency-is-that-bad-jgx)

title.title: Common Trig (Trigonidium cicindeloides)
title.body:
| Latin Name | Observation Date | Location |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ***Trigonidium cicindeloides*** | May 25, 2026 | Purulia, Natore, Bangladesh |

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVY16AFYj7GxZ2TWys5YmT5EkgvtkecSPMWagjzsCbhTb/mix_20260527_211313.jpg)

Nature sometimes plays a great game of hide and seek with our eyes. Today I am sharing with you a macro photo of an insect taken from a grass field in my village, which can fool anyone at first glance.
​When I saw this insect sitting on a leaf, I thought it might be a common beetle, given its black shiny back. But when I looked closely, its true identity came out. It is not a beetle at all, but a type of cricket, which has taken the form of a beetle to escape from predators.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcRysTHqLKoqQ8jUyomJdCDtyxXJpXwLekSXo9hseoJZ8/mix_20260527_210552.jpg)

​Let's learn some scientific facts about this great camouflaged insect:
​Common name:
**Common Trig or Pygmy Bush Cricket.**
​Scientific name:
***Trigonidium cicindeloides***
​Family:
Trigonidiidae (Sword-tailed cricket or cricket family).
​Size and Mimicry:
This is a very small insect. Its most notable feature is the dark blue-black hard covering on its back, which looks exactly like a beetle. But its thick reddish-orange legs and slender proboscis, which are longer than its body, prove that it is actually a jumping cricket.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXVAHs2meYbZhx7b2dSfPFn3TdB5ambWzNtSBpSXwvB4D/mix_20260527_211035.jpg)

​Habitat:
They mainly like to live in damp environments around ponds or water bodies, on short grass and low shrub leaves.

​Calling Song:
As adult crickets, they have a wonderful nature. Like other crickets, they also make a kind of sound or 'song' by rubbing their wings, with which they mainly attract a partner.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUa9emNAXeVvkFG6ZK6MGsNUjKRBaYYrCAwWUv9JoYHJd/mix_20260527_210842.jpg)

​Diet:
They usually survive by eating soft leaves of trees, rotten vines and occasionally other small insects and spiders in the garden.

​Its role in nature:
Although it looks a bit tough, it does not cause any damage to crops, so it is not considered harmful in agriculture. Rather, it helps to maintain the ecosystem of the garden as a natural food for frogs, lizards and birds.

​Have you ever seen a singing cricket disguised as a dung beetle? Be sure to share your opinion in the comments.


  I learned about them from various sites including iNaturalist, Wikipedia and Google.

(All posts are written in Bengali and translated into English using Google Translate.)

links.title: Everyone you meet is fighting a battle you know nothing about.
links.body: > ## Hello, everyone. I welcome you to my blog. Saw a post on a friend's status that says to be kind to people you cross paths with, for 9 out of every 10 people you meet are fighting battles you know nothing about, if not all 10 of them. A little kindness can actually go very far in giving them the courage to keep fighting or giving them the motivation they need to win whatever war it is that is going on in their head or life. Over the years I have come to realize that every action has a way of impacting those around us or those around when the action was carried out. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcKCSC1iihoR8VGYHrp9KMmvowbSFrKjCXTXpzDryq5qL/1779912955822.jpg) [Source](https://unsplash.com/photos/a-man-and-woman-kissing-BkhIxji_bJE) This impact can either be positive or negative; sometimes people can be handling the war in their heads perfectly until a friend or a family member says something that breaks them, and then they start losing the war and end up getting pushed to do what they would not have done if what was said to them was not said. Sometimes it is our action that breaks their spirit and forces them into things they have been holding back from. There are many people we are judging from afar, but I tell you that when you get close to them and hear how much they tried to hold back before they gave in, you will no longer be able to judge them as you are doing right now. We humans have forced each other to keep things boxed up. In those days it was believed that a problem shared is already half solved; these days the story is different because a problem shared becomes the talk of the town and a topic for discussion. For that reason we have been forced to keep things to ourselves no matter how heavy they are. Those days, once you make the move to share what is bothering you, you get people giving you all the attention you need. Today, the moment you do that, they consider you weak, and then they badmouth you to the point you regret ever thinking about opening up. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZ64iRziSdrL45VUc7P8EqnEJE6gKwYBctMmWSH4N8kQ2/1779912955781.jpg) [Source](https://unsplash.com/photos/man-in-red-and-black-hoodie-wearing-black-sunglasses-0faZdQINKi4) Our generation needs to relearn sympathy and empathy; we lack all of that, which is why we have the highest rate of suicide compared to the generation before us, because they helped each other, they gave listening ears to those who opened up without judging them, and they convinced those who tried to keep things boxed up to open up. Our generation is the opposite of all that, we shut those who try to open up and mock those who open up.

links.title: Can People afford HEALTHCARE?
links.body: > ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTMLAvEgcPxnX9Fhz63UdnTVNx1b5HNo1b7XN1APKCzHV/can_people_afford_healthcare.jpg) The health care situation is very complicated in several countries around the world. The good health of citizens, which should be one of the fundamental things in life, has become a market, in which the focus is no longer on keeping the patient well, but on increasing profit. And the problem has spread beyond hospitals that treat last-level problems, but to day-to-day consultations, where instead of prescribing cheap medicines or long-lasting solutions, it seems that the objective is to keep the patient alive, but continuing with the problem, which causes them to spend much longer on maintaining their health than would otherwise be necessary. Have you ever imagined what this scenario will be like with the arrival of AIs? One of the premises of this technology is that it will replace several functions, and one thing is a fact, in a time of need being attended to by a robot instead of a human being who can understand, at least a little, it will be something very difficult for any patient. This goes to show that no matter how bad the situation is, there is always room for it to get worse. The question that remains is: Is it possible to improve and for people to be able to pay the costs of healthcare? I'll be much appreaciated if you **Votes**, **Reblogs** or give any **Tips**. Thanks and have good reading! 🍀 ---

> ## Can People afford the costs of HEALTHCARE? When talking about healthcare costs, it is worth mentioning that in some countries, governments have implemented a system to help their population's health. An example of something along these lines is in the United States, which has a federal health insurance program called Medicare, which covers some hospital expenses that a person may incur. There's one detail, this program only comes into effect around the age of 65 and for people who have some specific problems. This means that the rest of the population ends up having to find some way to pay for their health care. What countries have not understood is that their population is the engine that makes the nation turn and a healthy population can produce more and for longer. If doctors and hospitals fail to treat younger patients who have a problem or fail to carry out preventive procedures, in the future they will not be able to perform their functions for society with the same efficiency, because they will be in pain, heart problems, illnesses, which could have been avoided if they had received average assistance. Even for a society focused on profit and capital, if analyzed from the point of view of efficiency, it is much cheaper to prevent a problem than to let it worsen and have to deal with it in the future. For people, the best thing to do is to try to improve their health to prevent as many problems as possible, by doing physical exercise, eating a good diet and seeking advice on how to improve their health from professionals. Think of yourself as a company, the better your health is, the less problems you will have in your production, just don't forget to do maintenance and adjustments from time to time. It's curious that sometimes people care more about their possessions than themselves. --- https://img.leopedia.io/DQmeCJZEK6UG5Tc3avBibmLNHkgkN9PXcmVN1jYhHR6aHGG/image.png ---

> ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTMLAvEgcPxnX9Fhz63UdnTVNx1b5HNo1b7XN1APKCzHV/can_people_afford_healthcare.jpg) A situação dos cuidados com a saúde é bem complicado em diversos países ao redor do mundo. A boa saúde dos cidadãos que deveria ser uma das coisas fundamentais à vida, se tornou um mercado, em que o foco deixou de ser deixar o paciente bem, para ir para o lucro cada vez maior. E o problema se espalhou para além dos hospitais que tratam problemas de último nível, mas para consultas do dia a dia, em que ao em vez de receitar medicamentos baratos ou soluções duradouras, parece que o objetivo é manter o paciente vivo, mas continuando com o problema, o que faz com que ele gaste na manutenção da sua saúde por muito mais tempo do que seria necessário. Já imaginou como será esse cenário com a chegada das IAs? Uma das premissas dessa tecnologia é que ela virá para substituir diversas funções, e uma coisa é fato, em um momento de necessidade ser atendido por um robô em vez de um ser humano que consegue entender, ao menos um pouco, vai ser algo bem difícil para qualquer paciente. Isso serve para mostrar que por mais que a situação esteja ruim, sempre há espaço para piorar. A dúvida que nos resta é: Será que é possível melhorar e as pessoas terem condições de pagar os custos dos cuidados com a saúde? Fico agradecido se você puder dar um **Voto**, **Reblogs** ou algum **Tips**. Obrigado e boa leitura! 🍀 ---

> ## Can People afford the costs of HEALTHCARE? Ao falar de custos com a saúde, vale mencionar que em alguns países, os governos implementaram um sistema para ajudar à saúde da sua população. Um exemplo de algo nesse sentido é nos Estados Unidos, que tem um programa federal de seguro saúde chamado Medicare, que cobre alguns despesas hospitalares que a pessoa venha a ter. Só que tem um detalhe, esse programa só começa a valer por volta dos 65 anos e para pessoas que tenham alguns problemas específicos. Isso faz com que o restante da população acabe tendo que arrumar algum jeito para custear os seus cuidados com a saúde. O que os países não entenderam é que a sua população é o motor que faz a nação girar e uma população saudável consegue produzir mais e por mais tempo. Se os médicos e hospitais deixam de atender os pacientes mais jovens que estão com algum problema ou deixam de fazer procedimentos de prevenção, futuramente eles não vão conseguir exercer as suas funções para a sociedade com a mesma eficiência, porque vão estar com dor, problemas cardíacos, doenças, o que poderia ter sido evitado se elas tivessem recebido assistência média. Mesmo para uma sociedade voltada para o lucro e para o capital, se for analisado do ponto de vista da eficiência é muito mais barato prevenir um problema do que deixar ele piorar e futuramente ter que lidar com ele. Para as pessoas o melhor é buscar formar de melhorar a saúde para se prevenir ao máximo de problemas, fazendo exercícios físicos, tendo uma boa alimentação e buscando conselhos de como melhorar a saúde de profissionais. Pense em si mesmo como uma empresa, quanto melhor você está de saúde, menos problemas você terá na sua produção, apenas não se esqueça de fazer manutenção e ajustes de tempos em tempos. É curioso que as vezes as pessoas cuidam mais dos bens do que de si mesmas. ---

# <center><u>English Version</u></center>
# <center><u>My Battle with Cancer #4: PET-CT</u></center>

**<u>Note</u>**: For this video, I wanted to try out a GIF thumbnail since I’ve seen other users doing it.

I recorded this video on 05-25-2026. It took me a while to get it out because I've had a hard time working on it; severe pain has returned. Anyway, here I’m going to show you a test result where things didn’t actually go badly, but I’m still not completely cancer-free. Why? It all comes down to metastasis and a lack of treatment (AFATINIB). In my recent conversations with my oncologist, she mentioned that it would practically be for life because my cancer is due to a congenital mutation. Who in Venezuela can spend $2,100 (USD) a month on medication just to survive? I'll leave that as an open question for the comments.

Now, let's look at the information I talk about in the video:

1. In the article I wrote about cycle 10, I mentioned this scan, which is important to see how the cancer is progressing [HERE](https://peakd.com/hive-110372/@gerzon/my-fight-against-cancer-cycle-10-new-center-espeng).

2. The oncology report instructed me to get a bone scan (scintigraphy) or a bone PET-CT.
 
3. I managed to get it done on 09-18-2025 at the Centro de Diagnóstico Docente (CDD), located in Las Mercedes, Caracas, Venezuela. (It’s one of the few places where they perform this scan; a while ago, it was the only one available in Venezuela, though nowadays there are more options).
 
4. I show the different images generated by this study. (When they do it, you lie down on a machine that scans you, very similar to a CT scan, and they inject radioactive material, just like in a bone scintigraphy).
 
5. I discuss what is mentioned in the report generated by the CDD, where some spots related to my current pain are visible. But overall, it turned out well, with no signs of the tumor or new nodules.
 
6. I mention a little something extra—even though it has nothing to do with the scan, it was something I did that same day: I took my mom out to eat at the CCCT (Centro Comercial Ciudad Tamanaco). It was a nice moment to break away from the medical routine.
---------------------
I hope to start recovering soon and bring you content more frequently. There are so many things I've wanted to share. I just have to go at my own pace due to the current pain.

# God bless you, and see you next time!

--------------




https://images.hive.blog/DQmTphUarKuYr5DZnpue1jqNXi6kg3s7koZrrYxYfaQvyGe/18.png

# <center><u>Versión en Español</u></center>
# <center><u>Mi lucha Contra el Cáncer: Recaída</u></center>

**<u>Nota</u>**: para este video quise probar una miniatura GIF ya que he visto a otros usuarios que lo han hecho

Este video lo grabe el 25-05-2026, Me he tardado un poco porque he tenido dificultades para trabajar en ello, me han vuelto dolores fuertes, y bueno acá voy a mostrar un examen donde realmente no salí mal, pero aún no he salido por completo del cáncer. ¿Por qué?, todo se resumen a la metástasis y falta del tratamiento (AFATINIB), en ultimas conversaciones con mi oncóloga me ha comentado que prácticamente sería de por vida, porque mi cáncer es debido a una mutación congénita, **¿En Venezuela quien puede gastar 2100$ (dólares) en un medicamento mensualmente para sobrevivir?**, Esa pregunta queda abierta para los que gusten comentar. 

**Ahora veamos referente a la información que comento en el video:**

1. En el artículo que hice sobre el ciclo 10 comenté acerca de este examen, que es importante para ver como va el cáncer [AQUÍ](https://peakd.com/hive-110372/@gerzon/my-fight-against-cancer-cycle-10-new-center-espeng).

2. El informe oncológico me indicaba Realizar Gamma grama o PET-CT Óseo. 

3. Logré realizarlo el 18-09-2025, en el Centro de Diagnóstico Docente, ubicado en Las Mercedes, Caracas, Venezuela (es uno de los pocos lugares donde hacen este examen, hace un tiempo era el único disponible en Venezuela, en la actualidad hay más opciones)

4. Muestro las distintas imágenes que se generan en este estudio, (Cuando lo realizan uno se acuesta en máquina, que te va escaneando, muy similar al de una Tomografía, e inyectan material radioactivo como en el Gamma Grama óseo).

5. Comento lo que menciona el informe generado por el CDD (Centro de Diagnóstico Docente), donde en se ven unos puntos relacionados con mi dolor actual. Pero en general salí bien sin rastro del tumor o nódulos nuevos.

6. Menciono algo extra, aunque no tiene que ver con este examen, fue algo que hice ese mismo día, invité a mi mamá a comer en el CCCT (Centro Comercial Ciudad Tamanaco). Un momento agradable para salir de la rutina médica.

----------------

Pronto espero ir recuperándome, y traer contenido más seguido. Hay muchas cosas que he querido contar. Tengo que ir a mi ritmo por los dolores actuales.

# Dios los bendiga, Hasta la próxima.


https://images.hive.blog/DQmTphUarKuYr5DZnpue1jqNXi6kg3s7koZrrYxYfaQvyGe/18.png

# <center><u>English Version</u></center>
# <center><u>My Battle with Cancer #4: PET-CT</u></center>

**<u>Note</u>**: For this video, I wanted to try out a GIF thumbnail since I’ve seen other users doing it.

I recorded this video on 05-25-2026. It took me a while to get it out because I've had a hard time working on it; severe pain has returned. Anyway, here I’m going to show you a test result where things didn’t actually go badly, but I’m still not completely cancer-free. Why? It all comes down to metastasis and a lack of treatment (AFATINIB). In my recent conversations with my oncologist, she mentioned that it would practically be for life because my cancer is due to a congenital mutation. Who in Venezuela can spend $2,100 (USD) a month on medication just to survive? I'll leave that as an open question for the comments.

Now, let's look at the information I talk about in the video:

1. In the article I wrote about cycle 10, I mentioned this scan, which is important to see how the cancer is progressing [HERE](https://peakd.com/hive-110372/@gerzon/my-fight-against-cancer-cycle-10-new-center-espeng).

2. The oncology report instructed me to get a bone scan (scintigraphy) or a bone PET-CT.
 
3. I managed to get it done on 09-18-2025 at the Centro de Diagnóstico Docente (CDD), located in Las Mercedes, Caracas, Venezuela. (It’s one of the few places where they perform this scan; a while ago, it was the only one available in Venezuela, though nowadays there are more options).
 
4. I show the different images generated by this study. (When they do it, you lie down on a machine that scans you, very similar to a CT scan, and they inject radioactive material, just like in a bone scintigraphy).
 
5. I discuss what is mentioned in the report generated by the CDD, where some spots related to my current pain are visible. But overall, it turned out well, with no signs of the tumor or new nodules.
 
6. I mention a little something extra—even though it has nothing to do with the scan, it was something I did that same day: I took my mom out to eat at the CCCT (Centro Comercial Ciudad Tamanaco). It was a nice moment to break away from the medical routine.
---------------------
I hope to start recovering soon and bring you content more frequently. There are so many things I've wanted to share. I just have to go at my own pace due to the current pain.

# God bless you, and see you next time!

--------------




https://images.hive.blog/DQmTphUarKuYr5DZnpue1jqNXi6kg3s7koZrrYxYfaQvyGe/18.png

# <center><u>Versión en Español</u></center>
# <center><u>Mi lucha Contra el Cáncer: Recaída</u></center>

**<u>Nota</u>**: para este video quise probar una miniatura GIF ya que he visto a otros usuarios que lo han hecho

Este video lo grabe el 25-05-2026, Me he tardado un poco porque he tenido dificultades para trabajar en ello, me han vuelto dolores fuertes, y bueno acá voy a mostrar un examen donde realmente no salí mal, pero aún no he salido por completo del cáncer. ¿Por qué?, todo se resumen a la metástasis y falta del tratamiento (AFATINIB), en ultimas conversaciones con mi oncóloga me ha comentado que prácticamente sería de por vida, porque mi cáncer es debido a una mutación congénita, **¿En Venezuela quien puede gastar 2100$ (dólares) en un medicamento mensualmente para sobrevivir?**, Esa pregunta queda abierta para los que gusten comentar. 

**Ahora veamos referente a la información que comento en el video:**

1. En el artículo que hice sobre el ciclo 10 comenté acerca de este examen, que es importante para ver como va el cáncer [AQUÍ](https://peakd.com/hive-110372/@gerzon/my-fight-against-cancer-cycle-10-new-center-espeng).

2. El informe oncológico me indicaba Realizar Gamma grama o PET-CT Óseo. 

3. Logré realizarlo el 18-09-2025, en el Centro de Diagnóstico Docente, ubicado en Las Mercedes, Caracas, Venezuela (es uno de los pocos lugares donde hacen este examen, hace un tiempo era el único disponible en Venezuela, en la actualidad hay más opciones)

4. Muestro las distintas imágenes que se generan en este estudio, (Cuando lo realizan uno se acuesta en máquina, que te va escaneando, muy similar al de una Tomografía, e inyectan material radioactivo como en el Gamma Grama óseo).

5. Comento lo que menciona el informe generado por el CDD (Centro de Diagnóstico Docente), donde en se ven unos puntos relacionados con mi dolor actual. Pero en general salí bien sin rastro del tumor o nódulos nuevos.

6. Menciono algo extra, aunque no tiene que ver con este examen, fue algo que hice ese mismo día, invité a mi mamá a comer en el CCCT (Centro Comercial Ciudad Tamanaco). Un momento agradable para salir de la rutina médica.

----------------

Pronto espero ir recuperándome, y traer contenido más seguido. Hay muchas cosas que he querido contar. Tengo que ir a mi ritmo por los dolores actuales.

# Dios los bendiga, Hasta la próxima.

Let me start by saying that I don't condone violence or bullying.  They both suck.  I should know because I was often picked on in school and yeah, got beat up in Grade 5.  I know from experience.

However, there is another side of things.  The boy who beat me up?  Apologized later and while we were never, ever, friends I learned that there are other sides of people.

When I was picked on and teased?  Yeah, that sucked too.  Mostly that was in high school but it also sucked pretty bad.  But again, I learned things from it.

It didn't happen overnight at all.  It made me pretty insecure when I was younger but it also made me look to myself for self worth and recognition instead of needing approval from others.  It taught me to make my own \

on whether I was doing ok or not an kept me from seeking others approval and using societies guidelines for whether or not I'm successful.

Following my own path has given me a far better life than I would have had otherwise.  You said that lessons in youth form the adult.  Absolutely correct.  For many it causes irreparable damage as you said.  For others it helps them grow stronger and follow a different (hopefully better path).

As for disciplining children?  I do believe in physical punishment...but only when warranted.  Did I spank my children?  Yes.  However, there were always rules.

* I never, ever, punished my children when I was angry.
* I never punished my children for accidents, mistakes or things they didn't know about.
* I only punished my children for willful disobedience and even then only we had discussed everything calmly and the knew *why* they were receiving punishment.

I'm not perfect by any stretch.  I get mad and I remember one time when my son asked \
and I had to tell him honestly \

.

My son hated having to wait but I also refused to punish when angry.

Good article.

I agree with a lot of it but..
... there are always exceptions :)

json_metadata.title: Cycling Down the Baja - Chain Break at the Playa Calavera
json_metadata.body:
After Ensenada my next destination was the Playa Calavera. A WarmShower host, who was not there to offer me a place to stay, suggested that I could escape the noise of the busy Transpenninsular highway 1, by going down to the beach where I could also camp. Sounds great! In the town of Santo Tomas where my turn-off was, I even talked to some locals, who said the road was paved, only the last part had a difficult descent. Okay...

Well, it turned out that only the first 200 meters or so were paved. The rest? Dirt of all types and variations: hard packed clay, which was no problem to ride on. Gravel, which was more difficult. Sand, where my bike liked to slip, so I tried to avoid it. Worst of all, however, was the powdery dust, filled with large rocks. This formed a mean trap, as it looked just like the hard clay, but it made my bike slip nonetheless. All this on a steep up-and-down rollercoaster that didn't even feel like it was taking me downhill.

![WhatsApp Image 2026-05-25 at 07.07.42.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/stortebeker/241QK89dBJxqUvQq8UxDxqSZ67sATbYUHwgmKSWHD8LJtqQWpt6cwgxqPaiL5jUkL9heX.jpeg)

As much as cursed this road, amazingly I rode most of it. Until I came to the last two kilometers, which became steeper and sandier than ever. There I had no other option but to walk my bike, while keeping my brakes pulled, to keep it from taking off without me. That's how I arrived at the Playa Calavera.

![WhatsApp Image 2026-05-25 at 07.07.41 (1).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/stortebeker/243WPu9E1zrzTUUhwHunRhrQb2Ky6zQDpaNJpSWHVMs6hy79g7tmsEgaVoqjGbJPLkrnw.jpeg)

Calavera in Spanish means death skull. Not the round head-bone we carry around on our shoulders, which is called *craneo*. *Calavera* is literally the skull of the dead, as in on the pirate flag, or the Day of the Dead imagery. As for the beach, it was as beautiful as if I had died and gone to heaven. A completely secluded beach. Mom's house, where nobody would disturb my peace. 

![WhatsApp Image 2026-05-25 at 07.07.41.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/stortebeker/23wgKUyWea3ciXHfhViJW4qWZnNMywHa1Fu8t5ehrVUZomitnXbDVYPqAFdwBSTEzJzcS.jpeg)

I pitched my tent, locked my bike to a tree, with the front wheel removed, because you never know, Then I climbed down the shore and took a dip in the cold ocean to wash the thick layer of dust and sweat caked on my body. Needless to say, that night I slept like a baby.

![WhatsApp Image 2026-05-25 at 07.07.40 (2).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/stortebeker/23r1gzAi2xRnRPAzFL35HcUTeMUzXR1znJHD79ZjA6qDCGEFJd52DS4FnhuRvA8SGuLtC.jpeg)

The next day I had to get moving, precisely because that there was nothing there on that beach. I still had enough water, but not for long, so I had to get back to civilization to find some. The same road continued along the beach to the next town, about 10 km further. However, those turned out to be the longest 10 km for me.

Struggling up on one of those sandy inclines, my chain suddenly broke. It was the master link, which turned out to be the weakest link. After fiddling around with it for quite a while, I eventually fixed it, but it lost its flexibility. As a result it kept skipping, no matter which gear I rode in.

![WhatsApp Image 2026-05-25 at 07.07.40.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/stortebeker/23tSWkSSpttDFm97HK9iJhSeopXXrQbuAR1LKG4C14ieEZszYqT7nMsfittfYiw4BwwkW.jpeg)

In the end I managed to reach the next town, where I stocked up on water and fruit, along with useful intelligence: I could possible get a new chain in the town of San Vicente. There were two ways: one was a direct way of 20 km on a sandy road. - NO THANKS! The other was an asphalted road, kinda backtracking to the highway 1 also about 20 km. From there it was another 20 km to San Vicente. I gladly opted for the extra 20 km.

![WhatsApp Image 2026-05-25 at 07.07.39.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/stortebeker/23sdZF5VEv2VDjGLFiopkq4uC1oZXKEAg4zdYe6bDmBGMvn8UNMgMQWdbSR6h6S7fQuo4.jpeg)

Arriving in San Vicente I felt deadly exhausted. It was also a late afternoon on a Sunday, so there was no chance I could get a bike chain. So I booked a room at a hotel, where I was happy to take a shower and wash my clothes... once they had called the water truck, just for me, since there was no water in the whole town.

![WhatsApp Image 2026-05-25 at 07.07.39 (1).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/stortebeker/23w2ktojzbwGQGsMZWb87jTmzqBxuJoHCzhGUGAfGuB4y6SQSrooUxQqJLbsHN7u8BjDP.jpeg)

The next day I set out early morning to find a chain, got one right away, and fixed my bike. Then I allowed myself a hearty breakfast, stocked up on supplies, and by noon I was on my way to my next adventure.

json_metadata.title: Maybe Passion is back
json_metadata.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTR8hLawSeFDQFBBYXdKo3hdPEos2R4kJzC3CgYzwpNVm/img_20260527_103735.jpg)

---
Yesterday was a day to rediscover the excitement of what I do at work. As an anesthesiologist, you start out with fear and insecurities, which gradually fade as you do and learn more and more.

There comes a moment when every step of any procedure flows naturally and effortlessly, as if those skills had been implanted in your brain since birth. The same happens with surgeons and other specialties that perform special procedures.

Complications used to catch me off guard when they occurred, but with so much practice I usually anticipate them before they even show their face. Yet yesterday something happened that I couldn’t prevent. It happened simply because it had to.

But hey, no problem—I managed to resolve everything quickly and without any lasting consequences for the patient. That’s what I meant. Even though the complication couldn’t be foreseen, preparation helped me solve it without fuss and with effectiveness.

However, even if my body language didn’t give me away, my heart started beating again like when I was a young resident in training. I felt nostalgic for those moments when everything surprised me. I think this is good. I think it helps me remember that what I do is valuable, and that I shouldn’t lose motivation as much as I sometimes do, despite how much I dislike the place where I work. I’ve said this before.

I suppose that to survive here I’ll have to cling to those moments. Focus on what I enjoy. Experience should make me wiser, but at times it makes me overconfident. That’s dangerous and I should avoid it.

I don’t want complications to happen to my patients again, at least not the ones that can be avoided. I think that’s impossible. Either way, the mind and body must stay active.

---

json_metadata.title: Television Review: Ship in a Bottle (Star Trek: The Next Generation, S6X12, 1993)
json_metadata.body:
![(source:tmdb.org)](https://image.tmdb.org/t/p/original/8Nn4kvqpcIFvgJThpj1z8gdOVHC.jpg)

**Ship in a Bottle (S06E12)**

Airdate: 25 January 1993

Written by: René Echevarria
Directed by: Alexander Singer

Running Time: 46 minutes 



Among the many iconic recurring characters that populate the expansive universe of *Star Trek*, one of the most intellectually compelling and narratively unexpected is a figure who originally hailed from an entirely different literary canon. Professor James Moriarty, the archetypal archenemy of Sherlock Holmes conceived by Sir Arthur Conan Doyle almost a century prior, was ingeniously co-opted by *The Next Generation* to serve as the chief antagonist in the superlative second-season episode, [*Elementary, Dear Data*](https://hive.blog/hive-166847/@drax/television-review-haven-star-trek-the-next-generation-s2x03-1988). That instalment, a profound meditation on artificial consciousness, left its creation – a self-aware hologram of staggering intellect – in a state of suspended animation, a narrative thread tantalisingly left dangling. Four years later, the series returned to this rich vein with its direct sequel, the sixth-season episode titled *Ship in a Bottle*. This follow-up not only successfully revisits a beloved adversary but also elevates the conceptual stakes, delivering a mind-bending narrative of layered realities that stands as a testament to the show’s enduring ingenuity even in its later years.

The episode commences with a familiar scenario: Lt. Commander Data and Chief Engineer Geordi La Forge are enjoying a recreational jaunt in the holodeck, playacting another Sherlock Holmes adventure. The serene pastiche is disrupted, however, by Data’s meticulous observation of a minor anomaly—a character using his left hand instead of his right. Concluding correctly that this signifies a glitch in the simulation’s programming, they summon the often-nervous but technically brilliant Reginald Barclay to effect repairs. In a classic stroke of holodeck misfortune, Barclay’s corrective programming inadvertently reactivates the long-dormant, self-conscious hologram of Professor Moriarty. This immediate re-establishment of the character is handled with efficient grace, bypassing lengthy exposition and trusting the audience’s memory of the prior classic, which transformed a seemingly frivolous Season One trope into a profound meditation on consciousness.

Once awakened, Moriarty’s singular demand from four years prior returns with renewed urgency: he insists on the ability to leave the holodeck and exist in the physical universe. He summons Captain Picard, who arrives prepared to deliver the same painful, truthful impossibility he offered before. To Picard’s—and the viewer’s—genuine astonishment, Moriarty demonstrates that he can, indeed, step beyond the holodeck arch. Furthermore, he demands the concomitant release of his beloved, the holographic Countess Regina Bartholomew (Stephanie Beacham). When Picard hesitates, citing the profound ethical and practical ramifications, Moriarty unleashes his formidable intellect, successfully stealing the *Enterprise*’s command codes. He presents the crew with a stark ultimatum: he and the Countess will be allowed to depart the ship via a shuttlecraft, or he will destroy the *Enterprise*. This central conflict brilliantly inverts the moral dilemma of the first episode; where *Elementary, Dear Data* ended with a philosophical stalemate, “Ship in a Bottle” escalates into an active, intellectual crisis.

The narrative’s coup, however, lies in its ingenious second act twist. While attempting to resolve the seemingly intractable situation, Data arrives at a startling realisation: Moriarty has never truly left the holodeck. The Moriarty they have been interacting with, the one who seemingly walked the corridors of the *Enterprise*, is part of an elaborate ruse—a flawless simulation *within* the holodeck, crafted by the Professor to convince the crew his demands had been met. In essence, Picard, Data, and Barclay have themselves been unwitting participants in a nested simulation, a meta-conceit that plunges the episode into fascinating ontological territory. Picard, perceiving an opportunity, appears to capitulate. The crew seemingly uses the transporter to “materialise” the duo into physical form, and they are seen departing in a shuttlecraft. In a final, brilliant counter-manoeuvre, Picard then reveals his own deception: he created yet another simulation, a bespoke, persistent universe within the ship’s computer where Moriarty and the Countess can live out their dream of exploration, forever believing themselves to be free. The episode concludes not with triumphant fanfare, but with Picard’s haunting, philosophical musing to Barclay: how can they be certain *they* are not also part of someone else’s simulation? It is a question that lingers, disturbingly, in the air.

The journey to this sequel was itself a minor feat of persistence. The idea of revisiting Moriarty had percolated for years, but production was delayed by the necessity to settle copyright intricacies with the Conan Doyle estate. Once these legal hurdles were cleared, the experienced writer René Echevarria and veteran director Alexander Singer collaborated to craft an episode that is, first and foremost, a worthy successor. It avoids the pitfall of mere repetition; instead of rehashing the “holodeck being demands freedom” plot, it complexifies it, exploring the dizzying concept of multi-level realities. This thematic preoccupation with nested simulations would later become a central motif in science fiction cinema, explored in films like [*The Thirteenth Floor*](https://peakd.com/hive-166847/@drax/film-review-the-thirteenth-floor)—a 1999 film which deals with the themes of reality, consciousness and identity through a virtual reality construct—and Christopher Nolan’s architecturally complex [*Inception*](https://peakd.com/film/@drax/capsule-film-review-the-inception-2010), noted for its *[Matrix](https://peakd.com/film/@drax/retro-film-review-the-matrix-1999)*-like concepts of dream-within-a-dream layers. “Ship in a Bottle” operates as a sophisticated television precursor to these cinematic explorations.

The episode’s success is heavily anchored by Daniel Davis’s reprisal of the role of Moriarty. Davis plays the part with undiminished gusto, blending aristocratic menace with a profound, relatable pathos. This Moriarty is nominally the villain, yet his motivations are intensely human: a desperate yearning to breach the limits of his programmed existence and a shared passion with Picard for the exploration of the unknown. The script wisely affords him a form of happy ending, granting him his heart’s desire within the confines of a specially crafted simulation, a resolution that feels both ethically nuanced and emotionally satisfying. Stephanie Beacham is suitably elegant as the Countess, though her role is inherently more passive and less memorable than Davis’s tour de force or Dwight Schultz’s wonderfully anxious and endearing turn as the perpetually flustered Reginald Barclay, here making another of his recurring appearances that add texture to the *Enterprise* crew.

Director Alexander Singer’s work is exemplary, particularly in his meticulous attention to detail. Small, easily missed clues—such as Counselor Troi inexplicably wearing an older-style uniform—are subtly seeded throughout the early scenes, retrospectively revealing themselves as tell-tale signs that the “reality” the characters inhabit is itself a fabrication. This directorial care enhances the conceptual puzzle, rewarding attentive viewers and reinforcing the episode’s core theme of perceptual uncertainty.

Beyond its immediate narrative pleasures, *Ship in a Bottle* holds significant legacy value within the *Star Trek* franchise. The character of Moriarty as a sentient, rights-claiming hologram established a powerful precedent. It directly paved the narrative and philosophical way for the Emergency Medical Hologram (The Doctor) in *Star Trek: Voyager*, whose journey towards personhood became a series-long arc, and for the self-aware holographic crooner Vic Fontaine in *Deep Space Nine*. Moriarty was the proof of concept that holographic life could be more than mere scenery.

In the end, “Ship in a Bottle” is a compelling demonstration that *Star Trek: The Next Generation* was far from exhausting its creative vitality as it entered its penultimate season. Against the odds of a potentially gimmicky sequel premise, it delivered a surprisingly sophisticated, intellectually rigorous, and emotionally resonant piece of television. By weaving together a taut thriller plot with deep philosophical questions about reality and consciousness, the episode secured its place not merely as a worthy follow-up to a classic, but as a classic in its own right—a clever, bottle-shaped confection that remains one of the series’ most ingeniously constructed puzzles.



RATING: 8/10 (+++)

json_metadata.title: Man United getting started early.
json_metadata.body:
Man United seem to be wasting no time now that Carrick is signed up to be manager.

In stark contrast to what we’ve become used to in recent years, United are actually moving early and with a bit of purpose in the transfer market. They’re reportedly on the verge of signing Ederson just one week after the season has ended, which feels very un-United in the best possible way. Normally this is the point where the club drags its feet, misses out on its first-choice targets, then scrambles late in the window and overpays for plan B or plan C.


![](https://images.hive.blog/DQmNTVfUnnLa8k9b64FNdRW8kyY6iS12pRtpH9HNizY9ZuG/image.webp)
[Ref: Sky Sports](https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11667/13547526/manchester-united-transfer-news-ederson-close-to-agreeing-move-from-atalanta)

This is the complete opposite of the usual slow, hesitant approach we’ve seen before, where the club waits too long, gets boxed in, and ends up panic buying players for way above the odds. When you move early, you at least give yourself a chance to get the right player at the right price, instead of making desperate decisions when everyone knows you’re short on time.

I will say that Amorim bought well last year and seemed to get the players that he actually wanted instead of Fellani, Sanchez, Antony, Van de Beek.... to name a few. 

That matters more than people think. When a manager is backed properly, you usually see clearer recruitment, better squad balance, and fewer signings that feel like a compromise or a commercial gamble. United have gone through far too many years of bringing in names instead of fitting pieces.

Hopefully the deal goes through as Ederson seems like a solid replacemnet for Casemiro but younger and more mobile. That alone makes the move appealing. Casemiro has still had his moments, but the team needs legs in midfield, someone who can cover ground, recover possession, and handle the physical side of the Premier League without looking stuck in second gear. If Ederson can bring that energy while still being reliable on the ball, then it could be a very smart piece of business.

body.title: Elaborando y degustando deliciosa bebida de: Piña con leche condensada.(Esp/Eng)
body.body:
# Español

# Saludos amigos amantes de las ricas y saludables bebidas.💁☀️

¡Feliz día para todos!

Hoy, amigos, fui de compras al mercado, y mis ojos resplandecieron como luceros, al observar que se encontraban en ventas piñas maduras, este fruto rico en vitamina C y otros nutrientes, que me resultan agradable incorporar a mi organismo con su consumo natural. Inmediatamente, compré una unidad mediana, y me dirigí a mi hogar, dónde me puse manos a la obra y elaboré una deliciosa bebida refrescante con la piña, de ingrediente principal. Los invito amigos a conocer la espectacular receta de: Piña con leche condensada.¡Comencemos!

#
<center>
![GridArt_20260526_155202796.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marydeluz/23viEYigZ71fxK5xXZjJuAUtqLCx1yu2iMj9EYosPVKARKyYaY64uGPrgaTMdEMZnVMJC.jpg)
</center>
#

# ✨Piña con leche condensada✨

# ✨Ingredientes para dos comensales
#
<center>
![GridArt_20260526_151940050.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marydeluz/23xpD4isKZzVwGpsekFC5e2jfg4eZVvPzkqyPgbn611ueZNhbabXT46fQUHUmK3PhQgRb.jpg)
</center>
#
.Piña madura: 1/2 de una unidad entera.
.Leche condensada: 1/2 del contenido de una lata de 390g.
.Agua fría: 1/2 litro.

# ✨Modo de confección✨
#
<center>
![GridArt_20260526_152217492.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marydeluz/23wX9hjCGhwRJ3RG7pVW5Yg8pWf7Lj1uJVm9Xi6VNrv5wsSGMT8FZ5Wcr9UhGvhoDGVkr.jpg)
</center>
#
Inicié el proceder lavando con abundante agua la piña entera, que se encontraba sin sus piñones .Seguidamente, con ayuda de un cuchillo fui despojándola de toda su cáscara externa, que poseía relieves contínuos con forma de rombos. Una vez que obtuve pelada la piña, la corté centralmente, pues sólo emplearía media, y continué el proceder realizándoles cortes a esta porción, que me permitieron obtener cuadraditos medianos, desprovistos de su duro eje central.

Ya teniendo la piña a emplear lista, la resguardé unos instantes, mientras me dispuse abrir la lata de leche condensada, con ayuda de un cuchillo de mesa y machacador, pues mi abridor de latas, lamentablemente se rompió dejándome a medias del proceso.Pero bueno, amigos, logré la apertura de la lata exitosamente.

Con la leche condensada y la piña lista, comencé la confección de la bebida de la siguiente forma:
#
<center>
![GridArt_20260526_153417345.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marydeluz/23uFgNDzV66b75vNCLnNBvLvQ21P65PFogfhQn5PnpPt59pd5DJA2sKoY4yDmkEHzBR1a.jpg)
</center>
#
Tomé el vaso de mi batidora e incorporé en él: los trocitos de piña, la 1/2 lata de leche, y 1/2 litro de agua fría.Tapé el vaso, conecté mi batidora, y la puse a batir en velocidad 2 , por 4 minutos.
#
<center>
![GridArt_20260526_154049208.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marydeluz/23uR5GYbsXoA38xyqpTVtheNhZxBj6sDxrSqiQirUkMSC9myoJxW5fLFeZS8Nxwret1iu.jpg)
</center>
#
Transcurrido el tiempo , destapé el vaso y un aroma delicioso dulce, a helado de piña, impregnó la cocina, un aroma que me motivó a servir gustosamente en vasos, donde le agregué un toque más de leche condensada.
#
<center>
![GridArt_20260526_154201883.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marydeluz/23xVZuLvHENHoKBz7eVq5fgHLX4WxsATtNCjRGfvRetaAdyY1sehNpUPasZBzcapDqmja.jpg)
</center>
#
Divina en sabor esta bebida, a la que también pueden agregarle el paso extra de colado, en caso de que deseen la textura más suave. En lo particular, yo prefiero hasta el paso de batido, pues me encantan los grumitos de piña que resaltan en la bebida.Ambas terminaciones amigos, créanme, le harán refrescar y deleitar el paladar.

Me despido, esperando que les haya gustado y motivado la bebida frutal compartida, a su pronta degustación en familia.Les deseo vibras positivas, y una excelente semana laboral.¡Abrazos!

Fotografías propias.

*** 
*** 
# English
# Making and tasting delicious drink of: Pineapple with condensed milk.

# Greetings friends lovers of rich and healthy drinks.💁☀️

Happy day to everyone!

Today, friends, I went shopping at the market, and my eyes shone like stars, when I noticed that ripe pineapples were on sale, this fruit rich in vitamin C and other nutrients, which I find pleasant to incorporate into my body with its natural consumption. Immediately, I bought a medium unit, and headed home, where I got down to work and made a delicious refreshing drink with pineapple, the main ingredient. I invite you friends to know the spectacular recipe of: Pineapple with condensed milk.Let's get started!
#
<center>
![GridArt_20260526_155202796.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marydeluz/23viEYigZ71fxK5xXZjJuAUtqLCx1yu2iMj9EYosPVKARKyYaY64uGPrgaTMdEMZnVMJC.jpg)
</center>
#
# ✨Pineapple with condensed milk✨

# ✨Ingredients for two diners

#
<center>
![GridArt_20260526_151940050.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marydeluz/23xpD4isKZzVwGpsekFC5e2jfg4eZVvPzkqyPgbn611ueZNhbabXT46fQUHUmK3PhQgRb.jpg)
</center>
#
.Ripe pineapple: 1/2 of a whole unit.
.Condensed milk: 1/2 of the contents of a 390g can.
.Cold water: 1/2 liter.


# ✨Mode of preparation✨
#
<center>
![GridArt_20260526_152217492.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marydeluz/23wX9hjCGhwRJ3RG7pVW5Yg8pWf7Lj1uJVm9Xi6VNrv5wsSGMT8FZ5Wcr9UhGvhoDGVkr.jpg)
</center>
#

I started the procedure by washing the whole pineapple, which was without its pine nuts, with plenty of water.Then, with the help of a knife, I stripped it of all its external shell, which had continuous diamond-shaped reliefs. Once I got the pineapple peeled, I cut it centrally, because I would only use half, and I continued the procedure by making cuts to this portion, which allowed me to obtain medium squares, devoid of its hard central axis.

Already having the pineapple to use ready, I protected it for a few moments, while I got ready to open the can of condensed milk, with the help of a table knife and crusher, because my can opener, unfortunately broke leaving me halfway through the process.But well, friends, I managed to open the can successfully.

With the condensed milk and pineapple ready, I started the preparation of the drink as follows:
#
<center>
![GridArt_20260526_153417345.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marydeluz/23uFgNDzV66b75vNCLnNBvLvQ21P65PFogfhQn5PnpPt59pd5DJA2sKoY4yDmkEHzBR1a.jpg)
</center>
#
I took the glass of my mixer and incorporated in it: the pineapple pieces, the 1/2 can of milk, and 1/2 liter of cold water.I covered the glass, connected my mixer, and set it to beat on speed 2, for 4 minutes.
#
<center>
![GridArt_20260526_154049208.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marydeluz/23uR5GYbsXoA38xyqpTVtheNhZxBj6sDxrSqiQirUkMSC9myoJxW5fLFeZS8Nxwret1iu.jpg)
</center>
#
After a while, I opened the glass and a delicious sweet aroma, of pineapple ice cream, permeated the kitchen, an aroma that motivated me to gladly serve in glasses, where I added a touch more of condensed milk.
#
<center>
![GridArt_20260526_154201883.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marydeluz/23xVZuLvHENHoKBz7eVq5fgHLX4WxsATtNCjRGfvRetaAdyY1sehNpUPasZBzcapDqmja.jpg)
</center>
#
Divine in flavor this drink, to which you can also add the extra step of straining, in case you want the smoothest texture. In particular, I prefer even the smoothie step, because I love the pineapple lumps that stand out in the drink.Both endings, friends, believe me, will refresh and delight the palate.

I say goodbye, hoping that you liked and motivated the shared fruit drink, to its prompt tasting as a family.I wish you positive vibes, and an excellent working week.Hugs!

Own photographs.
