body.title: My First Cross-Country Drive in a Tesla (Part 2)
body.body:
<center> 
https://media2.giphy.com/media/v1.Y2lkPTc5MGI3NjExbWY1cDl5M3BhOWRhMWt6aXI0a2FvdTJvczAxZ25iazZhMGhmbTg4NSZlcD12MV9pbnRlcm5hbF9naWZfYnlfaWQmY3Q9Zw/d3fl6aZoceQ1V0Jtqc/giphy.gif
</center>

Our second day’s drive on our trip from Minnesota to Sedona, AZ was from Grand Island, Nebraska to Trinidad, Colorado. It was the most brutal travel day of the trip by far. We traveled for over ten hours, rode a total of 557 miles, and stopped three times along our route. 

<center> 
![1.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ericvancewalton/243M75a9Cc6Jir2g73oCvHaKcNp98ysrmxqYrZLZR77erh8UgrRuSTMTaB4oUSi9Wuwzp.jpg)
</center>

About three quarters of the way through the drive we encountered some pretty bad storms and a few [dust devils](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dust_devil). We’ve learned from previous trips through the middle of the U.S. that the weather is usually unpredictable and can be severe. 

<center> 
![2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ericvancewalton/242DNyk7aD7fBjXodGXLtFN7dRjEPqyFMP6rsUwrnua6TrcyMQ3CiTSgvpb6C4cEzek32.jpg)
</center>

Full Self Driving handled the heavy rain and wind with ease. However, it was on this leg of the drive that some of the flaws of FSD (v14.2.2.5) revealed themselves. The car violently swerved more than once to avoid tire tracks and dark asphalt patches on the highway. Although the car never left the lane and didn’t put us in danger it was still pretty unnerving. 

<center> 
![3.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ericvancewalton/Epzz9eCcJEaNiXtdz7dD12pPgg3k5X1gyvHAUGkiTxAmc8F4FM8R6xw817MifQ7Kovh.jpg)
</center>

I’m sure this flaw will be fixed in future FSD updates but the system needs to do better at differentiating between real and perceived hazards. As a believer in the technology I think it’s important these kinks are worked out quickly or else the general public will be more hesitant to trust it. 

<center> 
![4.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ericvancewalton/Eoke3fuasThjq8rAEZkohvWrziEA4dLVyGyPMbjyrHWD6DBneXP3cCNgpYdSEiM1Kcb.jpg)
</center>

<center> 
![5.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ericvancewalton/EoiW825DxGzi59orAhzSJTuEoKbcxmLZpZaoTPBnYa1sZMWpAPKpGefTLDJNTavNZx6.jpg)
</center>

The car also pulled into the wrong entrance at one of our Supercharging stops. The parking lot was adjacent to the chargers but wasn’t connected. This seemed like more of an error in navigation data than a problem with the Full Self Driving itself. Again, not a huge deal but somewhat of a disappointment when the tech handles a majority of driving tasks so well. 

We rolled into Trinidad, CO in the early evening and stayed at a very unique little hotel called [The Well Hotel & Taproom](https://wellhoteltrinidad.com/). Situated in historical downtown Trinidad, The Well had ample parking, decent food, and good beer. They also had karaoke, which was pretty amusing. Thankfully the singing ceased at 10pm. 

The building was built in the 1880s and the owner said it was originally a general store and residence hotel. The hotel rooms themselves still had some of the original 1800’s charm but had been updated with all the modern conveniences. If only those walls could talk I bet they’d have some interesting stories to tell. We even found the town's oldest skating rink on the same street as the hotel. 

<center> 
![6.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ericvancewalton/23vi5t54FEcR5EiJhuecLAjRweSSj2HNQtDmzbVo3PqcjKj7wEr5VXvYWcKt7KAaPSj66.jpg)
</center>
<center> 
![7.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ericvancewalton/23ynYemChCDvvUNWBqErb5q5n8Yn757fyBfkYze6jBnpBfhmQhibvFLgHf5nNkkgHUqxc.jpg)
</center>
<center> 
![8.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ericvancewalton/245cRkusc7rNUFXhnarBZEjWDyGoJUXqgzvBnm762cCWk6A9pa9eQqThGP67krzmfQEs2.jpg)
</center>
<center> 
![9.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ericvancewalton/242DNPA3zJ66vYanrHvTeCsYYkKZawnPZyehxPG4Can1KkoM3XabugBSEWtXc3aTkzwM1.jpg)
</center>




## Charging Costs ##
<center> 
![Charging.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ericvancewalton/23swkTYoaS6RGVHksJxyuNsQspUoUBVfr15fww8t3j4wzaRfo4Rteaedry17zTH169qyr.jpeg)
</center>

The 6 Tesla EV charging stops this day added up to:

$4.64 + $4.78 + $7.34 + $7.66 + $12.98 + $17.96 = $55.36

The last and most expensive charging session was topping off the battery in preparation for the next day's drive. So we the charging costs for the day's drive was truly only $37.40. 

For comparison, an ICE vehicle getting an average of 40mpgs would have cost us roughly $66.86. 

We saved $29.46 in the Tesla Model Y Premium AWD on this day over a gasoline powered car. 


# Drive Time ##

The trip would have only taken around 8hrs in a tradition vehicle plus stops for restrooms and food. 

In the Tesla it took 9hrs, 15mins. Additional stops (which we would have had to do in the Forester too) and charging a little extra made it more like a 10hr, 20min day of driving. 

Again, gasoline wins on drive-time here. The Tesla took about an hour and fifteen minutes longer. 


## Final Thoughts ##

Again, I was less fatigued at the end of the day using FSD than I otherwise would have been if I was driving. It was a much more enjoyable experience being able to take in the sights. I'm learning the little bit of extra drive time doesn't bother me much. Being less stressed and fatigued at the end of each day is a decent trade off for an extra hour of drive time. 

The critical FSD disengagements due to tire marks and asphalt patches were concerning. I know Tesla is trying to get the cars to avoid hazards like potholes and debris on the road but it needs to be fine-tuned. 


*Stayed tuned for Day 3 of the journey, coming soon!*

## If you have any questions about road tripping in an EV please drop them in the comments below ##

*Also, if you're considering seeing what the Tesla experience is like for yourself please consider using [my referral code](https://ts.la/eric17162) for three months of Full Self Driving for free (a $300 value).* 









All for now. Thanks so much for reading. 



---

Greetings, dear friends of this community, which allows us to discover more places in our world every week.

This time, I’d like to show you some of the streets and avenues that lead to a small chapel called “Santa Teresita del Niño Jesús,” located right next to a beautiful square called José Angel Álamo—or “Chess Square,” as we call it.

![portada.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gpache/23wWrUzWEHedbeGuvUHTaXHGN44nQVuCWFtawCkCxcxxdgScwgLL7YEvq1tvuyGtBuyqM.jpg)

I stopped by this chapel since I was nearby to pay my respects to the Blessed Sacrament. The first time I entered this church was when I attended a friend’s wedding several years ago.

![6.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gpache/242YCCw1EVBHL3Gc2ZrKXbSvo6v8GiZfRKYdrQPyR9ATkgCZSA8BoZPYUNaKtL7BuiuUF.jpg)

body.title: Day 2872 | 35-Hour Travel To Destination
body.body:
https://images.hive.blog/DQmdQD8zgW729eQXkSou5TR8bTkSayEUjN3Kd97xGbrF3T3/Screenshot%202026-05-27%2018.11.24.png
I started a challenge of taking 100 days off to mainly focus on my health and overall personal development and used this account as a personal blog to keep track of all my activity. I enjoyed it and continued afterward trying to build better habits and find a good balance between health, fitness, work, entertainment, and my personal life...

Tuesday was the day where I left on my first big solo trip with a very long travel ahead. It started with a drive the the Brussels Airpor arriving there a bit more than 3 hours before my flight. There was quite a traffic jam so it was a 2-hour drive and we left earlt enough just to be safe.

It has been ages since I took a plane and never done so alone and main feeling I had is \

It's one thing to think about traveling and being up for it the moment you book a ticket, and another thing when the time to leave is actually there. At least for me as someone who likes to stay in his comfort bubble.

The first flight was a big one around 10-hours to Beijjing also in a big plane and I got a window seat with a very kind old Chinese Lady Sitting next to me (Miss Meng) who I talked quite a lot to. Initially I thought that's a bit broken english just assuming that all Chinese people speak it fluently until the point she asked me what I thought she did after she revealed she was a English Teacher. That's one of the reasons she enjoyed chatting so much and we got along very well. I also learned that almost no Chinese people speak proper english. Anyway, that flight was an absolute joy and the hours really went by super quickly as aside from the chatting there were many distractions. There were 2 hot meals which weren't that bad. The 1st Meal was noodles with Mushrooms, some dry salad, a piece of bread with butter, and a rice cake dessert The 2nd Meal was some rice with fish, along with cucumber andtomato, again Bread with butter and a small Mattentaartje which is one of the Belgian classics

I also listened to a 2.5-hour Pocast at times falling asleep. The Soundcore Space One for just 65€ really did a superb job at the noise cancelling and was a real bargain. And I started watching the Documentary 'Should I Marry A Murderer' which I nearly finished as it's only 3 episodes. Once I arrived in Beijing, it was initially a bit of a search where I needed to go but I had 9 hours so no rush or stress and I quickly got myself to the hall where all the shops and restaurants were waiting for my plane to Bangkok. I did first do some steps, try to get EURO exchanged for Thai Baht which wasn't allowed, and managed to lay myself down on the waiting seats for what never really was a nap but I did manage to get rest. I also ate some of the crackers I brought, got some free water multiple times and avoided spending any money at the airport. I also changed clothes to keep everything fresh, and finished watching the series on ly laptop. The 9 hours also here flew by pretty quickly and I boarded my 2nd plane which was a much smaller one again with a window seat in the back but with nobody aside me which left me a bit more room. Also here the time flew by with a meal which this time was Rice with Chicken, cueumber, bread, and some Mango which I all ate. I again put on a podcast to past the time and needed to use the toilet but the line was always too long which kept me busy trying to find the good moment until I just could not hold it anymore. The plane landed and I was in bangkok. The first thing I did was to try to get my esim to work but apparently it connected first to my regular data plan which was followed by a message of a 60€ bill which is just a disgrace from Telenet and I will try to make it so that that wave that off. I did eventually get the esim right and continued to head to immigration which went smoothly, when I walked to the place where I needed to get my luggage, it was just in front of me and I was off to meet the taxi I ordered to Hua Hin. The sign with my name on was there and a guy guided me to the place where a rather young driver came pick me up. He didn't speak any engligh which I didn't mind during the 3-Hour+ Taxi Drive which cost 2000 Baht (under 60€). It was quite crazy how some people drive their motorbike with kids and no helmets at high speeds on the motorway. Overall The city itself wasn't that crazy different from what it's like in Belgium. I managed to get to my Hotel in time which is actually super nice for the 20$ a night price, had a quick call with my mom just to say I arrived. I took a quick shower and am now laying in bed to finally get some sleep even though I also am not super tired as some might assume. It was a long travel but nothing went wrong and it all felt a lot shorter than I imagined.
Next Day Goals: Even though I'm quite relaxed, I'm still in a mindset where I don't really want to be here even though I'm quite sure that will change sooner than later. Tomorrow, I will go on a hunt to find a condo to stay at the next 50+ days, I will convert some Euro to Baht, get some basic supplies and see where it takes me.

body.title: Das Aus für die Urban Tech Republic wäre ein kapitaler Fehler Warum Tegel über Berlins Zukunft entscheidet - Tagesspiegel
body.body:
## Warum das Ende der Urban Tech Republic ein strategischer Fehltritt wäre  

### Einleitung: Mehr als ein Startup‑Scheitern  
Die jüngste Ankündigung, die Urban Tech Republic (UTR) aus dem Berliner Innovations‑Ökosystem zu entfernen, hat in der lokalen Wirtschaftspolitik für Aufsehen gesorgt. Auf den ersten Blick mag es sich um einen simplen Fall von fehlgeschlagenem Unternehmertum handeln – ein weiteres Beispiel dafür, dass nicht jede Gründeridee die nötige Skalierbarkeit erreicht. Doch ein genauerer Blick enthüllt tiefere Implikationen: Der mögliche Verlust einer Schlüsselplattform, die nicht nur Start‑ups, sondern auch die digitale Infrastruktur von Berlin – und damit den Grundstein für die nächste Generation von Hive‑basierten Projekten – gefährdet.

### Der Standort Tegel: Eine vernachlässigte Ressource  
Tegel ist seit Jahren ein unterschätztes Asset im Berliner Wirtschafts‑Geschehen. Während das Regierungsviertel und die Medieninsel rund um den Alexanderplatz die mediale Aufmerksamkeit erhalten, bietet das ehemalige Flughafenareal ein weitläufiges, preiswertes und technisch gut erschlossenes Terrain. Für die UTR war Tegel nicht nur ein Standort, sondern ein **Ökosystem‑Knotenpunkt**: Hier konnten Unternehmen Prototypen testen, gemeinsam Labore betreiben und in einer offenen Kulisse die notwendige Infrastruktur für IoT‑ und KI‑Lösungen aufbauen.

Die Entscheidung, diesen Standort zu schließen, bedeutet mehr als den Verlust von Büroflächen. Sie würde einen bereits funktionierenden Knotenpunkt für **Dezentralisierung** und **Community‑Building** aus dem Netz reißen – beides Grundpfeiler der Hive‑Philosophie, die auf verteilte Datenspeicherung und kollektive Entscheidungsfindung setzt.

### Wirtschaftliche Konsequenzen für Berlin  
#### 1. Schwächung des Innovationsclusters  
Die Urban Tech Republic hat in den vergangenen fünf Jahren rund 80 Start‑ups, über 150 Projekte und zahlreiche Forschungskooperationen unterstützt. Durch die Schließung wird das **Netzwerk‑Energie‑Niveau** Berlin drastisch sinken. Der Verlust von Know‑how‑Transfer, Mentoring‑Programmen und Investorenkontakten kann das gesamte Innovationsklima erstarren lassen – ein Szenario, das Berlin langfristig in der Konkurrenz zu anderen europäischen Tech‑Hubs benachteiligen würde.

#### 2. Verlust von Fachkräften und Kapital  
Berliner Talente sind mobil; ein bedeutender Teil der derzeitigen UTR‑Mitarbeiter arbeitet bereits an Projekten, die auf **Hive‑basierte Token‑Economics** setzen. Das Fehlen einer lokalen Anlaufstelle zwingt diese Fachkräfte, nach alternativen Standorten zu suchen – und damit auch das Kapital, das sie mitbringen. Es entsteht ein Teufelskreis: weniger Fachwissen, weniger Investitionen, noch weniger Innovation.

#### 3. Gefahr von „Brain‑Drain“ nach Ost‑Europa  
Die Region Ost‑Europas investiert massiv in dezentrale Technologien und bietet vergleichbare Standortvorteile. Ohne eine starke, zentrale Anlaufstelle wie die UTR werden Berliner Gründer und Investoren zunehmend nach Prag, Warschau oder Bukarest abwandern – ein klarer Wettbewerbsnachteil für die Hauptstadt.

### Hive‑Community: Ein potenzieller Rettungsanker  
Die Hive‑Plattform bietet nicht nur ein dezentrales Social‑Media‑Ökosystem, sondern auch ein robustes **Governance‑Framework**, das für die Koordination gemeinsamer Projekte geeignet ist. Wenn die Hügel‑Community das Bewusstsein für die strategische Bedeutung von Tegel schärft, kann sie folgende Schritte initiieren:

| Maßnahme | Nutzen für Berlin | Umsetzung |
|----------|-------------------|-----------|
| **Dezentrale Finanzierung (DAOs)** | Ersetzt klassische Fördergelder durch Community‑Funding. | Gründung einer „Tegel‑Future‑DAO“, die mittels HIVE‑Tokens Mikro‑Investitionen sammelt. |
| **Open‑Source‑Labore** | Erhalt von Test‑ und Entwicklungsumgebungen ohne hohe Mietkosten. | Nutzung von Hive‑Bounties, um Entwickler zu motivieren, offene Lösungen für IoT‑ und Smart‑City‑Probleme zu erstellen. |
| **Stakeholder‑Governance** | Einbindung von Stadtverwaltung, Unternehmen und Bürgern in Entscheidungsprozesse. | Implementierung von Hive‑Voting‑Mechanismen für Standortentscheidungen. |

Durch diese Ansätze könnten die fehlenden öffentlichen Mittel zumindest teilweise kompensiert und die **Selbstbestimmung** der Berliner Tech‑Community gestärkt werden.

### Politische Implikationen: Wer entscheidet über Tegel?  
Die Entscheidung, Tegel zu schließen, liegt nicht allein bei der Stadtverwaltung, sondern ist das Ergebnis eines komplexen Zusammenspiels aus **Stadtplanung, Immobilienwirtschaft und föderalen Förderprogrammen**. Der Tagesspiegel betont, dass die Stadt Berlin die Kontrolle über das Areal behält, jedoch fehlt es bislang an einer klaren, langfristigen Vision, die die **digitale Infrastruktur** als Kernkompetenz priorisiert.

Ein möglicher Wendepunkt wäre die Etablierung eines **pluralistischen Governance‑Modells**, das die Stimmen von Start‑ups, Investoren und der Hive‑Community gleichwertig berücksichtigt. Ein solches Modell könnte über ein Hive‑basiertes Token‑Voting realisiert werden, das Transparenz schafft und gleichzeitig die kollektive Intelligenz nutzt, um die besten Nutzungsmöglichkeiten für Tegel zu ermitteln.

### Fazit: Die Chance, Berlin neu zu definieren  
Das scheinbare „Aus“ der Urban Tech Republic ist kein unvermeidliches Schicksal, sondern ein kritischer Punkt, an dem die Stadt entscheiden kann, ob sie **verloren gehen** oder **neue Wege beschreiten** will. Durch die Integration dezentraler Finanzierungs- und Governance‑Mechanismen, unterstützt von der Hive‑Community, lässt sich nicht nur das Innovationspotential von Tegel retten, sondern auch ein **nachhaltiges, inklusives Ökosystem** schaffen, das Berlin langfristig als führende Smart‑City‑Region Europas positioniert.

> **Schlüsselgedanke:** Wenn Berlin die Chance nutzt, Tegel mit dezentralen, community‑getriebenen Instrumenten zu revitalisieren, kann die Stadt nicht nur den Verlust der Urban Tech Republic abwenden, sondern zugleich ein **Leuchtturm‑Modell** für digitale Stadtentwicklung etablieren – ein Gewinn für die gesamte Hive‑Community und für die Zukunft der europäischen Technologielandschaft.

body.title: EID AL ADHA 2025 TABASKI, A CELEBRATION OF FAITH, PEACE AND SHARING
body.body:
O Allah, Lord of all worlds,
On this blessed day where the knife honors Your word, Receive our prayers, our hearts and our souls
As Ibrahim offered what was most precious to him.
Answer the wishes of every Muslim around the world,

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbdhgdFsemfsVQU2aqp8bQ6X9BePo2jVF1pSrMBK2e3bm/1779900048713.jpg)

From Cotonou to Mecca, from Dakar to Jakarta,
Grant them the peace that calms the wars within,
The health that allows rising each morning with gratitude,The prosperity that feeds families and opens closed doors.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbtzvPPCD8dQv4oZxK2qdg1z5cqcF84hnAuiVacsu8Nz7/1779900056574.jpg)

May Your blessings fall like gentle rain
Upon every home, every household, every heart that seeks You.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTkVfXAQGzx7C3wKmNgm7WACPPGePdix4dmwrcZ1MAa7K/1779900068310.jpg)

Today I lived Tabaski in its most beautiful and sincere expression the spirit of sharing. Quietly at home as the afternoon sun began its descent, at exactly 4:00 PM, a first messenger knocked at my door. He carried a generous bowl filled with approximately 2.5 kg of fresh ram meat beautiful, deep red boneless cuts, firm and abundant, held proudly in both hands as if delivering a treasure.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPaSsiyBSwe1BRVSuRnoprjVnedEcNgPXvzxh9tU1DwYS/1779900076280.jpg)

 The warm golden light of the afternoon sun fell across the wooden table, making the offering glow like something sacred. Pure muscle, pure generosity, pure Tabaski.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTWbtfCbjZkXXbpEsz9eDGJ5GRNE57ygWB4tzxY4k5upF/1779900085022.jpg)

Then at 4:20 PM, just twenty minutes later, came a second knock. This time, another approximately 1 kg portion arrived meat with bone, a rich mix of cuts with fat, marrow and sinew all together the kind of piece that promises a deep, slow-cooked broth full of flavour. 

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVnvTcdxdyti9Ebbx4p3Xby6dAMxFZKTJUmsGPHCZDNPL/1779900094442.jpg)

Laid out in a steel basin, it told its own story of sacrifice and abundance.Two visits. Two bowls. Two acts of love from neighbors and brothers who remembered me on this holy day. 

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRiXVBkuaZrsSKNpxHWGJC98aZnoe4mTf8KzokwmH7ViP/1779900107325.jpg)

This is the true soul of Eid not just the prayer at dawn, not just the sacrifice of the ram, but this quiet afternoon moment when someone sends a piece of their blessing to your door.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmY4PxcN6kjd5RrCQ6YWBgNK87Lmcse6Ywq9EuzyEp9VhN/1779900115566.jpg)

To all my Muslim brothers and sisters in Benin and around the world: Happy Eid Al Adha May your prayers be answered, your families be protected and your blessings overflow.

> *It's a bit of a tricky topic... Being a parent and also a son, I have lived through most of the things you described... On the other side, I know that I never hit my own child, but unfortunately, I did raise my voice a few times in his teenage years...

body.title: Life At All Cost
body.body:
Greetings, everyone!

Many people tend to have their own ambition or the desire to become a medical doctor, own a hospital to treat patients, and do all they can to save lives that are at risk. But their oath to save lives has been thwarted, and the doctors turn out to be liars and devils or have bad intentions towards the patients who came to be saved by them.


![1000738158.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/peckypeace/23zS5PyPVqPbvL4uZwcYUuuR53KpRBqynS2ZxL3EqUzGD9QXGvUT8BWnhuT9so3EX8ua1.png)


However, instead of help being offered first, money becomes the priority of the day before medical attention is given which is not proper. Some illnesses require medical attention; if not, the patient will die on the spot. The hospital that was built to save lives turns to MoniePoint, or the business center. Not knowing that people's life is not like goods sold at the market. 

Some are not worthy to be trusted, and they have been trained to kill, steal, and destroy the lives of the patients who need help from them. Some nurses are very wicked, with no compassion or mercy for others.

There was a day they rushed a patient to the hospital under emergency, who needed medical attention to be given, and one of the nurses sat comfortably watching the patient in without human sympathy. There was a shout from the nurse, saying, \

still sitting down, watching how this man would die. That was my first time in the hospital, and I was perplexed by her actions. I unconsciously kept my mouth open because of her actions towards this patient, who was rushed in to seek help from doctors or nurses, but to no avail. If I were the government or the manager, I would have said to sack the nurse from the hospital that very day. 

I wept for that patient, my heart reached out with mercy and compassion with tears rolling down my cheeks. Unfortunately, the man died there in the hospital without medical attention or any help from the doctors. Even when they were trying to deposit the bills they had requested. 

My issue is that, why money first, why not try to save the lifeless that were brought to receive life first while trying to make the payment. I felt so bad and discouraged when nurses or doctors behaved this way. Meaning they can deliberately kill a patient through injection or negligence.

If this continues, let us not have doctors and nurses and hospitals again in this world. 

The hearts of the nurses and doctors are desperately wicked.

-**This is my response to the Hivelearners featured contest week 219 episode 2**-

_**I love, I care and I forgive**_

body.title: A's drop another game vs Mariners | Big series finale today as A's look to maintain first place in AL West
body.body:
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXAZV4uKdvipr2SETWhmTNs8j3j5bT2HWzmq4hgxvyDFi/1776541685498.png)
[Src](https://www.stickpng.com/img/sports/baseball/major-league-baseball-mlb/oakland-athletics/oakland-athletics-a-logo)

Ah, yikes well, the A's have struggled against the Mariners in this series and it's been a bummer for sure. 

Gage Jump's MLB debut went reasonably decent yesterday I'd say. Nothing outstanding but considering it was his debut I was pretty impressed for the most part. After a slightly rocky second inning where Jump allowed three runs, he settled down pretty nicely. In the end he actually managed to get through five innings, allowing four runs in total. He seems pretty confident on the mound and has a pretty smooth throwing motion. 

But the A's were completely shutdown yesterday offensively. I'm normally pretty confident in the A's offensive power, but lately it seems they've fallen asleep a bit. The A's only totaled four hits yesterday and were nearly shutout until the bottom of the ninth when Tyler Soderstrom hit a solo shot, his 6th of the season. To make matters more depressing, Nick Kurtz failed to extend his 48-game on-base streak! He was on the verge of breaking the A's single season record had he reached base one more time! Nuts! Oh well, that's life sometimes. Kurtz still made his mark in A's history by tying Mark McGwire at 48! In a way, that's kinda cool he only tied it. Kurtz is only 23, he's got plenty of time to break more records, maybe even that one!

Today's game is pretty critical. If the A's lose they will get swept AND officially fall out of first place in the AL West. This normally strong offense has all of a sudden averaged only 2.33 runs per game in their past six contests. Not too great. 

Jeffrey Springs takes the mound for the A's today, let's hope he brings his best stuff and is dialed in! It's a pretty big late-May game!

body.title: PRIVACY IS NOT INTROVERSION
body.body: > # **Am I Really an Introvert?** Well... this question crossed my mind a few days ago while responding to a prompt on Ladies of Hive. And after thinking about it, my answer is simple: **No, I am not an introvert.** I am just someone who loves her private space. I am someone who prefers texts over calls. Someone who would rather stay at home with my phone and a bowl of cheeseballs than go out hanging with friends. Well... not like I have *that* many friends anyway 😂, but still, I believe I have every right to decide whether I’m an introvert or not. And I’m deciding that I’m not. So why does that always seem to be a problem? It’s funny how quickly people love to label others. The moment you enjoy your own company a little too much, prefer staying indoors, or don’t constantly crave social interaction, suddenly you’re tagged *“introverted”* or worse, *socially awkward.* But is that really fair? There are millions of people in this world, each carrying different personalities, experiences, fears, preferences, and coping mechanisms. Human beings are not one-size-fits-all. Some people recharge by being around others. Some recharge by being alone. Some enjoy both depending on their mood. So why must loving personal space automatically mean something is wrong with you? In a world where you never truly know what people are thinking, where loyalty can be uncertain and intentions can be masked, is it really so strange for someone to choose peace over constant interaction? Personally, I don’t think so. And no, this isn’t me attacking introverts 😅. Introversion is perfectly fine. But what I’m saying is that *privacy and introversion are not always the same thing.* Sometimes, choosing solitude is not about fear. Sometimes, it’s not social awkwardness. Sometimes, it’s simply preference. In a world filled with betrayal, gossip, and unnecessary drama, I often prefer to write things down instead of talking them out with someone. Not because I’m antisocial. Not because I can’t connect with people. But because writing feels safer. Writing doesn’t interrupt me. It doesn’t judge me. It doesn’t repeat my words somewhere else. That, to me, isn’t introversion. That’s protection. That’s self-preservation. That’s me choosing how I process life. Maybe I simply love having control over my personal space. Maybe I enjoy selective interaction. Maybe I just don’t like unnecessary noise. And honestly? That should be okay. ![vitaly-gariev-8MX_XzxoEDk-unsplash (1).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/eugenia7499/23xyTGpYRd4pqt97mVisNTXjwS1VQDxui5kN8pUEYjPUGikGxbEFKVF4DDNDVvu1F82MK.jpg) **[SOURCE](https://unsplash.com/photos/young-woman-watching-tv-and-eating-snacks-on-couch-8MX_XzxoEDk)** So quote me anywhere: **I’m not an introvert. I just deeply value my peace, privacy, and personal space.**

body.title: MY RAINY WEDNESDAY WALK TO FIND THE PERFECT GLOW.
body.body:
Hello 👋 everyone,


It’s Wednesday, and in my area, the sky decided to give us a full dramatic show. 

I stepped out around 11AM and the clouds were so heavy, I knew rain was coming. The air felt cool, and the red soil road looked even richer under the grey sky. 




![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNUAbCUB18m9fuj6LibsAuKVxcSDbsrN4o7Yx4xNgVjkC/1779899534592.png)



Instead of waiting for the rain, I hopped on a kek to make it to the shop before the downpour. There’s something peaceful about riding through wet roads, watching the world slow down for a bit. 




![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcZyb1k9SHfdxSh7nUf8C2i71SLBXgG2LHcy4HpEQpLdY/1779899513988.png)




When I got there, the streets were already wet already wet. Perfect for a walk after the shopping. 



![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPXcNDaNs8brxw9hXrXecR61dPG2rMdbrgXcZQxudfo9D/1779899483034.png)




 Why did I go out in this weather?
I needed to restock my skincare and get some turare. Self-care doesn’t pause just because it’s cloudy 😌

First stop was my favorite shop. The shelves were fully stocked with everything from body lotions to oils. 


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPMJ8voogHgHqDPKdKfNtqzF6QcJ3fV1dtDrqsuS438D4/1779899447185.png)


I settled for this S&K Duchess Glow shower gel. It cost me 10k, but the scent is amazing and my skin feels smooth already. 



![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPZi7VN71kHpH3o5xFEUz2PPbcC7zXH9ruE5jw3WoksS5/1779899432367.png)




I also checked different types of turare before picking these two for 11k. If you know, you know — good turare changes the whole vibe at home. 


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmaPNEGdg9Nejt8PGhfGwMUSFkx4Rp47usYgUWLrXkz1Vn/1779899407503.png)




  Now it’s your turn:
What’s one thing you usually go out to buy or do on your Wednesday walks, rain or shine? 

Drop it in the comments — I want to see how other people spend their midweek walks!.


❤️‍🩹All photos are mine❤️‍🩹

/> We have two of these local made sedans at home. One of them have lower power and manual transmission for efficiency. Luckily we picked the automatic transmission for this trip. Otherwise holding down the clutch pedal for 5 hours kind of chores is truly harsh for me. > 我們家有兩架國產國寶車（Perodua Bezza）。一架是低馬力的手波（Manual），貪它省油；另一架是自動波（Auto）。還好這次出門有保佑，選了 Auto 那架。不然的話，要在車龍裡面踩足 5 個小時的 Clutch（極力子）…… 我看我這條老命一到半路就要報銷，那種 Chores（苦工）真的很折磨人。

/> We left home by around 7 after we had breakfast at one of our local mamak shop, and arrived at the Mersing jetty by almost 1 O clock. > 早上 7 點多，在我們這裡的 Mamak 檔隨便吃個 Roti Canai 當早餐就出發，結果來到 Mersing（豐盛港）碼頭時，已經快要下午 1 點了。坐車坐到屁股要開花。

/> The jetty parking is totally full and therefore they arrange shuttle services to send us to one of the parking lot quite far away from the jetty. > 假期出遊就是這樣的代價，碼頭的停車場直接 Full 到完，一輛車位都沒有。幸好主辦方有安排 Shuttle Service 接駁車，把我們載到一個遠到不懂在哪裡的臨時停車場，有得停已經要謝天謝地了。
/> Since the island is a duty free island, having need to inspect citizenship has become one of the crucial procedure. > 因為這個島是免稅島（Duty-Free），所以檢查公民身份就變成一個很重要的 Procedure（程序）。排隊看 IC 和護照是逃不掉的。

/> Despite it took a long time queuing up at the jetty, but the officers are very helpful and being very efficient to handle all the passengers. From here we saw one of the boat arrived at the jetty and passengers disembark from the boat. > 雖然在碼頭排隊排到很累，但那些 Officer（官員）還是很 Helpful 的，做工也很有 Efficiency（效率），很快就把那麼多遊客 Settled 掉。站在這裡等的時候，剛好看到一艘船到岸，那些乘客下船的畫面，熱鬧到好像難民營開飯。

/> Royal customs office is situated right at the jetty exists, so if passengers bought any duty free items from the island, it's best to declare first. If it's taxable, better pay it off than breaking the laws. > 皇家海關（Customs）的 Office 就建在碼頭出口的 Right Side。拉叔溫馨提示：如果你們在島上買了什麼免稅的東西，最好是乖乖去 Declare（申報）。如果要中抽稅，就還錢啦，奉公守法好過犯法，等下中到重罰就不划算。

/> Cata 1903 is our ship and finally we get to board the ship. Since the seats are numbered, so we're not too worry if our seats will be taken even if we queued at the back. > 「Cata 1903」就是我們這次坐的船，終於可以 Boarding 上船了。還好這裡的座位是有 Number 的，所以就算排隊排在最後面也不用怕 Seat 被別人坐掉，不用像平時那樣去搶。

/> It was a twin isle passenger ferry. It feels like riding on a giant airplane. I haven't got a chance to ride in a 747, but I guess that's how 747 passenger jet design was. > 這是一艘有兩條通道（Twin Aisle）的大型客輪，坐在裡面那個 Feel，真的很像在坐那種 Giant（巨大）的大飛機。雖然拉叔這輩子還沒有機會坐過真正的 747，但我猜 747 的 Cabin 設計大概也就是這個 Layout 吧。
/> The passenger cabin also contain overhead storage compartment, which conveniently stored our standard size luggage. > 船艙頭頂也是有那種 Overhead Storage（行李艙），很方便，剛好可以把我們 Standard Size 的行李箱塞進去，不用塞在腳下頂着頂着。

/> After suffering for another 2 hours of boat ride, finally we arrived at the Tioman island and we disembark at the Detik Jetty. We thought that was over but then... > 在船上又受罪了差不多 2 個小時，終於來到 Tioman Island（刁曼島）了。我們在 Detik 碼頭下船，本來以為受難記已經 Ending 了，結果哪裡知道……

/> It took us another 30 minutes off road in a 4 wheel drive Hilux 😂 that finally sent us to Kampung Juara. Juara in Malaysia means Champion, Kampung means Village. So this place is Champion Village. > 我們還要坐另外 30 分鐘的 Off-road 越野路！坐那種 4 Wheel 的 Hilux 四驅車 😂，一路上震到我的五臟六腑都要移位，才終於把我們送到「Kampung Juara」。Juara 在馬來文是「冠軍」的意思，Kampung 是「村」，所以這裡就是「冠軍村」咯。

/> Barat beach resort is as it's name suggested this part of the habour is situated at the east side of the island, which means we are facing South China sea. > 這次住 Barat Beach Resort。雖然它的名字叫 Barat（西），但其實這個海港是位於島的 East Side（東邊），也就是說，我們開窗面對的就是南中國海。
/> I am a part time aviation geek, so I really enjoy seeing the blue sky being pierced by a bright contrail. > ​我自己算是半個 Aviation Geek（航空迷），所以看到藍藍的天空被一條亮亮的飛機雲（Contrail）狠狠刺穿，那個心靈真的很 Enjoy、很治癒。

/> Beach sand is clean, however this part of the beach being cleaned and heavily polluted by human. So, not much of sea creature activity we can see from here. > 沙灘的沙是蠻乾淨的，不過這一區已經被開發了，多多少少被人類活動「重度污染」到。在海邊看過去，基本上沒什麼海洋生物活動的跡象，大自然還是不夠遊客來。

/> This is one of those activity available, kayaking. This two kids is happily grinding through and shouting towards their friends at the sandy beach. > 這裡也是有提供一些 Activity，比如划獨木舟（Kayaking）。看這兩個小孩子一槳一槳在那邊死撐，還一邊對着沙灘上的朋友大喊大叫，年輕真的有活力，拉叔看到我的腰都有點酸。

/> I picked up one of the sea shell and thought it was beautiful. I am not sure if I want to bring it back to Kuala Lumpur. We are still in the arriving day, for the next 3 days I am not sure if I'm gonna love this place or not. > 在沙灘撿到一個蠻漂亮的貝殼，在想着要不要帶回吉隆坡。不過今天才第一天到步，接下來的 3 天，我到底會不會愛上這個地方，我自己都還不知道。

/>\n\nTowards the end of this side of the habour was a shack that looks quite modern. From what I see it, this is not one of those commercial accommodation. It has post box, this is probably one of those private holiday House or \
just like those police movie. > 走到海港的盡頭，有一間看起來蠻 Modern（現代）的小木屋。看它的樣子，又不像是那種給遊客住的 Commercial 住宿。門口居然有 Post Box（郵箱），我猜這不是人家的 Private Holiday House（私人度假屋），就是那種警匪片裡面主角用來躲避的「Safe House」（安全屋）。

/>

Sun is setting behind the hills, which means we will be able to see the sunrise from the sea the next day. So we went back to the resort for a quick shower and getting ready for dinner.​
> 夕陽已經落到山後面去了。既然黃昏在山那邊，那就代表明天早上我們一定可以在海那邊看到日出。不講那麼多，先回 Resort 沖涼洗掉一身汗，準備去吃晚餐咯！

body.title: For European glory this afternoon in Leipzig
body.body: > This afternoon (Venezuela time), the Conference League final will be played at the Red Bull Arena in Leipzig, Germany, between Crystal Palace and Rayo Vallecano, both teams vying for glory. Crystal Palace, the English side, aims to become the third English team to lift the trophy in the last four years, highlighting the economic and sporting superiority of English clubs over others. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmY2xR7mENVPmViPyPq7E5TDwtmVim2KZs4EWrdkcjzcwF/1779898320722.png) [source](https://es.uefa.com/uefaconferenceleague/) Both teams reached the final after defeating their opponents in the semifinals. Crystal Palace is arguably the favorite to win the trophy, which would be unprecedented, as it would be the first time a debutant in any **UEFA** competition has achieved this feat in their first appearance. Furthermore, the winner would earn an even greater prize: a place in the **Europa League** next season, since they failed to qualify through their domestic league. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmekxNHLTZ64SzYSu2zb7TSxFLWyLykW1E4CaLSRHrguES/1779898391480.png) [source](https://www.eluniversal.com.mx/deportes/crystal-palace-vs-rayo-vallecano-horario-y-canales-para-ver-la-final-de-la-conference-league-hoy-miercoles-27-de-mayo/) I must confess that I haven't seen a single game of the competition so far, but now I'll be able to watch the final, which will be historic for both clubs as they try to lift the title. I've been looking for some information, and well, the teams are on very different streaks, but right now Rayo Vallecano seems to have the advantage. It should be said, though, that in their last **Premier League** games they played with reserves to avoid injuries, since they were far from everything else with only this competition on the horizon. That's why I see Crystal Palace as the favorites, although it should be a very close match, with both teams looking to give their opponent no space and looking for any opportunity to make the difference.

If you have a garden or a yard, you can practice a little with your son. You definitely need to try out a few swings to see what is needed but it's a good game and practice for both of you. 

At least you keep him busy and he's learning something too. It's a win-win. 

By the time you go to Thailand 🇹🇭 again, you both know how to do it 😎

body.title: Mis nuevos vecinitos [Esp/Eng]
body.body:
>  ![380152.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/emilypino/23xL3A37eB7wSvpEoFjWGYk8DZBFVyU86G1iRcxrU9FVuCEsyqGmKfSWVbaZk2qeTe12Z.png) Hola, ¿qué tal amigos cómo están por aquí? Muy bien, gracias a Dios, aunque un poquito trasnochada por problemas de la luz donde vivo una locura, pasamos toda la noche sin luz y ando con un sueño horrible. Gracias a Dios no me tocó ya trabajar porque estoy de vacación y aunque un poco dormido, aún les deseo un lindo día. Me levanté muy temprano. Gracias a la luz y la verdad es que yo no había detallado mis nuevos vecinitos. Se trata de unos chivitos que nacieron todos casi para la misma fecha y yo soy la verdad amante de los animales, decidí acercarme a echarle un ratico broma.
Hello, how are you all doing over there? I’m doing very well, thank goodness, although I’m a bit sleep-deprived because of power cuts where I live – it’s been madness. We spent the whole night without electricity and I’m absolutely knackered. Thank goodness I didn’t have to go to work as I’m on holiday, and even though I’m a bit sleepy, I still wish you all a lovely day. I got up very early. Thanks to the light, and to be honest, I hadn’t really had a proper look at my new little neighbours. They’re some little goats that were all born around the same time, and as I’m a real animal lover, I decided to pop over and spend a little while with them.
![20260527_085041.heic](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/emilypino/EoK6imb8MFyFCxRmC1rezrnV1sGHqpn8Cu8Jm5uFTPQuqW6598Br6mNxH3MLK5EDXHo.jpg) ![20260527_084553.heic](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/emilypino/23wMabYaG3VTLjTBy8pjT6u77yXDnPMoCaf6ZMDJboFSjVNVpLEoxmMHmwa6APp1xJX6r.jpg) Todos ellos pertenecen a mi vecino y hay de todos los tamaños, lo cual a mí me sorprendió bastante porque él empezó con una sola borrega. Y de esa borrega, ha tenido todos los que tiene la actualidad, que la verdad son bastante… No sabía que tenía tantos así, o quizás no le había prestado tanta atención… Al principio vi un pequeñito con su cabecita negra y su cuerpito amarillo; se veía bastante chistoso, y era bastante pequeño. Estaba justo al lado de mi casa y me acerqué un rato, pero no dejaba que yo me acercara en eso. Yo me hice vecino y me ayudó para que pudiera jugar con él. Cuando el medio aquí estaba tan emocionado, decidió presentarme sus otros bebés, uno de ellos son 2 morochas, que me pareció bastante interesante cómo en la naturaleza también se dan estos casos, las 2 eran idénticas bueno, allí lo pueden ver. Eso fue algo que me dejó bastante bastante impresionada ver a las 2 borriguitas idénticas.
They all belong to my neighbour and come in all sizes, which really surprised me because he started out with just one ewe. And from that one ewe, he’s ended up with all the ones he has now, which, to be honest, are quite a few… I didn’t realise he had so many, or perhaps I hadn’t really paid much attention… At first I saw a tiny one with a little black head and a little yellow body; it looked quite funny, and it was quite small. It was right next to my house and I went over for a bit, but it wouldn’t let me get close to it. I became friends with it and it let me play with it. When the little one here was so excited, he decided to introduce me to his other babies; two of them are brunettes, which I found quite interesting as these cases also occur in nature – the two were identical, well, you can see them there. That was something that left me quite, quite impressed, seeing the two identical little ones.
![20260527_085156.heic](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/emilypino/Eou9ExxnrdX3wSXFM4jMRNWtSZFoWJCrruNN9qMj6V2H6vuJkwhdLwZYHfpqgNMcMHo.jpg) ![20260527_085154.heic](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/emilypino/EoyPvFLLZ31AD3K8vBUtk2ew7adGu8f4kRHjAzneSam9NQFCv79ZJkNqEnskwBHFvVe.jpg) ![20260527_085246.heic](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/emilypino/EoGyx4FNnihRcp8j7aunqtd7oF4G14kkGkYTyPUTmqB5PrcJ6ufbeEjH652tcGbLm6p.jpg) ![20260527_085156(0).heic](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/emilypino/EowGe9g35shX46Sn622KbXHFu8EP9eW6AA53VrJ7busM6847m74sapjp9Y9T4VGtMhn.jpg) ![20260527_085247.heic](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/emilypino/23xAcLnqrDDg1PzMpXjxfAdTH55Uri3UTc8XbWQqVJb8dxx7Px4QYsjeaLhgLteH7BFCJ.jpg) El último que me presentó fue el que me enamoró totalmente se trata de un borriguito pequeñito que su mamá murió al parirlo, a mí me pareció impresionante que siguiera vivo y le pregunté a mi vecino, y me dijo que lo había salvado dándole leche vaca desde chiquito, por lo cual él es uno de los más grandes y parece uno de los más pequeños porque no se ha criado con su mamá y al estar criado con personas, lo hace pegado a las personas y él llega súper tranquilo a dónde estás tú es muy cariñosito, porque desde pequeño solo ha visto a los humanos. Ya gracias a Dios, está tan grande que come solo y es de vida, Pero es hermoso se llama Ñe, así que yo aproveché de tomarme fotos con él saludos amigos.
The last one he showed me was the one I fell completely in love with—a tiny little lamb whose mum died giving birth to him. I was amazed that he was still alive, so I asked my neighbour, and he told me he’d saved it by feeding it cow’s milk from a very young age. That’s why it’s one of the biggest, yet it looks like one of the smallest because it wasn’t raised by its mum. Having been brought up by people, it’s very attached to them and comes over to you very calmly; it’s very affectionate, because it’s only ever seen humans since it was little. Thank God, he’s now big enough to eat on his own and is full of life. He’s lovely – his name is Ñe – so I took the opportunity to have my photo taken with him. Cheers, mates.
![20260527_085928.heic](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/emilypino/23wgYezwvSZuk2VWL9bYqKxWAjpYkENezjkzJtd29v2JPRAdPS8mvpGR75K6fKANBMmqA.jpg) ![20260527_092037.heic](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/emilypino/23wgQH986TVxmZB7TJ5dtFy1nSMLVamKHuGuGxJbPCYphEfTwyBNbMo5nLyCwj4zZU41t.jpg) ![20260527_092034.heic](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/emilypino/23yd5rTX6bc4RPMZuUn44peNE12eQihPwP7xXqyYJojSGKmfftYvAUpGWuhvx64jrGH6Q.jpg)
https://images.hive.blog/DQmPp3w4d7XKqyHe7ehy2vRmWfJDa3A7FvafWG3WpoLJcc5/11.png

body.title: The Road to Rebellion: Abundance Year Episode 1979 (audio: noxsoma.substack.com)
body.body:
Full Metal Ox Day 1914
Wednesday 27, May 2026
Abundance Year Episode 1979
Noxsoma Life Camp:  
The Road to Rebellion
Omnipotence 
Common Senses
From stubborn child to enlightened rebel. 

![1979.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmckWkvnchcZNxoMANGrd4STZCvzRYqZtaaihBJN3Tx2Bs/1979.png)

Today's Episode:   https://odysee.com/@Noxsoma:2/1914_full_5-27-26_1979_rebel:0?r=47k2ScJsm9Uex9eETqgCCA8q1fukdST9 
Channels: go to noxsoma.substack.com and subscribe.
The Road to Rebellion 
Friends, frequenters, visitors and tourists, need not, “figure out” that your humble scribe is a smart-ass. We let you know upfront. No hidden fees, no bait & switch, and no promises. No salesman will call. Operators are not standing by. It is what it is. And I is what I is. The only question is, “is he more smart than ass? Or more ass than smart?” It’s like the question with advertising. “Half of all advertising works. The question is, which half?”  
Being a wise-guy is a rung on the ladder to “evil genius.” Maybe it’s halfway up that ladder. Way down near the bottom, is cute, trusting and naive. “You’re so schweet. Adorable!” The savvy mindecant has already figured out the ascension scale. The formula. The secret. The higher one ascends on this philosophical scale, the more frustrated one becomes. More cynical, skeptical, suspicious. More aware, more discerning, more enlightened. More disappointed, more self aware, more self sufficient, and less tolerant of the herd. Less tolerant, and more contemptuous. Because as you ascend this latter, and you make these self actualizing discoveries, you’re thinking, “Whoa, I gotta tell people about this. It will really help them.” It’s like you got some gospel and you think, “this knowledge can change the world.” 

And the reception you get is less than enthusiastic. It can range to much darker reactions. 

“That’s nice honey. What’s on Nutflix tonight?”

“Don’t disturb this groove. Sucka!”

Your humble vagabond is not at evil genius level yet. We’re not aiming for that level. We wouldn’t mind, “genius.” But evil is a little too much to manage. 
Here’s an abstract of the evil genius. There are a coupe of models. Model A, is born into an upper class family and sent to the kinds of private schools that still teach Latin and fencing. There’s already mild contempt for the lower classes and that contempt is amplified in this scholastic environment. They read Malthus, Darwin, Bentham, and Huxley. They admire the Dulles brothers, Harry Anslinger and Dick Cheney. Despise the Kennedys and regard FDR as a class traitor. They have a brilliance that is half nature and half nurture. And if they can manage to stay away from alcoholism and their homosexual proclivities, they will be installed into the policy making apparatus that ensures that the poor stay poor, or get poorer, the middle class continues to struggle, the upper class remains a class buffer between the wealthy and the middle classes, ensuring there will be no revolution, and the rich, continue to make policy and remain so powerful that the numbers don’t matter. 

The evil genius, isn’t evil in their own view. They are pragmatic, simply preserving the status quo. 

Then, there’s the evil genius that comes from the herd. They figure out the game. It’s a little more nature, or environment, than nurture. Nobody is nurturing these cats. They might be Ivy League smart, but can’t afford to attend. Family is, “ineligible” for some reason. This cat still has options. He can thrive in the parallel economy. This economy maybe does some damage to the community, so he figures out how to ply his talents outside of his community, and bring the profits back home. 

He wants to do right by his peeps. His hood, the friends he grew up with. But guess what. Someone on that ladder, with more ambition than brains and even less scruples, wants to shine. So he tries to mess up the whole system. Of course he’s discovered. Set up, and never seen again. 

But now our parallel economy entrepreneur, is a little more enlightened. He ascends the ladder. “All skin-folk ain’t kin-folk.” He’s a little bit smarter and a little bit harder. Closer to evil. And a little bit less visible.  

So you get the picture. Dumb doesn’t last very long, anywhere. Dumb and ambitious. Even shorter lifespans. This is across the board. 

Your boy is a proponent of the middle way. Mediocrity is not a bad word to my ears. It means balance. It’s the ends that are nearly always attacked first. The periphery. 

“Give me liberty, or give me death!” And the next morning you’re swinging from an old oak tree. 

I will take my liberties, and no one needs to know. Stroll through the gates while the watchers are watching those deemed more suspicious. More watchable. But you don’t trespass and start bragging about it to those you have trespassed against. That’s dumb. And dumb gets you vanished.  

In many ways, Vagabond Rebellion is against dumb shit. 

“When you do dumb shit, dumb shit happens.” 

Rebellion isn’t limited to the usual suspects. It also includes movements and concepts and stuff out here that excites the herd and gets them following the charlatans du jour. I see it on social media daily. I’ve monitored it for years. I have witnessed channels I’ve followed for years change their editorial presentation and lean and little further ideologically one way or the other. Then, their sponsorship revenue increased. Good for them. I don’t count their money. But I can’t count on their information anymore either. So why watch? 

I don’t call them out, any more than I’d narc on dude thriving in the black market. If I can get some European-type knock-offs, made in China, from the Senegalese “vendor,” just off El Puerta del Sol, that’s a win. I’m not gonna dime him out. We’re both fightin’ against the system in our own way. 

So even when I can clearly see what some of these accounts are up to, and I can smell the bovine excrement on this side of my screen. I don’t call them out, personally. Because it won’t even make a difference.  

If you’re gonna be a rebel. At least find a cause. 

Currently, if you are still with me. (Sometimes I don’t think fingers type this stuff to be understood.) Mind is rebelling against a cosmogony we were preparing to create a new religion from. Or at least a philosophy. Or maybe even a rebellion. 

Our groove was that the Annunaki wanted to wipe out humanity, which we would parlay into a tax exempt religion that would encourage a “re-vie-lution.” (Vie means life. Get it?)  Using reverse psychology, we’d convince the herd, to buff it up, get their minds straight and their bodies strong and prepare for the Annuanki at the gate! But the Annunaki are not the enemy. The herd is the enemy.

So much for that revolution. Maybe I level up a rung. Closer to evil genius status. A little more brilliance. A little more ruthlessness. Maybe I will sacrifice the herd to save the herd. Perfectly logical from a European perspective. But Mind is working away from those concepts. 

Emindcipation.

# Learn Zig Series (#61) - Assembler: Disassembler and Binary Inspector

![zig.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmaHuB6qTWHaSpJHQ1S8FCCRmNQuUxTcPZdU4yKHsJ7vEP/zig-banner.png)

**Project G: Assembler/Disassembler (3/3)**

### What will I learn
- How to read a binary file and decode instructions back to human-readable assembly text;
- Building a decoder function: `decode(u16) -> Instruction` that reverses the encoding from episode 59;
- Pretty-printing disassembled output with instruction addresses and aligned columns;
- Building a hex dump mode that shows raw bytes alongside decoded mnemonics;
- Heuristics for detecting data vs code regions in a flat binary;
- Round-trip testing: assemble source, disassemble the binary, compare with original;
- A unified CLI tool (`zigasm`) that combines assembler, disassembler, and VM in one binary;
- Project retrospective: what building an assembler/disassembler taught us about Zig.

### Requirements
- A working modern computer running macOS, Windows or Ubuntu;
- An installed Zig 0.14+ distribution (download from ziglang.org);
- The ambition to learn Zig programming.

- Advanced

# Learn Zig Series (#61) - Assembler: Disassembler and Binary Inspector

In [episode 59](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-59-assembler-instruction-encoding) we built an instruction encoder and VM. In [episode 60](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-60-assembler-two-pass-assembly) we built a two-pass assembler that turns human-readable assembly text into binary. Today we close the loop: we're building a disassembler that reads binary files and produces readable assembly text, plus a hex dump inspector that shows you exactly what's inside every byte. And then we tie the whole project together with a unified CLI that lets you assemble, disassemble, inspect, and run programs -- all from one tool.

This is the final part of Project G and the satisfying conclusion. Going from binary back to text is the inverse of what the assembler does, which means our decoder is essentially the mirror image of our encoder. If the encoder packs an opcode and operands into a 16-bit word, the decoder unpacks that word back into its constituent parts. If we've done everything correctly, we should be able to assemble a program, disassemble it, and get back something functionally identical to the original source. That round-trip property is the ultimate test that our encoding scheme is consistent and lossless (at least for the instruction data -- comments and label names are of course lost in the binary).

Here we go!

## The decoder: unpacking a 16-bit word

The decoder is the inverse of the `Instruction.toU16()` function from episode 59. Given a raw `u16` value read from a binary file, we need to extract the opcode (bits 12-15), the destination register (bits 9-11), the mode flag (bit 8), and either the source register (bits 0-2) or the immediate value (bits 0-7). We already have the packed struct layout from episode 59, so we can reuse it directly:

```zig
const std = @import(\

case gracefully. For now we're fine.

## Pretty-printing disassembled instructions

A raw struct dump isn't very useful. What we want is output that looks like actual assembly listing -- addresses on the left, mnemonics and operands on the right, nicely aligned. Something like:

```
0x0000: MOV  R0, 5
0x0002: MOV  R1, 10
0x0004: ADD  R0, R1
0x0006: HLT
```

The formatter needs to know which operand format each opcode uses. HLT, NOP, and RET take no operands. JMP, JEQ, JNE, and CALL take a single address. PUSH and POP take a single register. Everything else takes a destination register and either a source register or an immediate, depending on the mode bit:

```zig
const InstructionFormatter = struct {
    fn formatInstruction(decoded: DecodedInstruction, address: u16, writer: anytype) !void {
        // address prefix
        try writer.print(\

but every instruction decodes to something slightly wrong.

Second, we handle the edge case of odd-length files. If the binary has an extra byte at the end (which shouldn't happen if it was produced by our assembler, but we're being defensive), we emit it as a `.byte` directive -- a common convention in disassembly listings for raw data.

The output goes into an `ArrayList(u8)` which acts as a string builder. We use the ArrayList's writer interface, which is the same pattern we used in the markdown renderer back in [episode 39](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-39-markdown-to-html-renderer-and-cli). The writer interface is one of those Zig patterns that once you learn it, you use it everywhere.

## Hex dump mode: bytes alongside instructions

Sometimes you need to see the raw bytes. A hex dump that shows the encoded bytes next to the decoded instruction is invaluable for debugging encoding issues. Here's what the output looks like:

```
ADDR   HEX      INSTRUCTION
0x0000 0105     MOV  R0, 5
0x0002 0A11     MOV  R1, 10
0x0004 0022     ADD  R0, R1
0x0006 0000     HLT
```

And the implementation:

```zig
fn hexDump(self: *Disassembler, binary: []const u8) ![]const u8 {
    self.output.clearRetainingCapacity();
    const writer = self.output.writer();

    try writer.print(\

heuristic catches the most obvious cases -- runs of zero bytes, or garbage after a HLT -- but it won't catch every code/data boundary.

Having said that, for the programs produced by our assembler this heuristic is perfectly adequate. Our programs don't embed data in the instruction stream, so every word is a valid instruction. The region analysis becomes more interesting when inspecting binaries from external sources or when we eventually add data sections to our assembler.

## Round-trip testing: the ultimate correctness check

The best test for our assembler/disassembler pair is round-trip verification: assemble source text into binary, disassemble the binary back into text, and verify the instructions match. Label names will be lost (they exist only in the assembler's symbol table, not in the binary) but the instruction mnemonics and operands should be identical:

```zig

that don't tell you anything. For debugging you might want to see all registers, but for normal runs the non-zero filter keeps things clean.

## Testing the full CLI pipeline

Let's verify the entire workflow with a complete test that exercises assemble, disassemble, and hexdump together:

```zig
test \

is a foundational principle in compiler construction.

**Episode 61** -- the disassembler and tooling. The inverse of the assembler: binary to text. Plus a hex dump inspector and a unified CLI that ties the whole project together. The round-trip test (text -> binary -> text) validates that encoding and decoding are mirror operations.

What's remarkable is how much of this project reused concepts from earlier in the series. File I/O from [episode 10](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-10-project-structure-modules-and-file-io). Testing from [episode 12](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-12-testing-and-test-driven-development). Tagged unions from [episode 6](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-6-structs-enums-and-tagged-unions). Error handling from [episode 4](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-4-error-handling-zigs-best-feature). Memory management from [episode 7](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-7-memory-management-and-allocators). Each concept built on the last, and now they all come together in a real tool.

That's the thing about systems programming -- you don't just learn individual features and forget them. Each concept layers on top of the others. Packed structs are useful for encoding. Encoding is useful for assemblers. Assemblers are useful for understanding how computers actually work. And understanding how computers work makes you a better programmer in every language, not just Zig ;-)

## Wat we geleerd hebben

- The decoder is the mirror of the encoder: `@bitCast` on a raw `u16` extracts the packed struct fields (opcode, destination, mode, operand) without manual bit shifting
- Pretty-printing uses Zig's format strings with left-alignment (`{s:<5}`) to produce properly columned output
- The disassembler reads binary two bytes at a time in little-endian order, decodes each word, and formats it as an assembly listing with hex addresses
- Hex dump mode shows raw byte pairs alongside decoded instructions -- invaluable for verifying that the encoding matches expectations
- Region detection uses heuristics (consecutive zeros, HLT boundaries) to guess where code ends and data begins, though real disassemblers use much more sophisticated techniques
- Round-trip testing (assemble, then disassemble) validates encoding consistency -- labels are lost but instruction mnemonics and operands should survive the trip
- The unified CLI (`zigasm`) wraps assemble, disassemble, hexdump, and run commands behind a single binary, giving a complete development workflow for our teaching ISA
- This project combined packed structs, hash maps, file I/O, error handling, tagged unions, testing, and CLI argument parsing -- concepts from across the entire series working together in one tool

This wraps up Project G and the assembler/disassembler mini-project. We went from raw bit encoding to human-readable assembly and back again, building every layer ourselves. Next time we're moving into a completely diferent domain -- working with the file system at a low level, reading directory contents and metadata.

How about this:

The Aharonov-Bohm effect is a phenomenon in which the phase of a charged particle's wave function is changed when it passes around a completely enclosed magnetic flux, despite the particle traveling only in zero electromagnetic fields. 

Essentially, if two identical coherent charged particle waves are sent around a completely enclosed magnetic flux, their phases are slightly shifted and visualized as a shift in their interference patterns when they merge back together.

今天看了江南老贼的《葵花白发抄》，书买来很久了，今天下午没课专门找个空地方去看，还没看完我整个人就开始懵逼，看完后更是一头雾水恨不能找个东西打几拳出出气。

写的啥啊这是，不可否认，老贼的文字的那股味道和特色还在的，这个故事也符合他的风格，只是让我很难接受啊😦

年轻力盛励志光耀门楣的一击必胜的易小冉爱上了十三岁开始卖身卖艺的妓女天女葵，跋涉千里来到波诡云谲的党派纷争的帝都，他做了一场温柔乡的美梦，他不想再争什么了，在确认这个女人也爱着他的时候，他什么都顾不得了，只想摆脱所有人对他们二人的束缚后远走高飞。他涉世未深，可一旦下定决心后，马上制定了严密的计划，及时中途发生了变故，他也抵抗住了，可是哪里能如他的愿，最终还是倒下了，流尽所有的血也只是爬到了新生活的门前，还是没能跨出去啊……他作为飘忽不定的风筝，那个女人比他大十岁，十三岁开始早已历经风尘，她早年就爱上了另一个男人，那便是握着风筝线的他的丈夫……

天女葵没有出卖易小冉，她爱小冉吗？我不知道，也许早已对丈夫失望的这样一个孤独寂寞的女人爱上帅小伙未尝不可，她真心想跟你走，自己赎了自己的身，给你生下一儿一女，因为你说过能生下儿女的女人就是好女人，然后浪迹天涯或者隐姓埋名过这一生也愿意。她没有等到你啊，小冉！对着丈夫，她弹奏一曲悼念亡夫的曲子后就决绝地残忍地凄美地了解了自己，她来陪你了啊！小冉！

这便是爱吗？我不知道，是两颗孤独的灵魂互相依偎取暖产生的错觉吗？但是你为我挡刀，我带你逃命，吐露心声坦露心怀，爱意便悄悄的在此萌生。

我觉得这是一个好故事，在那样的背景时代下，每个人哪怕高官都身不由己何况这样两个卖身卖命的人，那么产生这样的爱恋也是正常的，很现实啊！我原本觉得这个故事很恶心，看完后我的心里发毛，只是现在写下这些话，我又有些理解他们了。我一直在纠结他们这算爱吗？可爱究竟是什么呢？我不知道。但是他二人都愿意了，对了，我知道了，故事就该在小冉的死那里结束，阿葵一人继续卖艺搜罗情报也罢，就此回老家也罢，被杀自杀都行的。

写什么不行，老贼就不该写出握线人是她的丈夫，他们也许有感情吧，当我想应该不是爱了，阿葵决定把自己交给小冉了，最多就是念及旧情吧，想到这个男人就要死了任谁都会难过一下吧，可她一没有告密，二没有后悔，就乖乖的坐在门口等你啊小冉，小冉你毁约了啊！

都怪你老贼，我超级生气😠真不应该啊，你别写这茬的话，它就是个凄美的故事，你这么一毁，变得有些恶心了，我气死了老贼！

body.body: > Today was a very beautiful and blessed day. Today is the 10th of Dhul-Hijjah. According to the Islamic calendar, on 10th of Dhul-Hijjah, all Muslims sacrifice and remember the Sunnah of Abraham. Hazrat Abraham (peace be upon him) sacrificed while obeying the command of Allah Almighty and then Allah liked this sacrifice and thus Muslims will continue to follow this Sunnah of Abraham until the Day of Judgment. So today we sacrificed three goats and the purpose of this sacrifice was only to please Allah and follow the Sunnah of Hazrat Abraham (peace be upon him). The time of sacrifice is after the Fajr prayer when the sun rises and the light spreads, then Eid al-Adha is offered. After Eid al-Adha, every Muslim sacrifices his animal. So today we also sacrificed. When Muslims sacrifice, the meat of the animal is divided into three parts. One part is for the poor and needy, the second part is for their loved ones and relatives, and the third part is for the person who is sacrificing. So after the sacrifice, Muslims eat different types of food from the meat. They make the dough and invite friends and relatives, but the first day is the busiest day. Every Muslim is busy, and most butchers are also busy. So today's day began with the blessed name of Allah, the Almighty. When I woke up early in the morning, I prayed the Fajr prayer and then thanked Allah for giving me the opportunity to sacrifice. Allah gave me the strength and the ability to spend some money to buy an animal for sacrifice. I sacrificed one animal on my behalf, one animal was from my mother, and one animal was from my younger brother. In this way, we sacrificed three animals. We divided the meat of the three animals equally and distributed it to the poor and needy. The story of the morning is as follows: When I woke up early in the morning, I prayed. After praying, I gave water to the animals we had bought for sacrifice, served them, and prayed to Allah that Allah may accept my sacrificed animals. Then I went to take a bath and at 6:30 it was time for the Eid al-Adha prayer. I reached the mosque at 6:30. After reaching the mosque, I offered the Eid prayer. And immediately I returned home. As soon as I reached home, the butcher had arrived at our house. He slaughtered the first animal and then we skinned the animal and in the same way, whatever process is done, we divided the meat into small pieces. In this way, by one o'clock in the day, we had slaughtered the three animals and divided their meat. Then we cooked the meat for ourselves. After cooking, all of us in the family ate it and thanked Allah Almighty for giving us the opportunity to make a sacrifice in His way. After eating, we were very tired and then I rested for a while. After resting, I offered the noon prayer and then chatted with my mother and my wife at home for a while. This is how this beautiful day passed. When it was time for Asr, I offered Asr prayer and then got busy with my other work at home. But we made a program that we would cook a salty meal. Then my daughter, I and my nephews cooked a salty meal together. It was so delicious that we ate it in the evening. It was a beautiful day. I went to my sister's house to give the meat. I went to my aunt's house and my uncle's house. The meat that we were supposed to distribute among our relatives went to the houses of our relatives and friends. First of all, I gave the meat that I distributed to the poor people in my neighborhood and near my house. Those who had not bought a sacrificial animal and did not have the strength, I was the first to go early in the morning when our animal was slaughtered and We distributed the food, so immediately after distributing it, I went to the homes of the poor families around my house and distributed the meat. Then I went to my sister's house and gave the meat to her. After that, I went to the homes of my other relatives to give the meat. Then I returned home. We cooked the meat that was now my share, and then the whole family ate it together. It was a beautiful day. It was a busy day. And my prayer is that Allah will accept what we have sacrificed in the way of Allah for the sake of Allah. There was no pretense in it, no arrogance. ![IMG_20260527_075327.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRvApbJKe4VYb4C3pq3e19Tc2hfm85xUri6uS95myaair/IMG_20260527_075327.jpg) ![IMG_20260527_075548.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRUsG9ronCA58mth8RGPiNSPSQAjPNsRgGW3Rrv9aKRN2/IMG_20260527_075548.jpg) When the sacrificial meat was being cut, I took some pictures, which you can see. I took very few pictures and I did not take pictures so that I would not be arrogant or proud. You can see the pictures, which I took, three or four pictures, which I am sharing with all of you here. ![IMG_20260527_075333.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTHAWLjgd1g2G4q5aByEwZrH4oCrp8zMR1Ep1JTyNFFGg/IMG_20260527_075333.jpg) ![IMG_20260527_075315.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQg5WzoC6hEZEcEhWmLMQrhr6V8ynWLJCTwxKpxZjep3E/IMG_20260527_075315.jpg) IMG_20260527_075313.jpg(https://images.hive.blog/DQmP7qvZMv4YsK5Vj3PAHcyeS2bPDiiZztYhYGoueQyXbD4/IMG_20260527_075310.jpg) ![IMG_20260527_075302.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmV8WbNTiH76awCp7RDEn5ePdvP7nr4JLCsYvHCBtGqKFv/IMG_20260527_075302.jpg) ![IMG_20260527_075552.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmUGBHUWULWUEd74ELTnbpuTHpkqJ4G4d9mF1Tp1hGH3pt/IMG_20260527_075552.jpg) ![IMG_20260527_075536.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPSP9t2xsewZTcciTX6pVmGQMnnXAWP4XySG25JXrRCDc/IMG_20260527_075536.jpg) ![IMG_20260527_075554.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRBD7Bk8x4aPR3Mj2cw989mazrLEcRPHXvLEaNsZ8k2Hh/IMG_20260527_075554.jpg) This was my beautiful and lovely day today, the story of which I have told you. So, the purpose of writing this article is only to motivate you, to create that passion within you that creates humility and modesty. I want to write one more thing here that when a person does any work for the pleasure of Allah, Allah's pleasure is included in it. If you do any good deed for the pleasure of Allah, or help the poor, or treat the people around you with kindness, then Allah will definitely be pleased with you and will reward you. Life is very beautiful and all the people who live around us are beautiful, but we should also pay attention to those who are poor, who are needy. This philosophy of sacrifice has only one purpose. Then when Allah was pleased, then we do this Sunnah of Abraham so that the action that Hazrat Ibrahim (peace be upon him) did for the pleasure of Allah pleased Allah Almighty. And then Allah Almighty made sacrifice obligatory on Muslims. Sacrifice is obligatory only on those who can afford it, those who can buy animals. If you are poor, if you do not have the strength to buy it, then this sacrifice is not obligatory on you at all. Sacrifice is not showing off. Sacrifice is not arrogance, pride, rather it is humility. Sacrifice should be made for the pleasure of Allah. And this also creates in man that meat is distributed among the poor, feelings of sympathy and love are also created. This is the philosophy. I hope you like this article I have written today. Thank you very much to all of you.
