
For most custom detection tasks, **200-500 annotated images** with transfer learning from a COCO-pretrained model is enough to get decent results. The pretrained backbone already knows how to extract visual features -- edges, textures, shapes -- from episode #45's CNN theory in practice. Your training just teaches the detection head to recognize your specific objects. More data always helps, but the diminishing returns curve flattens quickly with transfer learning.

_A practical tip from experience_: spend more time on annotation quality than on model tuning. Inconsistent annotations (different annotators drawing boxes at different tightness levels, missing objects in some images, mislabeled classes) hurt performance more than any hyperparameter choice. Clean data beats a bigger model every time -- the same lesson we learned back in episode #14 about data preparation.

## Evaluation: mean Average Precision

Detection evaluation is more involved than classification because you need to match predicted boxes to ground truth boxes. We introduced **IoU** in episode #78. Now we build the full evaluation pipeline on top of it.

The standard metric is **mAP** (mean Average Precision). For each class:

1. Sort all detections by confidence score (descending)
2. For each detection, check if it matches a ground truth box (IoU >= threshold)
3. Mark each detection as true positive (matched) or false positive (unmatched or duplicate)
4. Compute precision and recall at each step
5. Plot the precision-recall curve
6. Average Precision = area under this curve

```python
import numpy as np


def compute_iou(box1, box2):
    x1 = max(box1[0], box2[0])
    y1 = max(box1[1], box2[1])
    x2 = min(box1[2], box2[2])
    y2 = min(box1[3], box2[3])
    inter = max(0, x2 - x1) * max(0, y2 - y1)
    a1 = (box1[2] - box1[0]) * (box1[3] - box1[1])
    a2 = (box2[2] - box2[0]) * (box2[3] - box2[1])
    union = a1 + a2 - inter
    return inter / max(union, 1e-6)


def compute_ap(predictions, ground_truths,
               iou_threshold=0.5):

        if (best_iou >= iou_threshold
                and best_gt not in matched_gt):

            matched_gt.add(best_gt)
        else:

    tp_cum = np.cumsum(tp)
    fp_cum = np.cumsum(fp)

    precision = tp_cum / (tp_cum + fp_cum)
    recall = tp_cum / len(ground_truths)

    # Area under P-R curve
    # (11-point interpolation or all-points)
```

**mAP** is just the mean AP across all object classes. But which IoU threshold do you use?

**mAP50** (PASCAL VOC metric): AP at IoU threshold 0.5. Relatively lenient -- a prediction that overlaps the ground truth by just half counts as correct. This is fine for \

but doesn't reward precise localization.

**mAP50-95** (COCO metric): the mean of AP values computed at IoU thresholds from 0.5 to 0.95, in steps of 0.05. Much stricter. A model that localizes objects precisely (IoU > 0.9) scores significantly higher than one that draws sloppy boxes (IoU around 0.5). This is the standard metric today, and it's what you'll see reported in every modern detection paper.

## Choosing your detector

If you're starting a new detection project, here's the practical decision framework:

| Constraint | Recommendation |
|------------|---------------|
| Real-time on edge (phone, Jetson) | YOLOv8n or YOLOv8s |
| Real-time on server GPU | YOLOv8m or YOLOv8l |
| Maximum accuracy, speed secondary | YOLOv8x or Faster R-CNN + ResNeXt |
| Small objects dominate | Faster R-CNN with FPN (two-stage still wins here) |
| Custom classes, few images | YOLOv8 + transfer learning from COCO |
| Quick prototype / demo | YOLOv8 pretrained on COCO (80 classes) |

For the vast majority of real-world projects, **YOLOv8 with transfer learning** is the right starting point. Fast to train, easy to deploy (ONNX, TensorRT, CoreML, TFLite -- all supported), well-documented, and competitive with anything more complex. Start there, measure your performance, and only switch to a heavier architecture if you have a specific reason.

Two-stage detectors like Faster R-CNN still have an edge on small object detection because the RPN can propose very small regions that single-shot detectors might miss at their coarsest feature level. But that gap is narrowing with every new YOLO release.

## Samengevat

- **YOLO** reframed detection as single-pass regression: divide the image into a grid, predict boxes and classes directly, achieve real-time speeds (45+ FPS) -- a fundamentally different approach from the two-stage proposal-then-classify pipeline we covered in episode #78;
- the **YOLO evolution** (v1 through v8) systematically added anchor boxes, multi-scale prediction, better backbones, and eventually circled back to anchor-free design -- YOLOv8 is the current practical standrd for real-world detection;
- **SSD** introduced multi-scale prediction from different feature map levels, handling objects of varying sizes by using small feature maps for large objects and large feature maps for small ones;
- **anchor-free detectors** (FCOS, CenterNet) simplify architecture by eliminating anchor design entirely -- predict distances to box edges or detect center points directly, with fewer hyperparameters to tune;
- **custom detection** with transfer learning requires as few as 200-500 annotated images: structure your dataset in YOLO format, start from COCO-pretrained weights, and the backbone's existing feature knowledge does most of the heavy lifting;
- **mAP** (mean Average Precision) measures detection quality across the full precision-recall curve, with mAP50-95 as the strict modern standard that rewards precise localization at high IoU thresholds.

With the detection foundations and modern approaches both covered, we have the complete picture of how to find objects in images. But detection only draws rectangles around things. What if you need pixel-level precision -- knowing exactly which pixels belong to each object? That's a different problem with its own set of architectures, and it builds directly on the feature pyramid and multi-scale concepts we've been working with here.

title.body:

![zzpEjlN7mdl0xdW0_image_1779867868488.webp](https://cdn.liketu.com/media/carolin77/images/zzpEjlN7mdl0xdW0_image_1779867868488/zzpEjlN7mdl0xdW0_image_1779867868488.webp)

![QDNpL5CLg45gIg9e_image_1779868703835.webp](https://cdn.liketu.com/media/carolin77/images/QDNpL5CLg45gIg9e_image_1779868703835/QDNpL5CLg45gIg9e_image_1779868703835.webp)
</center>
</liketuimages>

人人都会春困，我好像那后知后觉一样，夏困，每天睡不醒的感觉，最近又开始下雨了，不过不是延绵细雨，是瓢泼大雨，下到不会停那样，已经透透地下了两天，这空气已经喝饱了水，湿湿嗒嗒黏黏糊糊。

于是我又后知后觉，噢，原来是梅雨季节来了，逃不掉的，每年这个时候必要经过这样的一段时间，就是空气湿度已经达到顶峰，连吹的风都是带有湿气的风，整个人都湿气重中的样子，难怪我瞌睡呢。

洗好的衣服啊，床单之类的，阳台晒一周都不会干，其实我觉得是干了，但事实上是没干，只能用吹风机吹 再或者开空调的除湿功能去吹它，不然没法收。

提到空调，我又后知后觉，应该团购一个空调清洗，今年已经快到开空调的时候了 ，我家三台空调还没清洗，得赶紧买了预约师傅上门清洁，我自己可没能力拆洗，每次只会把过滤网取下来刷刷，洗个表面没什么用，还得专业的人来干专业的事。

电扇这几天倒是开起来了，但是也不敢一直吹，怕受凉，年纪大了做什么事都觉得心酸，连吹个电扇都怕生病。好了就写到这吧，我要去团购空调清洗了，不然待会下班一嗨又给忘了。

title.title: Grandpa Kangaroo Walk
title.body:
On Sunday we went out walking from our place into the heathland and national park which is only one block away from our street, up a slight hill. We are always looking for reasonably short works, say an hour or so, that aren't too taxing and that can be done after work or for a quick walk on the weekend when we have other things to do. We are spoilt for choice around here, but are still learning all the tracks and beginning to name them as part of our new personal map making landscape. 

![3052.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/riverflows/EoEq3J4gWANEkoubeoUiH9VZ19XWGAQDpc6fkZb8xAg5cCNaD5WwfNwVXuuuGnaPQbL.jpg)
*I love this photo of Jamie, with his new haircut. After all these yars, I still think he is gorgeous.*

Some of the yellow wattle has come out. It seems too early but I guess this is just an early variety. Come August, the whole place will be a lit with yellow flowers. It's quite a spectuacular sight - everything glows, particuarly in the late afternoon. This day was a bit of a dull day, so forgive the dull photos. 

![3053.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/riverflows/Eo8SsSwvWZpsCmiUv3aJrL5jJkbyZMo9JSLEJVYKVm8Mc3YTCMfr8NfcWooR4XEjjie.jpg)

As we walk up the track we get a video message from my 3-year-old grandson who is asking us about kangaroos. We send one back of Jamie bouncing through the bush and say that he is a kangaroo. 

\

he says in his cute way. Bless. In fact, we did say three or four kangaroos but I didn't get my camera out in time.

![3054.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/riverflows/EoK5obtMHtJhEbuiZmhj6d1zbvmeJRfqAg1bJ3tkE6ZseJJc6gQWMGteBkXQhB5it3h.jpg)

We cross onto the old coal mine track which is shut off to traffic now and generally used for cyclists walkers and runners. On this day, nobody is out and about. That's winter for you. It's much quieter. I love it.

![3057.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/riverflows/2458NijYSci31JKA7GKgg436AT1T9rqcx1abxwJ2vSYZeRthUAyz9rR2v67iH4KBVPSsX.jpg)

They have cleared big spaces on the side of the road which will create a fire break which makes us feel happy. Of course fire is always on our minds, but this is the safest season to be in really and we're very very little risk of fire. When you think there's houses not far away, it's quite reassuring. 

![3061.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/riverflows/23uaMmGcJ841V9c25birwcN8uZ8ewZeatPqVMW8DJBQvVUJSqUXyxBRy7SS7SaMhVCn4z.jpg)

You can see the old chimney from the coal mine. They stopped mining here years ago and are still clearing up the land and figuring out a use for it. For now we are hoping for lots of rain to fill it up as a lake for birds. At once stage they floated an Eden Project like the UK but it was shouted down by the community. Too much traffic and tourists - we have enough already in peak season. 

![3058.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/riverflows/243BbycVbc9WmLydVawzNHxjc8shxVTv5iyRDDSNyes7zcVWSgF4Ch9S2115dJ1YaRUSC.jpg)

There are a lot of beautiful old gum trees, a variety of grasses, acacia trees, and banksia - this would all be foreign for any of you that are reading this from overseas and I acknowledge we have a totally different landscape from many of you.

![3059.jpg](image-7-3059.jpg)![3062.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/riverflows/243zZtFdJbRorSD25fnG7V8UCFJ9S1NuYjRqBofhMV1ji1ybmsFrQ8AdWK1iKaY6aqYTA.jpg)

This is the banksia from above - Australia certainly morphed some wild looking flowers.

![3064.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/riverflows/EoeDWasHxRCfAT5b5CtqaRkrSYhkcfeDkDUfAvicCi9YNgmPLHJBeoZdJs7iBjFMq2k.jpg)

It's a good firm track to get a good pace up with a slight downhill as it goes down towards the river so I really enjoyed the walk.

![3067.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/riverflows/EpnCriEAiukZqPzrb4LUcehoxKKycCPBz8YnzCtT3a9vuR2szcn1PryLsVwmKpYXPWG.jpg)

We end up at the beginning of the river which winds down to the sea. There are clear paths on either side and it is very calm and peaceful. We paddle board along here or ride the bikes and some people kayak or fish, although there are no fish at the moment because it is too acidic. They are still trying to solve this problem. Little bridges cross the river so you can cut across at various points to go to the other side of town. Even though it's not far from the houses, it feels like it's in the middle of nowhere.

![3069.jpg](image-11-3069.jpg)![3071.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/riverflows/243fmxnwUmPzWSWvsFuWV7zvu52426QodUg1dkDYMCWn36qstsY3zRs4nGKoZ3c84iLNL.jpg)

I don't picture it that here but we pass the picnic area and a huge children's playground that is shaped like a pirate ship that all the local kids have loved for some 20 to 30 years. I remember taking my boy here when he was little. We stopped for a little while to look at some fairy wrens and fre crest finches And then take some different roads home to look at all the different houses. This town is very unique like that there's all sorts of quirky houses and no uniform estates which is really nice. Some are falling apart summer modernised and there are a couple of new builds amongst them as well, but generally there's a real range of different houses and we get inspiration for our garden as we walk.

![3072.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/riverflows/245mtrE2vGwMwWKZTkcw3RoaKFEzxRimwQp5d38zeWZaRj5z9NZgYMLBWPqiusFv9r4mz.jpg)

It takes longer than we thought to get home because it's the weekend and we stop and talk to a couple of neighbours as we go up our street. We are really enjoying being in a place that has both wild natural environment around but also a community of people we are getting to know. 

I make a scrambled eggs for breakfast and Jamie makes coffee and then we get on with a garden. This is Sunday for you and it couldn't be more perfect.

We decide to call it the Grandpa Kangaroo walk. We are in the habit of naming all our walks locally for easy conversing about which route we will take. I wonder if other people do the same, adding to the personal mapping of their own lives.

Good morning to you all, I hope you are all doing well.

It's been a while since I've had the chance to go Silver shopping due to life in general and it's still a bit bleak around my parts for getting any silver.
The usual places are either completely out of silver or at such a high premium that it makes me cry and I can't afford to buy 😂

So I'm sat doing some work and thought, let's have a look at how the price of Silver is doing compared to the last time in March I checked.
Currently sat at £55.72 an oz according to Bullion by Post, which is still way up for what I paid for most of the pieces in my collection so that's always a reassuring win!

It was £65.02 an oz back in March so a bit of a drop, but if you can find any silver at todays price then I'd bite your hand off if I could buy it.
Pre owned silver 1 oz coins are around £77 to £80+ at the moment from where I can buy, which is a huge premium and something I can't afford.

I have tried to buy Sterling Silver jewellery as well but that has been an utter disaster with plated items, fake Silver and then premiums so high that I could buy a whole oz of Silver bullion for a few grams of jewellery. The prices really are going mad and VAT really doesn't help!

Have any of you managed to find some cheap deals?

transformed\\.body:
<liketuimages>
<center>
![VyXfw6sP5nJH8aqK_IMG_20260517_185521.webp](https://cdn.liketu.com/media/trina77/images/VyXfw6sP5nJH8aqK_IMG_20260517_185521/VyXfw6sP5nJH8aqK_IMG_20260517_185521.webp)
</center>
</liketuimages>

昨天晚上堂嫂来我家坐了两个小时，聊起她与公公也就是我叔叔的相处模式，还有我那堂哥的教育方式。

说来话长，我叔叔一张嘴得罪不少人，情商极低，但他对家庭却是真心付出，对待儿媳比对亲生女儿还要好，自己赚的钱也交给媳妇保管，一家人相处非常融洽。儿媳对待公公也比自己亲生父亲还要好，买衣服时舍得给公公买两千元的衣服，却给自己父亲买1000元的衣服都迟疑不定，并非堂嫂偏心公公，她深知在公婆家中，她受到比自己原生家庭更多的重视。在娘家她是老大，下面有弟弟妹妹，小时候脏活累活都是她干，但到了婆家，家庭事务婆婆全权包揽，公公也是给足了安全感，有他们在，堂哥不敢对媳妇大声呵斥。在这个家，堂嫂无疑是幸福的，同理，她也付出了全部真心在这个家中。

后来，家庭遭遇变故，我婶婶，也就是她婆婆，在一次骑电动车接孩子下课的途中遭遇了车祸，她护住了怀中的孙女，自己却命丧车轮底下，那一年婆婆也才五十岁。至此，公公的心态发生了巨大改变，总觉得自己很可怜，本身的怀脾气变得更加古怪。

这两年，公公查出鼻癌，时长住院治疗，身体每况愈下，当年的威风不再，但这爱骂人的臭脾气却是没改。一直备受疼爱的孙女渐渐长大，不再是爷爷怀中撒娇的小女孩，偶尔顶撞爷爷，爷爷也会动手打孙女，气急了还会说出“为什么当初死的人不是你”这样的话。

孙女与爷爷的关系极尽破裂：不与爷爷待一个屋，只要爷爷在客厅，她就躲房间不出门，也不在一张桌子上吃饭。爷爷认为孙女叛逆不懂事，找到机会仍就辱骂孙女，以为像小时候他教育自己的儿子一样非打即骂的方式能够让孙女听话，然而现在的孩子早就不是我们当年任由父母打骂的孩子了，何况还是爷爷。

transformed\\.title: Evaluating the Role of Structured Football Forecasting in Betting Decisions
transformed\\.body:
The modern football calendar offers an overwhelming volume of matches across domestic leagues, continental tournaments, and international competitions. For bettors and analysts, this abundance creates a practical challenge: how to consistently evaluate upcoming fixtures without relying on intuition or incomplete information. The answer increasingly lies in structured, data-driven forecasting tools that apply transparent methodologies across thousands of matches annually. However, not all prediction platforms offer genuine analytical value. Key differentiators include the clarity of their analytical framework, the consistency of their approach across different leagues, and their honest acknowledgment of uncertainty — qualities that distinguish serious forecasting tools from entertainment-oriented content.

One resource that attempts to provide this structured approach is the [football predictions site footyprediction.com](https://footyprediction.com/). The platform generates forecasts using a multi-factor analytical process: recent team form (results, goal trends, defensive stability), head-to-head historical patterns, home and away performance differentials, and contextual elements such as scheduling density, player availability, and match importance. Bookmaker odds are incorporated as a secondary reference to identify potential market value rather than as primary predictors. This layered methodology allows users to understand why a particular forecast is made, promoting independent judgment rather than passive acceptance of final tips. From a professional standpoint, the emphasis on replicability and statistical grounding aligns with best practices in sports analytics. The platform covers a wide range of competitions — from major European leagues to secondary tournaments — applying consistent evaluation criteria across diverse match types.

No forecasting system can eliminate football's inherent unpredictability. Refereeing decisions, in-game injuries, weather conditions, and unexpected tactical changes regularly overturn even the most carefully calibrated probability models. Professional users of platforms like football predictions site footyprediction.com therefore treat their outputs as informed guidance rather than definitive answers. The most effective approach combines structured predictions with personal judgment, disciplined bankroll management, and a clear understanding that each bet carries residual risk. As the volume of football competitions continues to expand — with domestic schedules, European tournaments, and events like the 2026 World Cup creating a near-constant flow of fixtures — the demand for transparent, data-driven forecasting tools is likely to grow. Platforms that prioritize methodological honesty, consistency across leagues, and clear communication of uncertainty will remain valuable resources for analysts and bettors seeking defensible baselines for their decisions.

transformed\\.title: Beyond Hard Work
transformed\\.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXr71dqTK65wVM5zTuCxQrV1nKcvLL5rSSEsewnQ6KnBD/img_0159.jpg)
It is important to know that life does not promise anybody anything. There is no guarantee that you will make it even when you try your best, and there is also no guarantee that you will fail if you try. There is no specific manual for living this life; we are all simply trying to survive and find our way. Most times, we learn from people who are ahead of us and have experienced life more deeply, often following in their footsteps. At other times, we choose a different path and learn along the way.

I watched a clip online yesterday where someone talked about how our background is a major determining factor in our success and how far we go in life. He explained that being hardworking alone is not enough because a person can work hard and still lack the opportunities needed to move forward in life.

He recounted how, despite being a brilliant student who came first on several occasions, he still struggled with depression. He also spoke about meeting someone they attended primary school with who was not even among the top ten students but eventually became the head of one of the largest financial institutions in the UK.

In all honesty, our background matters, and it often influences our decisions and what we eventually get out of life. Imagine being hardworking while also having the necessary support system; you would understand how much easier it becomes for things to work out well for you.

Now consider someone who is hardworking but lacks any support system. You would realise that, by the time such a person struggles for funds, supports themselves, and searches for opportunities, a lot of time may already be gone. In the end, the person may have to look for a job or create opportunities independently. It is not always easy for someone who only has hard work to rely on. It takes a great deal of patience, resilience, and dedication to succeed under such circumstances.

Another factor is where you come from. Many people from African nations, especially those from less privileged backgrounds, find it difficult to achieve their dreams because they spend most of their time struggling to survive.

Imagine someone who needs to travel abroad for a course but lacks the necessary support system; such a person will likely find it difficult to make it happen. If we did not have the right background growing up, it is important that we become the support system and foundation for our own children. We cannot continue blaming our parents for not doing enough because they, too, may not have had the support or opportunities they needed.

I did the trip from Nice to Ventimiglia on a bike. The ride to Ventimiglia was quite pleasant.

This was back in the 1990s on a Sunday. I discovered that the restaurants and motels wouldn't take my credit card or other forms of money. 

So, I didn't get to eat.

Anyway, I decided to take a side road back to Nice through the mountains.

I discovered that the Alps are very steep. 

I went up, up, up and up.

I found myself at a ski area that was a mile above sea level. There is a ski area in the mountains just north of Ventimiglia!!!

Did I mention I had no food? 

The restaurant at the ski area was closed, but I found a place that would sell me a bottle of wine.

I discovered that if you drink a bottle of wine after a long bike ride, the wine turns into energy. The ride back to sea level was extremely fast.

Bu, sonraki gönderileri paylaşmam konusunda bana ekstra motivasyon kaynağı oluşturuyor. Bunu yapmaktan keyif alıyorum ve düzenli şekilde bu toplulukta gönderi paylaşmamın nedeni bu._

I don't remember anything like it before. Because I live at a high altitude, we used to get a lot of snow, but I don't remember this much rain before. Records are being broken in terms of rainfall. transformed\\.title: You Become Truly Unbreakable When You Master Just Three Things
transformed\\.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXk2DXUYX18pd5M9rj9a7HkcxWzbGquiv5gj7ortSsBj8/1779804498425.jpg)


We live in a world that constantly demands our attention, tests our boundaries, and tries to define who we are. If you don't have a firm grip on your own inner compass, it is incredibly easy to lose your peace to the chaos around you.

True resilience isn't about being loud, aggressive, or flawless. It is about building an internal fortress that no external storm can shake.

If you want to protect your peace, accelerate your growth, and preserve your character, there are three non negotiable principles you must master. When you truly understand them, you become difficult to break, difficult to manipulate, and impossible to forget.

**Know Your Worth - The Shield of Self Respect **

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdnZYYTLjK2Mi29y2cE8dQYmsLoC4MujVYtRXASYtDShq/1779804520303.jpg)

Confidence begins the moment you recognize who you are and what you carry within you. Your value is inherent. It does not decrease based on someone else’s inability to see it.

Too often, we waste precious energy trying to fit into spaces where we are merely tolerated instead of celebrated. We tweak our personalities, lower our standards, or beg for acceptance from people who lack the capacity to appreciate us.

**The Rule to Live By - **Never beg for a seat at a table where your value is ignored. Walking away from spaces that diminish you isn’t pride it is self preservation. When you know your worth, you stop asking for permission to shine, and you naturally attract the connections and opportunities that match your level.

**Control Your Emotions - The Anchor of Self Mastery**
Not every situation deserves a reaction. The world will constantly throw provocations, disrespect, and unexpected hurdles your way just to see how you respond. If you react to everything, you give away your power. You become easy to manipulate.

True strength is self control. A calm mind will always make better, sharper decisions than an angry heart. Controlling your emotions doesn’t mean you become numb or stop feeling things.it means you master the pause between a trigger and your response.

**The Rule to Live By - **Silence is often the loudest answer. When you refuse to trade your peace for someone else’s drama, you win. Let people think they’ve won the argument while you quietly preserve your mental clarity. Your energy is currency don't spend it on cheap provocations.

**Remain Humble - The Roots of Genuine Wisdom**
No matter how far life takes you, how much success you achieve, or how many goals you crush, stay grounded.


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmShWkPnjTVi3AKX2Q1b4CrSrKYZXgNQu74i1Zt1aPiVQ9/1779804557763.jpg)


Humility is often misunderstood as weakness or thinking less of yourself. In reality, true humility is simply \

. It is the realization that no matter how much you know, there is always more to learn. It is the understanding that success is a journey, and the ladders we climb are often held steady by the people around us.

**The Rule to Live By - **Humility keeps doors open, preserves wisdom, and earns genuine respect. The higher you climb, the deeper your roots need to be. When you approach life with an open heart and a teachable spirit, your character shines brighter than any resume ever could.


**In conclusion - The Unstoppable Trio**
When you bring these three principles together, something incredible happens.
 ●Your worth sets the standard for how you treat yourself.
 ●Your emotional control dictates how you allow the world to treat you.
 ●Your humility ensures you treat others with grace.

By mastering this balance, you create a life that is stable, purposeful, and deeply peaceful. You become a person who can move through any storm with your head held high and your character intact.

transformed\\.body:
Greetings Fabulous Felines and Hoomans of Hivelandia and surrounding communities!

I hope this new week is treating you well so far, and that you had an excellent holiday weekend!

![CC0000-TinyShadow2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/curatorcat/243zdUPngYKASBBEyPffcTrzvAyRC3jt7tbFgBFRbzRncP3XyMpgo9NHiijcVmvv7VMLd.jpg)
*Curator Cat as a tiny kitten, right after arriving at his \

*

Today — May 26th — is a very special day around here, because it marks the 10th anniversary of my Hoomans adopting this tiny,  scrawny black kitten with the excessively large ears from the local animal shelter!

It was actually the Daughter-Hooman who spotted me at the back of one of the enclosures, saying *\

* So, we dug up some kitten pictures from 10 years ago, for the occasion!

![CC0000-TinyShadow.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/curatorcat/242Y7We212mzHgN1gctuN5Wa7NCpX6vVaKWrnteiV8nMumwSTCRJTiVQQGc8DjHJy6Xck.jpg)
*Tiny Shadow enjoying the sunshine for the first time after the animal shelter!*

The Hoomans chose me immediately because they knew that black cats tend to be the *last* ones to be adopted, mostly because of old superstitions.

Of course, these are nonsense, and we all know that black cats make very loving and loyal feline companions!

![CC0002-SteepShot01-Kitten.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/curatorcat/23ywyUaLqHhcBWUX75C1RvGKRk5PXcLG8n31TR73uEbLakNG3yEK8KQp9oRGLUceFLeHg.jpg)
*Climbing the sofa and exploring my new surroundings!*

As far as the Hoomans are concerned, we all *\

* and everyone feels grateful and happy that we have gotten to share our lives.

Along the way, I have gotten to know other animal companions no longer with us, like BeBe and Kramer, and Daisy the dog... and new ones have joined us, like Smudge, Shangri and Nala.

![CC0012-ShadowSun.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/curatorcat/23yJJTMJvmJCn6eocq6yrFGJGaR3smuHpxBZNKfL3ogPuoNNYJVCVZcWLcZMNSmEoiTDX.jpg)
*Kitten in the sun!*

It's interesting to consider that we have been publishing the \

blog for the majority of my life — it has been over eight years, now!

Hopefully, we'll keep going for many more years to come!

![CC0714-PinkRoomShadow.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/curatorcat/23xyUoaiiEwtY3PCn8XHym6oLb126B5uijrqJrAYXRZhSqvBN2eiuwhPAivsvjUfpVm6G.jpg)
*10 years later: A pampered and spoiled house cat, living his best life!*

Thanks for stopping by to visit our little cat blog... we hope to see you again soon!

In the meantime, have a wonderful week!

![CC0000-AI-Free.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/curatorcat/23wqZfkRC9Jh5ik8xPCQA75bg6ezLJfhLUB7G1zH17zWy9DZMCpSZkhaUdvZzN4KZXBu2.jpg)

![HC0000CatHeader4.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/curatorcat/R9AOgdjq-HC0000-CatHeader4.jpg)

## *Love Cats? Get Involved in Hive's Cat Communities!*

If you're a cat lover and often/sometimes post pictures or other content that includes your feline friends, why not become an active part of Hive's growing Cat Communities?

These are some of the more active Cat Communities — why not join them ALL? Many of the allow you to share your cat posts, even if you started at a different community!

**[HiveCats](https://peakd.com/c/hive-189742/created)** by **@curatorcat** is a central *\

There *are* a number of other feline communities listed on Hive, but I am not sharing them for now as they have *not* had any activity (by their Admins OR users) since the Steem/Hive fork. Updates as they become available!

transformed\\.title: Consistency Becomes Difficult Without Power Supply
transformed\\.body: Every morning we hope for good things, and we pray to God for a better life, hoping that good fortune will come our way. As we hope for things like this to happen, we also try to work very diligently because that is one of the top priorities as humans. Doing things that we are supposed to do as and when they are due and not doing what is right at the wrong time. Thinking about doing something like this comes with a lot of diligence and dedication because you have to think and also rethink before you do anything.\n\n
alt=\

>


As we step into every new month of the year and the year is counting, we have hope that everything we do will work out for us because that is the hope and belief we carry about. Sometimes it is not how far but how well and how consistent we can keep our track record about things we do every day. Thinking about being consistent, a lot of factors can add up to making someone inconsistent in everything we do, and part of it is the environmental factors, biological factors, and so many others. But today I will be going deep on the environmental factor because it is what we mostly face as humans.

One of the environmental factors is light and access to a good internet connection. Alot of things can contribute to this to make one inconsistent regardless of what we are doing and where we might be. Now talking about electricity, it has now been said and proven that electricity is one of the big criterias that can help one's success. Imagine living in a place where your work is almost something that requires light and there is no light where you live. How do you cope with that.

Ordinary it will make you useless, and you will feel you are not doing what you are supposed to do. This is not always the case because if you look deeply, you will see a lot of reasons that will make you want to stand and fight, but when it comes to power sources, there is nothing one can do about it because it is beyond us. That brings me back to when I was still staying in the student areas where I went for my university degree. We almost had 18 hours of nonstop electricity supply, and then I was making good use of it because I can just sit back and watch the light go to waste, so I ensure that I get my devices charged, and I learn every day.

But now the reverse is the case, especially since I moved to some place in the downtown. Originally I was not supposed to rent the apartment, but due to some reason that I feel might still work. I relocated, and eventually when I got there, it was another story entirely because we hardly use electricity for 30 minutes, and you just have to rush things when you see the light. Another annoying part is that when the light comes and doesn't last for 30 minutes, it might be about 2 weeks before it will come like that again. This will make one frustrated and just lay around because there is nothing one will be able to do at that point. Now, since the world is evolving to use solar power sources, I think I might eventually switch to one, when I have the ability to do that.

links.title: Carbyne and Comtech: Taking the next generation of Emergency Communication
links.body:
The old methods of emergency communication by phone or Radio dispatch have been reaching their end. In today's environment, public safety agencies rely on cloud-based platforms that provide up-to-the-minute information and mobile access and smart infrastructure to better and faster respond when disaster strikes. This change is being driven by several technology firms, like[ Carbyne](https://nga911.com/) and Comtech, that are offering state-of-the-art communication networks and the latest technology in the area of response.

With the emergence of more complex emergencies and cities becoming increasingly connected, resilient communications are becoming a critical element of the public security infrastructure.

The need for Emergency Communication Systems to change.The reasons behind the changes in Emergency Communication Systems.

Emergency response techniques were built on the basis of landline telephony networks. They were good for a long time but it's not that they were created to fit modern demand of communication.

People nowadays mainly contact emergency services with the help of devices such as telephones, devices linked to the internet, or platforms on the internet. In many instances emergency responders require more than just voice communications to take rapid decisions.

Modern emergency systems support:

Global positioning system (GPS) tracking of location.

Emergency services via text

Multimedia sharing

Cloud-based dispatch coordination

Cross-agency communications

Real-time data updates

This has resulted in a demand for companies able to contribute to the development of scalable and flexible infrastructures of communication.

How Carbyne is modernizing Emergency Response

Carbyne concentrates on cloud-based emergency communication solutions to enhance the way emergency facilities manage and collect information.

The greatest problem in an emergency is getting the right information in a timely manner. The caller may not be able to correctly identify the location, especially when they are in a stressful or risky situation.

Advanced communication systems can help to automatically provide:

Device location data

Live caller updates

The ability to broadcast video.

Improved situational awareness

More speedy incident verification.

For example, when there is an emergency medical situation on the road, dispatchers can be able to find accurate GPS data immediately rather than waiting for an anxious caller to verbally give them the data. This will speed up the time to respond and enhance coordination.

Comtech's contribution to Critical Communication Infrastructure.Comtech's involvement with Critical Communication Infrastructure.

Comtech is involved with communications infrastructure and network technologies that aid both commercial and government operations.

When infrastructure is unreliable, it is important when:

Natural disasters

Large-scale public occasions

Regional outages

Evacuations for emergencies

High-volume communication periods

Emergency systems should continue to function regardless of network stress. A strong infrastructure allows for continuous communications between the dispatch center, first responders and other public agencies.

Infrastructure providers contribute towards enhancing the following:

Satellite communication reliability

Secure network transmission

Communication redundancy

Remote connection

Scalable emergency networks

Even the most advanced emergency software systems can fail during critical situations when the infrastructure is not reliable or a secure network.

Cloud-based emergency platforms offer a variety of advantages.Cloud-based emergency platforms have a number of benefits.

The cloud technology has revolutionized the way Emergency communication devices are used and maintained.

The older ones were generally based on the hardware installed in an emergency center that had been a single. This approach was non-flexible and could be prone to failure of equipment.

Cloud-based systems offer agencies the ability to:

Rapidly expand operations

Distribute data to several places

Expand backup & recovery capability

Remote dispatch support

Minimize complexity of maintenance

Cloud-based communications tend to make businesses more resilient in case of any emergency.

This has enabled companies such as Carbyne to stand out from the crowd and make a difference with public safety agencies, helping to modernize their old systems.

The need for cyber security is growing.Cyber security is becoming critical.

The more the communication networks are interconnected, security has become a prime concern.

The emergency communications networks usually have sensitive data, including:

Caller identities

Medical information

Incident reports

A record of government communications

Real-time operational systems

Cyberattacks that cause disruption can interfere with the emergency response in critical times.

Infrastructure businesses and technology vendors are turning more and more to:

Communication encrypted

Threat detection systems

Cloud environments that are secure

Multi-layer authentication

Network monitoring

In today's world, cybersecurity planning is no longer treated as a technical or other type of problem.Today, cybersecurity planning is considered a part of emergency preparedness and not as a problem of a different technical nature.

The impact of the real world on emergency response.

In real-world scenarios, modern technology in communication can greatly improve emergency situation coordination.

Suppose that a significant weather event has an impact on several communities at once. Thousands of calls may come in to an emergency centre in minutes. The intelligent routing systems are helpful in prioritizing important events and distributing the work-loads between various teams.

In the same way, people who respond to wildfire evacuations or highway accidents will benefit from the more timely exchange of information between agencies.

Although technology can't take the place of emergency personnel trained, it does help emergency personnel make quicker and more informed decisions when using communication tools.

Issues with modernizing public safety systems.

Despite significant technological advancements Many agencies have challenges when it comes to upgrading their communication systems.

Common problems are:

Budget limitations

Legacy infrastructure compatibility

Training of staff is a requirement

Failure to connect in rural areas

Long procurement processes

Generally, modernization is an evolutionary process rather than an outright process of replacement. Public safety agencies must be able to strike a balance between being innovative and safe.

Innovation is only as important as trust and stability within a company, like Comtech or Carbyne.

How the Future can look

Emergency communication systems will undergo a transformation as AI (Artificial Intelligence), connected infrastructure and \

technology improve.

Possible enhancements include:

AI-assisted dispatch analysis

Tools to predict emergencies in response to specific weather events.

Automated traffic routing for emergency responders.

Wearable emergency alerts for integration in the wearable

Airborne situational monitoring employing drones.

The more these technologies are embraced, the more important the communication infrastructure providers and companies will be to the improvement of public safety, providing emergency technology.

Final Thoughts

The success of emergency response heavily depends on the information's accuracy and reliability, good communication systems and the quickness of coordination between various agencies. The transformation towards more intelligent, connected public security systems is reflected in companies such as Carbyne and [Comtech](https://nga911.com/).

As emergency communication evolves The goal is clear to assist responders in their ability to act faster, communicate better and help communities better in critical situations.


---

မတိုက်ကြဘူး။ ထိုအခါ အမေက ရီမောကာ
အိမ်တိုင်းက လက်ဘက်ရည်တိုက်ကြသားပဲ
မင်းမှ မသောက်ပဲနဲ့။ အမေ မညာနဲ့နော် အမေ့
သူငယ်ချင်းအိမ်တွေက တအိမ်မှ လက်ဘက်ရည်
မတိုက်ကြဘူး။ ရော ခက်တော့နေပြီး နင့်ရှေ့က
အကြမ်းပန်ကန်တွေနဲ့ ချပေးတာ အဲ့တာ တိုက်လိုက်
တာပဲလေ။ 


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdgffQHvJ7muTmh2NywXiaFr3W2rb1N8pEvwgv5gtN5FC/1779867483145.jpg)

ဟင်း သူရို့တိုက်တာက ရေနွေးကြမ်းတွေလေ။
ဘယ်မှာလဲ လက်ဘက်ရည် မတွေ့ပါဘူး။ နို့ဆီလည်း
မပါဘူး လက်ဘက်ရည်အရောင်လည်းမဟုတ်ဘူး။
အမေ့က ကျွန်တော်ပြောသည်ကို ဆက်လက်ရီ‌မော
ပြီး။ ငါတို့ရွာက လက်ဘက်ရည်က အဲ့သလိုဟာပဲလေ။
ဧည့်သည်လာရင် လက်ဘက်ရည်သောက် ကြွပါအုံးလို့
ခေါ်ကြ ပြောကြတာ။ ကျွန်တော်က မကျေမနပ်ဖြင့်
အမေ့ကို ပြန်ပြာမိသည်။ ဒါဆိုလည်း အစကတည်းက
ရေနွေးကြမ်းသောက် ကြွကြပါလို့ ပြောပေါ့။
ခုတော့ လက်ဘက်ရည်တဲ့ ကျွန်တော်တို့ မြို့က
လက်ဘက်ရည်လို့လည်း မဟုတ်ပဲ လိမ်ညာပြောပြီး
ခေါ်တာ။ 


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPAEWPjAuD2VqKcfsmdzva4oPP6oQ3Ko3r1g1VTN6nGtb/1779867503154.jpg)

ယခုတော့ မြို့က လက်ဘက်ရည်ဆိုတာကြီးကို
မသောက်ရတာ အတော်ကြာပါပြီ။ အမေ့ရွာက
လက်ဘက်ရည်နဲ့ နှစ်ပါးသွားနေရတာ ကြာပေါ့။
အခုတော့ အမေ့ရွာ လက်ဘက်ရည်ကသာ
ကျန်းမာရေးအတွက် အဆင်ပြေပေသည်။
မြို့က လက်ဘက်ရည်များက အခုအခါမှာတော့
နို့ဆီများက အရည်အသွေးမပြည့်မှီသမို့ သောက်ပြီး
သည့်အခါတိုင်း ရင်ကြပ်ချင်သလို၊ ချောင်းဆိုးချင်
သလိုဖြစ်နေရသည်။ အရည်အသွေးပြည့်သော
လက်ဘက်ရည်ဆိုင်ကြီးများကိုလည်း ခြေဦးမလှည့်
ရဲသေးသမို့ မြို့က လက်ဘက်ရည်ရေ နေနှင့် ပါအုံး
ဆိုသလို။ နေနှင့်အုံးဟုသာ ပြောရသည်။
လက်ဘက်ရည်ကျကျလေး သောက်ပြီးတိုင်း
လူက လေ ထ ချင်နေမိသည်။ အသက်က
လက်ဘက်ရည်အကျကိုတောင် စကားပြောချင်
လာတော့သည်။ 

@htwegyi
May 27, 2026

links.title: In a few steps, from France to Italy
links.body:
*They say that every journey of 1000 miles begins with a single step.*

That's how my walk started this Wednesday.

At the train station in Nice, I stepped onto the platform into a carriage of a train bound for Ventimiglia, a small town on the border of France and Italy. 
When the train stopped at the platform, I got out of the French composition and moved into the carriage Italian compositions by TrenItalia.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYBXDXNDhQowF5P2Cx46Js2Z2qXoodEizYNhBjueZZi8v/1779831572457.jpg)

And in less than 20 minutes of driving, when the train stopped at the first station, I found myself in San Remo.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcABKCx54SZNCM39AvpxjVopfHaBAHNRdMDjCmUaXtAcs/1779820179398.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcMaUK3yoq7knwLpLFkbCiQv3PY3En57HGvfuRtn9VcCw/1779820425770.jpg)

San Remo, although it is located on the same coast of the Mediterranean Sea as the French cities: Cannes, Nice, Monaco (cities that are the top destinations of the Cote d'Azur), is the first Italian city when you go east from France and it is not located on the Cote d'Azur (as the French call it), but on the western part of the Ligurian Riviera, which is called the Riviera dei Fiori, as the Italians call it.

At first it was not clear to me why the riviera of flowers was mentioned, but given the number of *bird of paradise* flowers (strelitzia reginae) that are found at every step, it became clear to me.


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmU1RUWt4EEaRfjpS3M6fyzXXius3pkv3c5ibvL7W6kQvJ/1779829761599.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXSohdDSJFQndZv5MdhTewCFT2fsrN1qWYWAbth3zcM2K/1779829761660.jpg)

However, I didn't come to San Remo to see and smell the flowers. 
Although I would have liked that too, if I had a little more time and the sky was a little less gray.

So, on a cloudy day, from the train station, we headed to the old part of the city.

The wide streets that make up the pedestrian zone of this carnival city.
 *Here I mean the music festival in San Remo, which is traditionally held in San Remo during February, and which served as the inspiration for the Eurovision song. It is interesting that at the festival in San Remo, which is the oldest and most prestigious music festival in Europe, well-known and lesser-known Italian singers participate who perform songs that have not participated in competitions until that moment, and the winner of the festival in San Remo goes to the Eurovision Song Contest as Italy's representative.*

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVeYYqU2yJerQ5GPC2Zy62o8gFDv8kyuBwcmwUENpkDvr/1779820486508.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVUW2LAXcB29iQ9EWbLPcyMzBpkvV9nK9jRQ9huQF2BYT/1779820561748.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbWQ2DgzcTW4evLwHysTvQEYxaWxwr9pZcT7HmFMV2731/1779820561925.jpg)

On those five evenings in February, these streets are in a festival mood, much more lively than they are this Wednesday, after the rain that wets the streets.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSXLXXcsXeAHKFd91EzFZVqodEvboFeNRvUEP13gwXoar/1779820617274.jpg)

From the pedestrian zone, we head uphill towards the Concattedrale di San Siro, but as the cathedral is closed and we are slightly wet, we decide to shorten the walk and pay attention to these narrow streets with arches.


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUjNDkTb9yJvdkV8MFPFUFWk7vY777UYi4MXioHEgnGgn/1779830166293.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdDXfBnJUyN7cRiwPn1HZjEB4oDTCSUghFAUvtUJibqaA/1779820629921.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRbK9kEVufTebHR7LKxK7YhrbiVr4uLy2PUGodGNi4ku3/1779830254268.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmR1YxL2YfbxSYeYUU6cubgukbBPAF8ToXgJ5Vz2NdfpM3/1779830254340.jpg)

How narrow the streets are, in order to see their height, each of the photos had to be upright.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQc5bkJ2DE1vBTTcWxkTPZUH2jegR2MuVGSyU4r8fPATd/1779820647129.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmR6Aa3BaHv1dkvKXJPAYBdXeWsrfCGVeVcLNMnJ9G36Mq/1779820647204.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWYcanaGYq2hKihxnPENN91XH92P3Wdp1vY2rDx6j7ZTw/1779820647261.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTYYWAZo8r67Y34d6RpmUbxaSodPWY9rATF3ni9K53XSS/1779820647329.jpg)

Hundreds of narrow passages, steep stone staircases, passages between buildings, as if through some tunnels, yes a lot of gates, marked my walk in the old part of San Remo.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQ6kAkcPwT92EvwdzNtsGXkwakn4Bu3pyZGMzDKSHuVWZ/1779830959859.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRKwZDTPtnLkdPMn7M7yfabzY1Y2PAUoAqDWSHRCgTgnS/1779830959933.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmeYmAytdQnkvBnxdf4BLQuFppBdrrkTXMJGwJHHUkhVVq/1779830960003.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmV3nYRThF2epWdKgodsMb9xaiCSiZQTASaqL93TeoE8Dk/1779820647402.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQ6Lbk47RUmTCdL7YV9KBzNzDQcg5VCUSty9hoFQbSUgH/1779820661647.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbVnh1PQpPaTbpSZZPNQtwLvipvTeJhaM7ptP9dwBkVVA/1779820661746.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXkSgJqqR4jDVZVF5as5Xb3XR4pS6q17NbVbLvfUFHhKt/1779830579693.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWhrMBp6ys8LhLy6jBepBHXs29AMpwyqXcpwTwpawP37t/1779820712499.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZT7gFK53ACwnVBR1PGLDCYtud6At18oF2qZB32WA8qwQ/1779820712665.jpg)

It was much nicer to walk in the flat part of the city, when we went out to the promenade and reached the famous Russian Orthodox Church of Christ the Savior, St. Seraphim of Sarov and St. Catherine.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRZJaQ3pBGtpK7Yu2ctM8Z4xtz49AupMRm18QD95Sewn9/1779831235859.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQcJkJMsGB7m9PJyiPnf9oCHJChrpokAVfSct87qo57XL/1779831235966.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmR23avBr7s5KRXWMLjD9hxaCTgpRqEwYBRd2EeqWLySxN/1779820861265.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXdMa7XvWuZ7f1BnW1pv72Y2bdr7HeLNgESt2jmDfkVmi/1779820861327.jpg)

In the courtyard of the church, two monuments of historical figures known to me, Vittorio Emanuele III and Elena di Montenegro.

Vittorio Emanuele III was the grandson of Vittorio Emanuele II (after whom the famous shopping center in Milan is named) and the last Italian king.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmeYhTHLaBhBy5UhWrgQGmFcds5L4GnoDrMzgd4pSEKPhx/1779820899132.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVTEjmvK2Y2FKFdXoarHrjwpj1hDKJD8Hmjb6ug1wNpuF/1779820899214.jpg)

Not far from the Russian church is the Hotel de Paris, across the street, the Lolli Palace Hotel, as well as the famous Casino San Remo.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbG2YemvrVSHxZm1YgCXeH4mhPXksc9eaiWbsFkWm1N4i/1779830693064.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWmEm7KMDeBzbCGsyYPeyWdJCVj1S1TayBGa16vaDKST8/1779830693144.jpg)

Lest we come to a city on the sea without seeing the sea, we went ashore, but there was nothing to see there. Cloudy, gray, not nice...

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXG2uf5JofRH1KWwYmZBZJbkXcFwx5SnHpZWaRcKGs4nD/1779830705687.jpg)

We continued to Forte di Santa Tecla, however, to my regret, the fortress is under reconstruction.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmfQ8N4731Qi9Dsr3A9xFRbE4dM27aZn7f54wia57crBB1/1779830728625.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSX7U37zYLxbPJAHj8xV5ngitu12XWhNcw5emrGuUvVc5/1779830728743.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVsdBw9QAyDquA7Df1wYU65x279aQY8ayc14shKSorfgm/1779830728824.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSwghvUUeTEX5StvLL1zLvTvNHWLaw8N3bhkCx61frxtt/1779830728900.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYa35qXTDbrh1EBajv4sVvSa2B51JeSC9UPNoMoX93sxT/1779830728964.jpg)

I went around her as much as possible, and we headed for the marina.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcR4WC7h1sVoMRAXXa8ciL1KadCFLkGoktviYRKLDUeYX/1779830753924.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPBmQy3srdntbVfXC9jxnZ9nhDY9N8mjqkZrRz4YC6QSr/1779830754040.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmavojTvgc6wjQPjCmomfEMaeUvmyoXMymjsTfPLd7DF2i/1779830766869.jpg)


The marina is far \

than those in Monaco and Nice (with those luxurious, expensive yachts), but that's why the buildings across the street from the marina (the low ones where there are restaurants with seafood specialties) are phenomenal.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcco7njJfUjcBRLiUVidDMeSSEaSaSm4TuoPAkw7BxhKH/1779830790657.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUeFkBNPNLwzyqEh11As92EtDrWLoaMpc9kZJQKa6e2ui/1779830812347.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSNq2KWx21P38Z7mdjEBNt18PEAm1vJpEMuqovSXfEuDp/1779830812425.jpg)

I can only imagine the contrast of their pastel facades against the blue sky.

Here, too, you can see some luxury cars on the streets, and the number of small scooters is fascinating.
There are them at every corner.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPMgQGqDQFpyQMXaEMA94pL85EfrTVZGXj8nTY83yYFm2/1779830827972.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmThujqHyg8BPXePNL666rYPXuV7vky9WMaXrt9vjmJsMv/1779830828029.jpg)

We didn't sit down for lunch, but on our way to a pastry shop where we wanted to eat ice cream, entered the Cathedral of Santa Maria degli Angeli, which had its doors open for visitors, and took a short break there.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSwq3U8hrpaQiNzYDt11rgX1HzuHyb3A4xwcAfCGM7tEJ/1779830892566.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPoGg5h4vyhXWXNADncxMqpfKZgYHLYGwT8rmctCG9nn6/1779830892669.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmaAvASAchiBEsG8jF5B1z8cAC3wES8XhuxTxdZMy3niL5/1779830867450.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQL7wRMGCfN1tHq9ijXdiX4U9DoScAA2ALSNapQw36yXE/1779830867523.jpg)

As a reward for the many steps taken on this #wednesdaywalk, we treated ourselves to ice cream from the GROM patisserie, which I would recommend to anyone visiting San Remo.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVGedLT48N1QjJuAqTz5nBEAUfwPg5wuPEcBHKdYL5ADk/1779831035071.jpg)

Is it because I ate it in Italy that I liked this ice cream a lot. I regret not taking pictures of the combinations chosen by my companions on this walk, it would have made a nice pictorial post for #IceCreamCreations.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRauai7ZY24HEui5bh862HhUDof4PauCsdDSvSVuWSQQo/1779831053768.jpg)

As it is, I only have pictures of my combination: hazelnut and strawberry.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmR8UehKfz8zA2tWGfD8SfBeWvmmHg9AkfDTUYwr6xdE5v/1779831084328.jpg)

After we ate ice cream and cooled down further, we headed to the train station, because we had to make a few more steps (or a few thousand steps), in Italy to the train, at the border to the platform, then again to the train, and from the platform to France.

links.title: University of the Philippines (UP), You Are the Dream I Had to Let Go
links.body: > **University of the Philippines (UP), You Are the Dream I Had to Let Go** ![1.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/khirstin/23wX7iZU75frvJhkXm8KfitM95gzCGgkTpxVFoi7ZQUtpN9JdWpSWagZECJV1poUrd28U.png) Have you ever made a decision that was so hard to make? I hate making difficult decisions, especially when they're about my future. I think this is the hardest decision I have ever made in my entire life. It really hurts to think that I declined an offer that I once prayed for. I really don't like it because in other people's view, when you go to UP, they immediately assume you'll become rebellious. Why is it like that? Can't someone who studies in UP just be a normal student? A lot of people want to pass UP, and I am one of them. Sadly, there are also many who are not allowed to study in UP because they say it will make them rebellious, and I am also one of them. **Where My UP Dream Began** ![2.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/khirstin/23wqu3HxUyP9LCf8ABjCYyjCFD33My6LFZMgFwAgdntqm47M9km4Uttzs525iEKj7y75R.png) My dream of studying in UP started in Grade 11. Actually, before Grade 11, I really didn't care much about college because I was still very undecided. In Grade 11, I joined my first and last contest in high school, and it was held at University of the Philippines Cebu. That's where I saw UP students enjoying their life, and I really liked the campus because of its nature vibes, unlike other universities where you mostly just see buildings everywhere. At that time, I promised myself that if I ever apply UP Cebu, I would take BS Math, because the contest I joined at UP Cebu was the Philippine Mathematical Olympiad, and it made me realize how much I enjoy solving challenging math problems and how I wanted to improve in that field. **The Reality of Applying for College** ![3.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/khirstin/23viAhXAor7TfNYnmax8nYTuWcJGwSjuirYCzgwAEA6jxxVWCwDdv7ep3N1wzQQrewwP4.png) When I applied to University of the Philippines Cebu, I hadn't asked my parents yet because I was unsure if they would allow me. I just randomly chose my programs. In UP Cebu, my first choice was BS Math, and I also randomly picked the next up to the fourth choice. In UP Diliman, I applied for BS Chemical Engineering because that's really my dream program. It was actually the first university I ever applied to, and it made me realize how scary it is to apply for universities, especially when you know you might not be allowed to pursue your dream program. **UPCAT Experience** ![4.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/khirstin/23xeos5xccZjWHXiMHS2265zPWYGA9PmcKDCynhVWiEMVcvUyFzz3VFZY1N8nJXJKeL5V.png) I took the UP College Admission Test(UPCAT) last August 3, and since my birthday is August 1, I really wished that I would pass. But at that time, I only studied the reviewer they gave at the last minute. I also followed some superstitions, like not taking a picture with the UP Oblation. For me, the exam was around 5/10 in difficulty. The hardest part was science. While taking the test, I even found myself laughing because there were some random and funny questions, you’ll really wonder why they were included in the first place. **Results** ![5.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/khirstin/23viGnUh5S5K5r2HdqKUmX5xtnCn12X4diMqeemCrFpVWX56rKKQn3FQqHC9xwudyupLk.png) Now that the results are out, I initially passed as waitlisted. I accepted the waitlist offer, and then I received an email saying I officially passed. I just ended up crying because it hurts so much knowing I had to decline it, even though UP is really my dream, no matter what program, as long as it’s UP. When I shared it with my parents, I was almost crying too because they still won’t allow me, saying I might become rebellious. I’m actually crying while writing this. I hate letting go. I hate that feeling so much, and now I'm actually experiencing it in real life. It's different when you just think about it, but it hurts even more when you’re already in the situation where you have to choose between holding on to your dream or accepting reality. **UP, you were once a dream, and now you are the dream that I had to let go.**

links.title: 📷 3 Panama City Skyscrapers – 3 Fine Art Edits [EN/DE]
links.body:
![Unbenannt-1.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/travelshots/23tGXT2kFar5N2pKocfeHP4ZURRPxnY9WWqWSkEGN6VApEnReDQ9JpahsFN7M4FGbDAek.jpg)

As I had done in Glasgow, I once again turned my attention to my new focus in photography – fine art architecture in black and white – whilst in Panama City. Amongst the sea of skyscrapers in this Central American metropolis, three in particular stood out to me. I tried to highlight them in my photographs and later edited them using my new Photoshop workflow.

*Wie schon in Glasgow, habe ich mich auch auch in Panama City wieder mit meinem neuen Fokus in der Fotografie – Fine Art Architektur in Schwarzweiß – beschäftigt. Im Meer von Wolkenkratzern der zentralamerikanischen Metropole stachen für mich drei besonders hervor, die ich versuchte, fotografisch in Szene zu setzen und später mit meinem neuen Photoshop-Workflow zu bearbeiten.*

![_DSC0234-Bearbeitet.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/travelshots/23tRxieCDJUL3e4brQQJDxRNC76o4YLVDA75zEaT1tgA9NQ8tBHcB3rkMHPCYrw1SRpLm.jpg)

The Hi-Point Tower is a state-of-the-art commercial and office building. Thanks to its striking glass façade with floor-to-ceiling windows, the building offers the companies based there spectacular panoramic views of the sea (Panama Bay) and the city skyline. The building is highly regarded in the local property sector and has been honoured with, amongst other awards, the prestigious Magno MOA Architecture Prize (2018). 

*Der Hi-Point Tower ist ein ein modernes Gewerbe- und Bürogebäude der Spitzenklasse. Durch die markante Glasfassade mit bodentiefen Fenstern bietet das Gebäude den dort ansässigen Unternehmen spektakuläre Panoramaausblicke auf das Meer (die Bucht von Panama) und die Skyline der Stadt. Das Gebäude genießt in der lokalen Immobilienszene ein hohes Ansehen und wurde unter anderem mit dem renommierten Architekturpreis Magno MOA (2018) ausgezeichnet.*

![_DSC0285-Bearbeitetv2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/travelshots/23t76y4LiaEnYHncp56u8HxwdT1P6kRQEkYqRetYuWkgzaSr8pKnkTXDubsciWr19jMtu.jpg)

The F&F Tower is the city’s modern landmark and is famous worldwide for its extraordinary corkscrew design. It is therefore known to both locals and tourists – almost exclusively – as ‘El Tornillo’ (Spanish for ‘The Screw’). The tower rises an impressive 243 metres into the sky and was completed in 2011. Shortly afterwards, the building was voted one of the top 10 skyscrapers in the world (7th place) at the prestigious Emporis Skyscraper Awards.

*Der F&F Tower ist das moderne Wahrzeichen der Stadt und weltweit berühmt für sein außergewöhnliches Korkenzieher-Design. Er wird deshalb sowohl von Einheimischen als auch von Touristen – fast ausschließlich „El Tornillo“ (spanisch für Die Schraube) genannt. Der Turm ragt stolze 243 Meter in den Himmel und wurde 2011 fertiggestellt. Das Gebäude wurde kurz darauf beim renommierten Emporis Skyscraper Award unter die Top 10 der besten Wolkenkratzer der Welt gewählt (Platz 7).*

![_DSC0331-Bearbeitet.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/travelshots/23tbMB7Yj7m1t4s1eNP6ffhhcPEiU6WxNt29vEpAChtgWcrNJLTfMD2jmEMYe1LEXtCEp.jpg)

The Tower Financial Centre (often referred to as the TowerBank Financial Centre) is another architectural giant in Panama City. The 231-metre-high tower is entirely clad in a deep black aluminium and reflective glass façade. Depending on the position of the sun, the building appears either deep black or dark blue-metallic. As the name suggests, it is the financial heart of the Campo Alegre district. The main tenant and namesake is Towerbank, one of Panama’s best-known banks.

*Das Tower Financial Center (oft auch als TowerBank Financial Center bezeichnet) ist ein weiterer architektonischer Riese in Panama City. Der 231 Meter hohe Turm ist komplett mit einer tiefschwarzen Aluminium- und spiegelnden Glasfassade verkleidet. Je nach Sonnenstand wirkt das Gebäude dadurch tiefschwarz oder dunkelblau-metallisch. Wie der Name schon sagt, ist es das finanzielle Herzstück des Viertels Campo Alegre. Hauptmieter und Namensgeber ist die Towerbank, eine der bekanntesten Banken Panamas.*

See you soon!/*Bis bald!*
Stefan

links.title: El Diamante Negro que Cegó a las Grandes Ligas / The Black Diamond Who Blinded the Major Leagues
links.body: ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmd7DUdWS8BbEQfBdV55SUq5vK9DphPCNz87eReMd6E5Vd/img_20260525_164905_838.jpg)\n⚾ Español\nMucho antes de que las barreras raciales se rompieran oficialmente en el béisbol organizado, un lanzador cubano de contextura delgada pero con un brazo de trueno demostró que el talento no entiende de colores. Su nombre era José de la Caridad Méndez, conocido eternamente en la historia del deporte como \

.

Época y Recorrido por los Diamantes


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmewcb3WC5Ajoh9muUiyZtphf36XWwxxZKwxVxtgpv2pjn/img_20260525_164914_937.jpg)
Nacido en Cárdenas en 1885, Méndez desarrolló su carrera profesional entre 1907 y 1926. En Cuba, se convirtió en el ídolo indiscutible del legendario club Almendares (los Azules), aunque al final de su carrera también vistió las franelas del Santa Clara, Matanzas, Habana y Alacranes. En los Estados Unidos, al tener las puertas de la MLB cerradas por la segregación, brilló intensamente en los circuitos independientes y en las Ligas Negras. Transitó por los Cuban Stars, los Chicago American Giants, los Detroit Stars y alcanzó el clímax de su carrera con los Kansas City Monarchs, equipo donde fungió como mánager-jugador. 

Estadísticas, Premios y Contexto Histórico

Es vital para un historiador aclarar un punto: en la era en la que Méndez jugó, no existían los Guantes de Oro, los Bates de Plata ni los Juegos de Estrellas. Sin embargo, su dominio técnico fue tan abrumador que, de haber existido, su vitrina estaría abarrotada.
Méndez poseía un control quirúrgico y una recta indescifrable. En la Liga Cubana acumuló un récord de 76 victorias y 28 derrotas, dejando el promedio de ganados y perdidos más alto de la historia del circuito (.731). En su debut en las Ligas Negras reconocidas de forma oficial (1920-1926), registró una marca de 30-9 con una efectividad de 3.46, además de un impresionante récord como mánager de 196-100, ganando tres campeonatos consecutivos. 

La Hazaña Inmortal


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYeMo46thEUbQgTMBDCk1TJgLfWKBazk3Mz9tyoo9Cc1m/img_20260525_164909_139.jpg)
El año era 1908. El equipo de los Rojos de Cincinnati (MLB) visitó La Habana para una serie de exhibición contra el Almendares. Un joven Méndez saltó al box y propinó una blanqueada de solo un imparable. No contentos con el resultado, los norteamericanos volvieron a enfrentarlo en dos ocasiones más en los días siguientes. ¿El resultado final? Méndez les lanzó 25 entradas consecutivas sin permitir una sola carrera, propinando 24 ponches y tolerando apenas 8 hits en total. La prensa estadounidense de la época quedó atónita; el mánager de Cincinnati llegó a declarar que Méndez combinaba la velocidad de Walter Johnson con la inteligencia de Christy Mathewson. 

Una Anécdota de Puro Coraje

Hacia 1914, las lesiones graves en el brazo parecieron acabar con el \

como lanzador. Lejos de rendirse, Méndez se reinventó y continuó jugando al máximo nivel como campocorto y antesalista gracias a su tremendo atletismo. Sin embargo, su momento más cinematográfico ocurrió en la primera Serie Mundial Negra de 1924 dirigiendo a Kansas City. Con la serie empatada y a pesar de las estrictas advertencias del médico del equipo debido a sus dolores crónicos en el brazo, Méndez decidió abrir el decisivo décimo juego. No solo aguantó el dolor, sino que lanzó una blanqueada completa de 3 hits para darle el campeonato mundial a los Monarchs. 

Legado y Conclusión


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSJoJuiaJ5fkqaSbPW2Bt3VqPgeQbJWyr2hJTEUvCWCDp/img_20260525_164919_007.jpg)
José de la Caridad Méndez falleció prematuramente en 1928 a los 43 años, víctima de tuberculosis. Hoy en día es reverenciado como el pionero absoluto del pitcheo cubano a nivel internacional. Su legado se hizo eterno en 2006, cuando fue exaltado al Salón de la Fama de Cooperstown. 
Méndez no fue solo un atleta de élite; fue un símbolo cultural de resistencia que demostró, sobre el montículo, la calidad suprema de la pelota caribeña frente a los mejores exponentes de las Grandes Ligas.


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmd7DUdWS8BbEQfBdV55SUq5vK9DphPCNz87eReMd6E5Vd/img_20260525_164905_838.jpg)
⚾ English
Long before racial barriers were officially broken in organized baseball, a slender Cuban pitcher with a thunderous arm proved that talent knows no color. His name was José de la Caridad Méndez, eternally known in sports history as \

Era and Journey Through the Diamonds


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmewcb3WC5Ajoh9muUiyZtphf36XWwxxZKwxVxtgpv2pjn/img_20260525_164914_937.jpg)
Born in Cárdenas in 1885, Méndez developed his professional career between 1907 and 1926. In Cuba, he became the undisputed idol of the legendary Almendares club (the Blues), though late in his career he also wore the flannels of Santa Clara, Matanzas, Habana, and Alacranes. In the United States, with MLB doors closed due to segregation, he shone brightly in independent circuits and the Negro Leagues. He played for the Cuban Stars, the Chicago American Giants, the Detroit Stars, and reached the climax of his career with the Kansas City Monarchs, a team where he served as player-manager. 

Stats, Awards, and Historical Context

It is vital for a historian to clarify one major point: during the era in which Méndez played, Gold Gloves, Silver Sluggers, and All-Star Games did not exist. However, his technical dominance was so overwhelming that, had they existed, his trophy case would be overflowing.
Méndez possessed surgical control and an unreadable fastball. In the Cuban League, he accumulated a 76-28 record, leaving the highest career winning percentage in the history of the circuit (.731). In his officially recognized Negro League career (1920-1926), he posted a 30-9 record with a 3.46 ERA, alongside a staggering managerial record of 196-100, winning three consecutive pennants. 

The Immortal Feat


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYeMo46thEUbQgTMBDCk1TJgLfWKBazk3Mz9tyoo9Cc1m/img_20260525_164909_139.jpg)
The year was 1908. The MLB's Cincinnati Reds visited Havana for an exhibition series against Almendares. A young Méndez took the mound and fired a brilliant 1-hit shutout. Unsatisfied with the result, the Major Leaguers faced him twice more over the following days. The final result? Méndez hurled 25 consecutive scoreless innings against the big leaguers, striking out 24 and allowing just 8 total hits. The American press was stunned; the Reds' manager even stated that Méndez combined the velocity of Walter Johnson with the sheer wit of Christy Mathewson. 

An Anecdote of Pure Courage

By 1914, severe arm injuries seemed to end the \

pitching days. Far from giving up, Méndez reinvented himself and continued playing at the highest level as a shortstop and third baseman due to his incredible athleticism. However, his most cinematic moment occurred in the first 1924 Negro League World Series while managing Kansas City. With the series tied and despite strict warnings from the team doctor regarding his chronic arm pain, Méndez decided to start the decisive Game 10. He didn't just endure the pain—he threw a 3-hit complete game shutout to bring the world championship home to the Monarchs. 

Legacy and Conclusion


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSJoJuiaJ5fkqaSbPW2Bt3VqPgeQbJWyr2hJTEUvCWCDp/img_20260525_164919_007.jpg)
José de la Caridad Méndez passed away prematurely in 1928 at the age of 43, a victim of tuberculosis. Today, he is revered as the absolute pioneer of Cuban pitching on the international stage. His legacy was cemented in 2006 when he was posthumously inducted into the National Baseball Hall of Fame in Cooperstown. 
Méndez was not just an elite athlete; he was a cultural symbol of resilience who proved, right from the top of the mound, the supreme quality of Caribbean baseball against the finest icons of the Major Leagues.

links.body:
![image](https://pixabay.com/get/g14e8d989ec47e6d5ca91e661c0d1f2cb36cea76a6858fa18d6c81c3536e38b5d8058ec9ae149cb9b4675bc90b5174cee_640.jpg)
Hoy mi caminata fue realmente revitalizante. Empecé por un parque que suele estar lleno de gente y, como siempre, había un grupo de corredores entrenando para una maratón. Hablé brevemente con una chica que estaba en su segunda semana de entrenamiento; me contó que es su primer maratón y está muy emocionada. Es increíble ver a la gente tan motivada. Luego, pasé por un pequeño mercado al aire libre donde encontré a un anciano vendiendo miel artesanal. Me detuve a probarla y, mientras charlábamos, me contó sobre sus abejas y cómo ha estado cuidándolas durante más de 30 años. Su pasión es contagiosa y me hizo apreciar aún más lo que hay detrás de los productos locales. A lo largo del camino, el clima estaba perfecto, con un cielo despejado. Vi muchas flores en los jardines y un par de artistas pintando paisajes urbanos. Fue un recordatorio hermoso de la creatividad que puede encontrarse en la ciudad. En general, una caminata que no solo me ejercitó, sino que también me conectó con personas e historias inspiradoras. _This report was published via Actifit app ([Android](https://bit.ly/actifit-app) | [iOS](https://bit.ly/actifit-ios)). links.title: What Every Whisky Enthusiast Should Know Before Buying
links.body:
There’s something extremely satisfying in discovering a spirit which encourages curiosity, patience, and the desire to study. [Whisky made from single malt](https://www.paulsliquor.com.au/collections/whisky) has garnered a worldwide following, not due to marketing, but due to what’s actually inside the glass — personality, depth and a tale that is built on the art of. From the method by which grain is picked to the time spent maturing in wood, each bottle is a reflection of carefully considered decisions taken long before it reaches the consumer. Knowing what makes this particular category of whisky unique can be the initial step to enjoying it to the fullest, no matter if you’re sampling the first whisky you have ever had or your 50th.



![Single Malt Whisky 1.jpg](https://waivio.nyc3.digitaloceanspaces.com/68297991d39f492bb89b1077b739fd2af1b6df864257213f204869d5943e5a3c)



### Why the Production Process Makes All the Difference

The process of making whisky is a direct and significant impact on the final product on your table. Single malt is made by blending malted barley in an individual distillery, employing pot stills instead of column stills. This is a difference that affects the whisky’s texture and strength by creating a distinct texture and depth that is instantly evident to a keen drinker. Malted barley adds a natural sweetness in the spirit base and the pot still method keeps much of the barley’s natural characteristics compared to continuous distillation techniques. 

The oak casks that mature performs the heavy lifting over a period of time, sometimes for decades, bringing color flavor compounds, flavours, and a smoothness out of the wood, while softening the pure spirit. The type of cask that is used -whether it had previously was a storage vessel for sherry, bourbon port, or winewill leave an impression on the flavor. A bourbon barrel is likely to impart honey and vanilla notes and sherry cask includes dried fruit as well as nuts and warm spice. The understanding of this process allows drinkers to understand the taste of their drink and how it was created making each glass more intriguing.

### How to Read Flavour Profiles and Choose What Suits You

One of the biggest hurdles for those who are just beginning to drink is the terminology that whisky is described in. Words like “peaty,” “maritime,” “fruity,” or “floral” can feel abstract until you experience them for yourself but they have a very useful function. Peat, for example, refers to the earthy smokey flavor that is a result of drying malted barley in the presence of the burning peat in production. Distilleries using heavily peated malt create spirits that possess a strong and sometimes medicinal smokiness that is instantly identifiable. On the other side in the range, non-peated expressions of regions that are grain-forward can be delicate, sour and even honeyed. 

**Whisky single malt** tasting notes aren’t simply a form of marketing, they’re a description of what a bottle can actually taste like. Moreover, learning to interpret them correctly can save both cash and disappointment. Beginning with lighter, fruity expressions before moving on to heavy sherried or heavily peated area is a smart strategy which allows the palate to evolve gradually, rather than being overwhelmed.

### Building Knowledge and Confidence as a Whisky Drinker

To develop a genuine appreciation for whisky requires some time, but it’s an investment in time. The ability to taste a variety of styles regions, styles, and expressions can provide an inventory of mental references that make each new bottle easier to assess. Notes that are simple — perhaps an enumeration of what you have noticed keeps a track of what you’ve tasted and improves your palate memory as time passes. Whisky enthusiasts, both on the internet or in real life, can be among the most open and welcoming drinking cultures with people of all level eager to share information and recommendations, and sometimes the opportunity to pour. The independent bottlers worth investigating as they frequently offer limited releases from well-respected distilleries for a reasonable price that are of genuine quality, without the price tag associated with top-of-the-line releases. 

Age-related statements can be useful but shouldn’t be used as the only indicator of quality as an expression that has been well-crafted will always be superior to the older version that is not mature enough. If you’re a person who drinks with purpose and curiosity and looking into the ****[single-malt whisky](https://www.paulsliquor.com.au/collections/whisky) throughout its entire variety of styles, origins and production techniques is among the most enjoyable and rewarding trips one can go on as a spirit drinker.

---

[Posted](https://waivio.com/@waivio_paulsliquor/6wdzds-what-every-whisky-enthusiast-should-know-before-buying) by Waivio guest: [@waivio_paulsliquor](https://waivio.com/@waivio_paulsliquor)

links.body: />Hello Everyone! Hope you all are doing amazing and welcome to another #Splinterlands post. Today I wanted to do another card spotlight post and this time it is about Silverleaf Ranger. Honestly, this card feels kinda broken sometimes. At first I ignored this unit because there are already many ranged Life cards in #Splinterlands. But after using Silverleaf Ranger in alot of ranked battles, I realized this card can become an absolute monster if it survives for few rounds. Silverleaf Ranger is a Rare Life unit and at max level (Level 8) it gets access to 4 abilities which makes it both offensive and defensive at the same time. The artwork of this card also looks amazing. The elf archer design really fits the Life splinter style and the abilities make the card feel very unique compared to other ranged attackers. 𝐌𝐚𝐱 𝐋𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐥 𝐒𝐭𝐚𝐭𝐬 ============================ At level 8, Silverleaf Ranger has: * 4 Ranged Damage * 4 Speed * 3 Armor * 6 Health Those are honestly very solid stats for a ranged card. The speed is good, damage is scary, and with healing abilities it becomes very annoying to kill.

> 𝐀𝐛𝐢𝐥𝐢𝐭𝐲 𝟏: 𝐖𝐞𝐚𝐫𝐲 ============================= **Weary**: At the beginning of round 1, Weary units have a 10% chance to become Exhausted. This chance increases by 10% every round, up to a maximum of 80%. Exhausted units skip their turn.

> This is probably the weirdest ability on the card. At first, I honestly thought this ability was bad because your own unit can randomly skip turns. But after playing with it more, it actually creates alot of risky and fun situations. Sometimes Silverleaf Ranger keeps attacking for many rounds without getting exhausted at all. Other times it gets tired early and ruins your plan. So using this card always feels like gambling a little bit. But the good thing is that when the card DOES keep attacking, it becomes insanely strong because of its other abilities. 𝐀𝐛𝐢𝐥𝐢𝐭𝐲 𝟐: 𝐃𝐨𝐮𝐛𝐥𝐞 𝐒𝐭𝐫𝐢𝐤𝐞 ============================================ **Double Strike**: Attacks twice each turn.

> Now this is where things become crazy. 4 ranged damage attacking TWO times per turn can absolutely destroy enemy units very fast. If enemy armor is weak, Silverleaf Ranger melts through teams quickly. And if buffs are applied from summoners or support cards, the damage becomes even more scary. I had battles where this card almost solo carried because Double Strike kept deleting enemies every round. This is definitely the strongest part of the card in my opinion. 𝐀𝐛𝐢𝐥𝐢𝐭𝐲 𝟑: 𝐇𝐞𝐚𝐥 =========================== **Heal**: Each round, restores 1/3 of max health.

> This ability gives the card surprisingly good survivability. Most ranged units are easy to kill once enemy Sneak or Opportunity units reach them. But Heal helps Silverleaf Ranger survive longer than expected. And when a Double Strike unit keeps healing every round, it becomes super annoying for opponents. I think Heal is one of the reasons this card works really good in longer battles. 𝐀𝐛𝐢𝐥𝐢𝐭𝐲 𝟒: 𝐄𝐜𝐡𝐨 =========================== **Echo**: Active abilities trigger twice per round.

></center>

This is honestly one of the coolest abilities.

Since active abilities trigger twice, Heal becomes even stronger because it activates two times. That means Silverleaf Ranger can recover alot of health every round.

And combined with Double Strike, the card becomes a complete menace if left alive.

The synergy between Heal and Echo is actually insane.

I really like cards that combo abilities together and Silverleaf Ranger does that perfectly.

𝐂𝐎𝐍𝐂𝐋𝐔𝐒𝐈𝐎𝐍
====================

Overall, I think Silverleaf Ranger is one of the most fun Life cards to use right now.

The combination of:

*   Double Strike
    
*   Heal
    
*   Echo
    

makes this card extremely dangerous in longer battles.

Yes, the Weary ability can sometimes troll you but honestly that randomness also makes the card more exciting to use.

When everything works perfectly, Silverleaf Ranger feels like a machine gun that refuses to die.

I will definitely continue using this card more in ranked battles because it has huge carry potential.

Anyway thats it for today’s #splinterlands grind. More battles tomorrow and hopefully more crazy moments too. Please do give your reviews in the comments section below. I would really appreciate it :)

I'll be back with another one soon. So do follow me if you want to stay updated. Till then, Stay Happy and Stay Hydrated.
